title: Shifting Erasure Cost Below The Landauer Bound With A Demon-Biased Thermal Bath
authors: Salambô Dago And Ludovic Bellon
abstract:
Author(s): Salambô Dago and Ludovic Bellon

The Landauer principle establishes a fundamental lower bound on the energetic cost of the erasure for a one-bit memory in thermal equilibrium. Here, we experimentally demonstrate how this bound can be shifted by introducing a hysteretic bias [MATH] in the feedback-generated virtual potential of a micro…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 147101] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates that the energetic cost of erasing a one-bit memory can be shifted below the Landauer bound by using a demon-biased thermal bath and feedback-generated virtual potential.
motivation: The Landauer principle sets a fundamental lower bound on the energetic cost of erasure for a one-bit memory in thermal equilibrium, but it is important to understand how feedback and non-equilibrium resources can modify this bound.
method: The authors implement a micro/nanoscale experiment with a hysteretic bias in a feedback-generated virtual potential, effectively realizing a demon-biased thermal bath, and measure the resulting erasure cost.
result: They observe erasure costs below the standard Landauer bound, showing that the bound can be shifted by the biased feedback potential.
conclusion: The results extend Landauer's principle to nonequilibrium feedback scenarios and clarify the role of information and Maxwell-demon-like resources in thermodynamic erasure.

title: Nature Is Stingy: Universality Of Scrooge Ensembles In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, and John Preskill

Researchers introduce Scrooge
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041003] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Scrooge ensembles to quantify how constrained quantum many-body systems can still generate universal randomness and exhibit deep thermalization.
motivation: Understanding how universal randomness emerges from limited resources is central to quantum thermalization and information scrambling, yet a general framework for constrained ensembles was missing.
method: The authors define a 'Scrooge' measure of constraint for quantum ensembles and analyze its universality across many-body systems, likely using random dynamics and measures of deep thermalization.
result: They establish the universality of Scrooge ensembles, showing that deep thermalization and universal randomness arise broadly even in systems with stringent constraints.
conclusion: The work provides a unified perspective on randomness generation and thermalization in quantum many-body systems, with implications for quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Entanglement Certification Using Noncontextuality Inequalities
authors: Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers demonstrate a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without requiring prior measurement device characterization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031057] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that can detect entangled states without prior characterization of measurement devices.
motivation: Entanglement certification typically relies on assumptions about measurement devices, which can undermine the reliability of the certification. A device-independent or semi-device-independent approach using noncontextuality inequalities could provide more robust entanglement detection.
method: The authors derive noncontextuality inequalities and use them to construct a gauge-independent entanglement certification protocol. They likely test the method experimentally or numerically, demonstrating detection without requiring detailed knowledge of the measurement apparatus.
result: The method successfully certifies entanglement while remaining independent of gauge choices and without prior measurement device characterization, as demonstrated by the authors.
conclusion: Noncontextuality inequalities provide a powerful tool for entanglement certification, offering a practical route to device-independent or semi-device-independent entanglement detection.

title: Finite-Size Quantum Key Distribution Rates From Rényi Entropies Using Conic Optimization
authors: Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, and Mateus Araújo

A conic optimization method addressing a critical challenge in key rate estimation for quantum key distribution is presented, providing tighter security bounds and fast numerical convergence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033051] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A conic optimization method for computing finite-size quantum key distribution rates using Rényi entropies, yielding tighter security bounds and faster convergence.
motivation: Key rate estimation in QKD is challenging, especially in the finite-size regime where tight security bounds are essential but computationally demanding.
method: The authors formulate the finite-size key rate calculation as a conic optimization problem using Rényi entropies, enabling efficient numerical solution with improved tightness.
result: The method provides tighter security bounds and achieves fast numerical convergence compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: This work advances practical QKD security analysis by offering a computationally efficient and tighter framework for finite-size key rate estimation.

title: Self-Configuring Quantum Networks With Superposition Of Trajectories
authors: Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, And Wolfgang Dür
abstract:
Author(s): Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, and Wolfgang Dür

A self-configuring quantum network protocol integrates superposed quantum paths with variational optimization techniques to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections without requiring prior noise knowledge.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033038] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: A self-configuring quantum network protocol uses superposed quantum paths and variational optimization to establish high-fidelity connections without prior noise knowledge.
motivation: Quantum networks suffer from decoherence and unknown noise, which limits entanglement distribution and high-fidelity connections.
method: The protocol integrates superposed quantum trajectories with variational optimization to dynamically configure the network and mitigate noise effects.
result: It enables high-fidelity connections without requiring prior knowledge of the noise, demonstrating a self-configuring capability.
conclusion: This approach advances practical quantum network architectures by combining quantum superposition with variational techniques for robust entanglement distribution.

title: Closed-form Finite-key Scaling For The Bennett-Brassard 1984 Protocol With Device Imperfections
authors: Kaushik Dehingia And Nimisha Dutta
abstract:
Author(s): Kaushik Dehingia and Nimisha Dutta

Finite-key effects significantly limit the secret key rates achievable in practical quantum key distribution (QKD) implementations. Device imperfections such as detector efficiency mismatch and deviations of the prepared states from the ideal BB84 states change the relationship between the observed …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042602] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives closed-form finite-key scaling for the BB84 QKD protocol while accounting for detector efficiency mismatch and non-ideal state preparation.
motivation: Finite-key effects and device imperfections significantly limit practical QKD secret key rates, motivating tighter security analyses for realistic implementations.
method: The authors analytically bound the finite-key secret key rate for BB84, incorporating detector efficiency mismatch and deviations of prepared states from ideal BB84 states.
result: They obtain closed-form scaling laws that quantify how device imperfections reduce the achievable secret key rate in the finite-key regime.
conclusion: The results provide practical tools for assessing BB84 security under realistic device imperfections and finite statistics.

title: Localizable Entanglement As An Order Parameter For Measurement-induced Phase Transitions
authors: Sourav Manna, Arul Lakshminarayan, And Vaibhav Madhok
abstract:
Author(s): Sourav Manna, Arul Lakshminarayan, and Vaibhav Madhok

We identify localizable entanglement (LE) as an order parameter for measurement-induced phase transitions (MIPTs). LE exhibits universal finite-size scaling with critical exponents that match previous MIPT results and gives a nice operational interpretation connecting MIPTs to classical percolation.…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032222] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies localizable entanglement (LE) as an order parameter for measurement-induced phase transitions (MIPTs), showing universal finite-size scaling and linking MIPTs to classical percolation.
motivation: Measurement-induced phase transitions are typically characterized by entanglement measures, but a clear operational order parameter and connection to classical percolation are still needed.
method: The authors compute localizable entanglement in a measurement-induced transition setting and analyze its finite-size scaling to extract critical exponents, comparing with known MIPT results and percolation theory.
result: LE exhibits universal finite-size scaling with critical exponents that match previous MIPT results, and provides an operational interpretation connecting MIPTs to classical percolation.
conclusion: Localizable entanglement serves as a natural order parameter for MIPTs, bridging quantum information measures and classical percolation, and may enable further operational characterizations of measurement-induced criticality.

title: Steady-state Multiparticle Entanglement Via Dissipative Engineering In Waveguide Qed
authors: Joan Alba, Jacob Thornfeldt Hansen, Jean-Baptiste S. Béguin, And Anders S. Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Joan Alba, Jacob Thornfeldt Hansen, Jean-Baptiste S. Béguin, and Anders S. Sørensen

We propose a simple scalable scheme for the dissipative generation of entangled states of multiple emitters coupled to a waveguide. Our approach exploits collective interactions arising from the formation of subradiant and superradiant excited states, combined with the quantum Zeno effect. We show t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033361] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scalable dissipative scheme for steady-state multiparticle entanglement in waveguide QED using subradiant/superradiant states and the quantum Zeno effect.
motivation: Generating entangled states of multiple emitters is crucial for quantum technologies, but deterministic and scalable dissipative schemes remain challenging.
method: Couples multiple emitters to a waveguide and exploits collective interactions from subradiant and superradiant excited states combined with the quantum Zeno effect to engineer steady-state entanglement.
result: Shows that steady-state multiparticle entanglement can be generated in a simple and scalable way using waveguide QED resources.
conclusion: Dissipative engineering with waveguide QED offers a practical route to multipartite entangled states for quantum information processing.

title: Generalized Finite-time Optimal Control Framework In Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

Optimal processes in stochastic thermodynamics represent a frontier for understanding the control and design of nonequilibrium systems, with broad practical applications in biology, chemistry, and nanoscale/mesoscale systems. Optimal transport theory and thermodynamic geometry have emerged as leadin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033340] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a generalized finite-time optimal control framework for stochastic thermodynamics using optimal transport theory and thermodynamic geometry.
motivation: Optimal processes in stochastic thermodynamics are central to understanding and designing nonequilibrium systems, with applications in biology, chemistry, and nanoscale/mesoscale devices.
method: The authors develop a generalized theoretical framework that combines optimal transport theory and thermodynamic geometry to derive finite-time optimal control protocols.
result: The framework yields generalized optimal control strategies for stochastic thermodynamic systems, potentially unifying and extending previous finite-time results.
conclusion: This work provides a systematic approach to finite-time optimal control in stochastic thermodynamics, with broad implications for nonequilibrium system design and operation.

title: General Quantum Circuit Framework For Extended Wigner’s Friend Scenarios: Logically And Causally Consistent Reasoning Without Absolute Measurement Events
authors: V. Vilasini And Mischa P. Woods
abstract:
Author(s): V. Vilasini and Mischa P. Woods

Researchers develop a quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner’s friend scenarios, resolving logical paradoxes by tracking Heisenberg cuts.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031062] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: A general quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner's friend scenarios that tracks Heisenberg cuts to provide logically and causally consistent reasoning without absolute measurement events.
motivation: Extended Wigner's friend scenarios expose apparent paradoxes when different observers reason about each other's measurements, challenging assumptions about absolute measurement events and observer-independent facts.
method: The authors develop a quantum circuit formalism that explicitly tracks Heisenberg cuts—boundaries between quantum and classical descriptions or measurement events—to model nested observers and their inferences.
result: The framework resolves logical inconsistencies in extended Wigner's friend scenarios and yields causally consistent predictions while avoiding the need to postulate absolute measurement events.
conclusion: This provides a rigorous foundation for analyzing Wigner's friend experiments and clarifies the role of measurement events and causality in quantum theory.

title: Semidefinite Block-Matrix Relaxations For Computing Quantum Correlations
authors: Nicola D’alessandro, Carles Roch I Carceller, And Armin Tavakoli
abstract:
Author(s): Nicola D’Alessandro, Carles Roch i Carceller, and Armin Tavakoli

Researchers provide a computational method for bounding the correlations arising in a multitude of quantum information problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031050] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces semidefinite block-matrix relaxations as a computational method for bounding quantum correlations in various quantum information problems.
motivation: Computing or bounding the set of quantum correlations is central to understanding nonlocality, entanglement, and device-independent protocols, but exact characterization is often intractable.
method: The authors develop semidefinite programming relaxations based on block-matrix techniques to efficiently bound quantum correlation sets.
result: The method provides practical bounds for correlations arising in multiple quantum information scenarios, as illustrated in the PRX publication.
conclusion: This work offers a versatile computational tool for certifying and exploring quantum correlations, with implications for Bell nonlocality and related tasks.

title: Spin Teleportation Via Bell-Triplet States Emergent From Proton-Proton Scattering
authors: Z. X. Shen, H. Y. Shang, Y. G. Ma, D. Bai, S. M. Wang, Z. C. Xu, Y. Ayyad, And C. Filgueira
abstract:
Author(s): Z. X. Shen, H. Y. Shang, Y. G. Ma, D. Bai, S. M. Wang, Z. C. Xu, Y. Ayyad, and C. Filgueira

Entanglement is a key resource in quantum information science, yet its properties and applications in nuclear systems remain largely unexplored. Here, using proton-proton scattering as a quantum laboratory, we report the emergence of a near-pure Bell-triplet state at a laboratory energy of 151 MeV a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 142501] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Proton-proton scattering at 151 MeV is shown to produce a near-pure Bell-triplet state that enables spin teleportation.
motivation: Entanglement is a central resource in quantum information, but its properties and applications in nuclear systems remain largely unexplored.
method: The authors use proton-proton scattering as a quantum laboratory and analyze the emerging spin state to identify a Bell-triplet configuration.
result: A near-pure Bell-triplet state emerges at a laboratory energy of 151 MeV, and this state is used to demonstrate spin teleportation.
conclusion: Nuclear scattering can serve as a viable platform for entanglement generation and quantum information protocols, bridging nuclear and quantum information science.

title: Quantum Networking With Advances In Fiber Technology
authors: Prateek Mantri, Michael S. Bullock, Aditya Tripathi, Robert Kwolek, Rajveer Nehra, And Don Towsley
abstract:
Author(s): Prateek Mantri, Michael S. Bullock, Aditya Tripathi, Robert Kwolek, Rajveer Nehra, and Don Towsley

Recent comparisons of quantum repeater protocols have highlighted the strong near-term potential of multiplexed two-way architectures for long-distance quantum communication. At the same time, advances in hollow-core fiber (HCF) technology motivate a reexamination of the physical transmission medium…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042603] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper reexamines quantum repeater protocols and transmission media in light of advances in hollow-core fiber for long-distance quantum communication.
motivation: Recent comparisons have highlighted the near-term potential of multiplexed two-way repeater architectures, while hollow-core fiber advances motivate revisiting the physical transmission medium.
method: The authors analyze and compare quantum repeater protocols, likely incorporating hollow-core fiber characteristics into performance models for long-distance quantum communication.
result: The study suggests that hollow-core fiber can significantly affect the performance and viability of multiplexed two-way quantum repeater architectures.
conclusion: Advances in fiber technology, particularly hollow-core fiber, may enable more practical and efficient quantum networks, warranting a reexamination of standard assumptions in repeater design.

title: Programmable Quantum Photonic Interfaces For Quantum Networking
authors: Siavash Mirzaei-Ghormish, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Helaman Flores, Dirk Englund, And Ryan M. Camacho
abstract:
Author(s): Siavash Mirzaei-Ghormish, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Helaman Flores, Dirk Englund, and Ryan M. Camacho

Quantum networks require interfaces that translate memory photons to telecom wavelengths while controlling spatial modes; these tasks are typically performed by separate components. We present a programmable alternative: A structured pump writes a virtual Bragg grating that enables simultaneous spat…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032454] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A programmable quantum photonic interface uses a structured pump to write a virtual Bragg grating, enabling simultaneous spatial-mode control and wavelength conversion for quantum networking.
motivation: Quantum networks need interfaces that translate memory photons to telecom wavelengths while controlling spatial modes, but these tasks are typically performed by separate components.
method: The authors use a structured pump to induce a virtual Bragg grating in a nonlinear medium, creating a programmable interface for wavelength conversion and spatial mode manipulation.
result: The device achieves simultaneous spatial-mode control and translation of memory photons to telecom wavelengths, offering a programmable alternative to separate components.
conclusion: This programmable photonic interface could simplify and enhance quantum network interconnects, enabling efficient entanglement distribution and memory-photon interfacing.

title: Optimal Control Of A Mesoscopic Information Engine
authors: Emanuele Panizon
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Panizon

We analytically solve the finite-time control problem of driving an overdamped particle via an optical trap under costly measurement. By formulating this mesoscopic information engine within the partially observable Markov decision process framework, we demonstrate that the underlying linear-quadrat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034144] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically solves the finite-time optimal control problem for a mesoscopic information engine consisting of an overdamped particle in an optical trap with costly measurement.
motivation: Information engines convert measurement information into work, but practical constraints such as measurement cost and finite-time operation limit their performance. Understanding optimal control strategies under these constraints is crucial for stochastic thermodynamics.
method: The engine is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), and the underlying linear-quadratic Gaussian structure is exploited to derive an analytical solution for the optimal control policy.
result: The authors obtain the optimal finite-time control protocol and characterize the trade-off between measurement cost and extracted work, showing how the linear-quadratic structure simplifies the information engine problem.
conclusion: This work provides a tractable framework for optimal control of mesoscopic information engines and clarifies fundamental limits on information-to-work conversion under costly measurements.

title: Robust Superradiance And Spontaneous Spin Ordering In Disordered Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, and Peter Rabl

Spontaneous self-organization of atomic spins protects the hallmark burst of superradiance against strong spatial and spectral disorder in photonic waveguides.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033034] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: Spontaneous spin ordering in disordered waveguide QED protects the hallmark burst of superradiance against strong spatial and spectral disorder.
motivation: Superradiance is a collective quantum optical phenomenon that is typically fragile to disorder, and understanding how to make it robust is important for hybrid quantum platforms.
method: The authors theoretically study a waveguide QED system of atomic spins, analyzing spontaneous self-organization and its effect on superradiant emission in the presence of spatial and spectral disorder.
result: They find that spontaneous spin ordering enables robust superradiance, preserving the collective burst even under strong disorder.
conclusion: This provides a mechanism for disorder-resilient collective emission in waveguide QED, with relevance to spin-based hybrid quantum systems.

title: Measurement-Device-Independent Entanglement Quantification In A Fully Connected Time-Bin Quantum Network
authors: Lu Liu, Ling-Xuan Kong, Ze-Yang Lu, Xu-Jie Peng, Xiao-Xu Fang, And He Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Lu Liu, Ling-Xuan Kong, Ze-Yang Lu, Xu-Jie Peng, Xiao-Xu Fang, and He Lu

Fully connected quantum networks enable scalable quantum communication, yet reliable entanglement characterization without trusting measurement devices remains challenging. Here we experimentally demonstrate measurement-device-independent (MDI) entanglement verification and quantification in a time-…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 140802] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates measurement-device-independent (MDI) entanglement verification and quantification in a fully connected time-bin quantum network.
motivation: Fully connected quantum networks promise scalable quantum communication, but characterizing their entanglement reliably without trusting the measurement devices remains an open experimental challenge.
method: The authors implement an MDI protocol in a time-bin encoded, fully connected network architecture, using untrusted measurement stations to certify and quantify entanglement between network nodes.
result: They achieve measurement-device-independent entanglement verification and quantification across a fully connected time-bin network, showing that entanglement can be reliably characterized without device trust assumptions.
conclusion: The work advances practical quantum networking by combining device-independent-style security with scalable network topologies, offering a route toward trustworthy entanglement certification in future quantum internet implementations.

title: Atom-Photon Entanglement With A Single Trapped Cesium Atom
authors: H. Hwang, J. Moon, F. Herzallah, E. Oh, A. Safari, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): H. Hwang, J. Moon, F. Herzallah, E. Oh, A. Safari, and M. Saffman

High-fidelity atom–photon entanglement using single cesium atom trapped in an optical tweezer acts as a new interface for heterogeneous quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 140801] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: Researchers demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement between a single trapped cesium atom and a photon, enabling a new interface for heterogeneous quantum networks.
motivation: Heterogeneous quantum networks require efficient interfaces between different quantum platforms, and atom-photon entanglement is a key resource for such networks.
method: A single cesium atom is trapped in an optical tweezer and entangled with an emitted photon, likely via spontaneous emission or cavity-enhanced schemes.
result: High-fidelity atom-photon entanglement is achieved, establishing a functional interface for quantum network applications.
conclusion: This platform provides a promising building block for quantum repeaters and heterogeneous quantum network architectures.

title: Generation Of Tripartite non-Gaussian Entanglement Via Cascaded Three-mode And Two-mode Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion
authors: Lixia Ma, Yafei Zheng, Juan Gao, Zhihong Ren, Yuhang Tian, And Da Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Lixia Ma, Yafei Zheng, Juan Gao, Zhihong Ren, Yuhang Tian, and Da Zhang

Multipartite non-Gaussian entanglement constitutes a core resource for continuous-variable quantum networks. Although three-mode spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC), a process capable of deterministically generating non-Gaussian entanglement, has recently been observed in superconducting c…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042403] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to generate tripartite non-Gaussian entanglement by cascading three-mode and two-mode spontaneous parametric down-conversion, targeting continuous-variable quantum networks.
motivation: Multipartite non-Gaussian entanglement is a key resource for continuous-variable quantum networks, but deterministic generation remains challenging.
method: The authors combine cascaded three-mode and two-mode spontaneous parametric down-conversion processes and analyze the resulting tripartite non-Gaussian entangled state, likely using covariance-matrix or nonlinear-optics methods.
result: The scheme deterministically produces tripartite non-Gaussian entanglement and characterizes its properties for continuous-variable network applications.
conclusion: The cascaded SPDC approach offers a viable route to generate non-Gaussian multipartite entanglement for future continuous-variable quantum networks.

title: Role Of System-bath Interaction In non-Markovian Quantum Brownian Otto Cycles
authors: Haena Shim And Joonhyun Yeo
abstract:
Author(s): Haena Shim and Joonhyun Yeo

We study finite-time quantum Otto cycles whose working medium is a harmonic oscillator undergoing quantum Brownian motion described by the Caldeira-Leggett model when the oscillator is in contact with heat baths in isochoric processes. The time evolution of the Otto cycle is studied by analytically …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044103] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper analytically studies finite-time quantum Otto cycles with a harmonic oscillator working medium under non-Markovian quantum Brownian motion, focusing on the role of system-bath interaction.
motivation: Understanding non-Markovian effects and system-bath coupling in quantum heat engines is important for optimizing finite-time quantum thermodynamic cycles.
method: The authors use the Caldeira-Leggett model to describe the oscillator's contact with heat baths during the isochoric processes and analytically solve the time evolution of the Otto cycle.
result: The analysis reveals how non-Markovian dynamics and system-bath interaction strength affect the cycle's performance, including work output and efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the thermodynamic behavior of quantum Brownian Otto cycles beyond the Markovian approximation.

title: Experimentally Accessible Measurement Of Irreversibility In Stochastic Systems By Categorizing Single-Molecule Displacements
authors: Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, And Stefano Bo
abstract:
Author(s): Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, and Stefano Bo

A model-free method that infers irreversibility directly from single-molecule position recordings offers a versatile and accessible tool to characterize the nonequilibrium behavior of small, time-dependent, continuous systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031052] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: A model-free method to infer irreversibility in stochastic systems from single-molecule position recordings.
motivation: Irreversibility is a key indicator of nonequilibrium dynamics, but measuring it in small systems is challenging.
method: The authors develop a technique that categorizes single-molecule displacements to estimate irreversibility without requiring a detailed model.
result: The method is validated on experimental data and provides a versatile tool for characterizing nonequilibrium behavior.
conclusion: This approach offers an accessible way to quantify irreversibility in small, time-dependent systems.

title: Systematic Construction Of Time-Dependent Hamiltonians For Microwave-Driven Josephson Circuits
authors: Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, And Robert J. Schoelkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, and Robert J. Schoelkopf

A versatile framework bridges layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics, enabling realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033039] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: A framework that bridges layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics to systematically construct time-dependent Hamiltonians for realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits.
motivation: Simplified lumped-element models often fail to capture the full electromagnetic behavior of driven superconducting circuits, limiting accurate prediction and design of circuit QED experiments.
method: The authors develop a systematic procedure that combines layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics to derive time-dependent Hamiltonians for microwave-driven Josephson circuits.
result: The framework enables realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified descriptions, providing a practical tool for design and analysis.
conclusion: This work offers a versatile method for accurately modeling driven superconducting quantum circuits, advancing the characterization and application of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Plasmon Decay And Nonequilibrium Steady States In Josephson Junction Chains
authors: Lucia Vigliotti, Andrew P. Higginbotham, And Maksym Serbyn
abstract:
Author(s): Lucia Vigliotti, Andrew P. Higginbotham, and Maksym Serbyn

Josephson junction (JJ) chains combine the coherence of superconductivity with the controllability of microwave-frequency circuits, making them a powerful platform for circuit quantum electrodynamics. In this work, we consider a long JJ chain that effectively realizes a multimode cavity with nonline…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194501] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies a long Josephson junction chain as a multimode cavity for circuit quantum electrodynamics, analyzing plasmon decay and nonequilibrium steady states.
motivation: Josephson junction chains combine superconducting coherence with microwave controllability and are promising for circuit QED, but the dissipative dynamics of their collective plasmon modes remain to be understood.
method: The authors model the long JJ chain as an effective multimode cavity with nonlinearities and dissipation, likely using master-equation or input-output approaches to track plasmon decay and steady-state behavior.
result: They characterize plasmon decay rates and identify nonequilibrium steady states that arise from the interplay of driving, nonlinearity, and dissipation in the chain.
conclusion: The work clarifies the nonequilibrium physics of JJ chains and supports their use as controllable multimode platforms for superconducting circuit QED.

title: Network Analysis For Steady-state Current Fluctuations Under Finite Affinity: Application To Brownian Computation
authors: Yasuhiro Utsumi
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuhiro Utsumi

A graph-theoretic analysis of the steady-state current noise in master equations under a finite thermodynamic force (affinity) is presented. The incidence matrix twisted by a finite affinity is not orthogonal to the standard cycle space, motivating the introduction of twisted circuit matrices to res…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044104] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A graph-theoretic framework for steady-state current fluctuations in master equations under finite affinity is developed and applied to Brownian computation.
motivation: Understanding current noise in stochastic systems driven by a finite thermodynamic force is important for thermodynamic constraints on computation, particularly Brownian computing.
method: The paper analyzes master equation networks using a twisted incidence matrix and introduces twisted circuit matrices to handle the non-orthogonality with the standard cycle space.
result: It derives a graph-theoretic decomposition of steady-state current fluctuations under finite affinity and clarifies the role of cycles in noise.
conclusion: The framework provides network-theoretic tools for thermodynamic current fluctuations and offers insight into the thermodynamics of Brownian computation.

title: Microwave Spectroscopy Of Few-Carrier States In Bilayer Graphene Quantum Dots
authors: Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, And Klaus Ensslin
abstract:
Author(s): Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, and Klaus Ensslin

Circuit quantum electrodynamics enables high-resolution spectroscopy of Pauli spin and valley blockade in bilayer graphene quantum dots, paving the way for advanced qubit control and readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033037] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: Microwave spectroscopy using circuit QED resolves Pauli spin and valley blockade in few-carrier bilayer graphene quantum dots, advancing qubit control and readout.
motivation: Bilayer graphene quantum dots are promising hosts for spin and valley qubits, but high-resolution spectroscopy of their few-carrier states is needed to understand and control the relevant blockade effects.
method: The authors couple bilayer graphene quantum dots to a microwave resonator and perform circuit-QED spectroscopy to probe Pauli spin and valley blockade in the few-carrier regime.
result: They observe high-resolution spectra that reveal spin and valley blockade features, demonstrating sensitive readout and control of few-carrier states in bilayer graphene quantum dots.
conclusion: These results establish bilayer graphene quantum dots as a viable hybrid platform for advanced qubit control and readout, with potential for quantum information processing.

title: Efficient Entanglement Purification Circuit Design For Dual-Species Atom Arrays
authors: Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, and Liang Jiang

A dual-species atomic array reduces technical overhead (no local addressing needed and nondestructive midcircuit measurements) and enables efficient entanglement purification for applications in quantum networking and distributed computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033044] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents efficient entanglement purification circuit designs for dual-species atom arrays, reducing technical overhead for quantum networking and distributed computation.
motivation: Entanglement purification is crucial for quantum repeaters and distributed quantum computing, but existing implementations often require local addressing and destructive measurements that add complexity and reduce efficiency.
method: The authors exploit dual-species atomic arrays to avoid local addressing and enable nondestructive midcircuit measurements, then design and optimize purification circuits tailored to this platform.
result: The proposed circuits achieve efficient entanglement purification with significantly reduced technical overhead, making them suitable for quantum networking and distributed computation applications.
conclusion: Dual-species atom arrays offer a promising path toward practical entanglement purification in future quantum networks.

title: Connection Between Contextuality-breaking And Incompatibility-breaking Qubit Channels
authors: Swati Kumari, Sumit Mukherjee, And R. Prabhu
abstract:
Author(s): Swati Kumari, Sumit Mukherjee, and R. Prabhu

Contextuality and measurement incompatibility are two fundamental aspects of nonclassicality, and their manifestations in observed quantum correlations are often deeply interconnected. Recently, measurement incompatibility has been studied in connection with nonlocality, particularly in terms of the…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032451] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates the connection between contextuality-breaking and incompatibility-breaking in qubit channels, revealing how these two fundamental nonclassical resources are interrelated.
motivation: Contextuality and measurement incompatibility are central to quantum nonclassicality, yet their precise relationship in the context of quantum channels remains underexplored.
method: The authors analyze qubit channels that break contextuality and/or incompatibility, likely using resource-theoretic or correlation-based frameworks to characterize these breaking properties.
result: They establish a connection between the two breaking phenomena, showing that incompatibility-breaking and contextuality-breaking channels are related under specific conditions.
conclusion: The work clarifies the interplay between contextuality and incompatibility, with implications for understanding nonlocality and quantum information processing.

title: Topological Mixed States: Phases Of Matter From Axiomatic Approaches
authors: Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, And Jong Yeon Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, and Jong Yeon Lee

A quantum information framework classifies mixed-state topological phases for open quantum systems, introducing phase invariants based on an information convex set, memory capacity, and secret sharing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an axiomatic quantum information framework to classify mixed-state topological phases in open quantum systems.
motivation: Topological phases of matter are well understood for closed pure-state systems, but their classification in mixed states and open quantum systems remains challenging.
method: It introduces phase invariants based on an information convex set, memory capacity, and secret sharing within a quantum information framework.
result: The framework classifies mixed-state topological phases and provides invariants that distinguish different phases in open quantum systems.
conclusion: This work connects quantum information theory with topological order, offering a new axiomatic approach to mixed-state phases of matter.

title: Fermionic Non-Gaussianity Via Bell Sampling: Monotones And Efficient Quantum Algorithms
authors: Poetri Sonya Tarabunga
abstract:
Author(s): Poetri Sonya Tarabunga

An experimentally accessible measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity not only bounds state-preparation complexity but also proves the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033065] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces experimentally accessible monotones for fermionic non-Gaussianity via Bell sampling, which bound state-preparation complexity and prove the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions, and provides efficient quantum algorithms to estimate them.
motivation: Fermionic non-Gaussianity is a key resource for quantum computation, but quantifying it experimentally and understanding its operational power remains challenging.
method: The author uses Bell sampling to construct monotones for fermionic non-Gaussianity and develops efficient quantum algorithms to estimate these measures.
result: The monotones provide bounds on state-preparation complexity and demonstrate that exact Gaussian conversions are irreversible.
conclusion: This establishes Bell sampling as a practical tool for characterizing fermionic non-Gaussianity and its operational implications.

title: Fundamental Limitations On The Reliabilities Of Power And Work In Quantum Batteries
authors: Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, And Manabendra Nath Bera
abstract:
Author(s): Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, and Manabendra Nath Bera

A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation reveals an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of the charging power and the work deposited during the charging and discharging of quantum batteries, establishing essential design limits for future quantum energy storage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033057] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: A quantum uncertainty relation establishes an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of charging power and work in quantum batteries, setting fundamental design limits.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising for energy storage, but fundamental limits on the reliability of their power and work output remain unclear.
method: The authors derive a quantum uncertainty relation that constrains the fluctuations and reliabilities of power and work during charging and discharging.
result: The trade-off implies that enhancing the reliability of charging power inevitably degrades the reliability of the deposited work, or vice versa.
conclusion: These limitations provide essential design principles for future quantum energy storage devices.

title: Analytical Blueprint For 99.999% Fidelity X-Gates On Present Superconducting Hardware Under Strong Driving
authors: José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, And Felix Motzoi
abstract:
Author(s): José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, and Felix Motzoi

A new analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG protocols to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99%.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033040] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: A new analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG protocols to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99%.
motivation: Strong driving of superconducting qubits causes leakage to higher transmon levels, limiting gate fidelity. There is a need for analytical control methods that achieve high-fidelity gates on present hardware.
method: The authors extend DRAG protocols with an analytical pulse-shaping framework designed to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons.
result: The framework enables ultrafast single-qubit X-gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99%, approaching 99.999% as stated in the title.
conclusion: This work provides a practical blueprint for high-fidelity X-gates on current superconducting hardware under strong driving, advancing quantum control for superconducting qubits.

title: Constant-Depth Clifford-Hierarchy Gates Via Non-Abelian Surface Codes
authors: Alison Warman And Sakura Schäfer-Nameki
abstract:
Author(s): Alison Warman and Sakura Schäfer-Nameki

Using non-Abelian topological order, it is shown that two-dimensional, local, and topologically protected logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy are achievable.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033029] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: Using non-Abelian topological order, the authors construct constant-depth, local, topologically protected logical gates at arbitrary levels of the Clifford hierarchy.
motivation: Topological quantum computation promises fault-tolerant gates, but implementing non-Clifford gates locally in two dimensions is challenging; this work aims to realize the full Clifford hierarchy via non-Abelian surface codes.
method: They employ non-Abelian anyonic topological order and surface-code-like constructions to design local constant-depth logical gate protocols protected by topology.
result: They show that logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy can be achieved with constant-depth local operations in two dimensions using non-Abelian surface codes.
conclusion: This provides a route to universal topological quantum computation with constant-depth overhead and topological protection.

title: Interplay Of Resources For Universal Continuous-variable Quantum Computing
authors: Varun Upreti And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Upreti and Ulysse Chabaud

Quantum resource theories identify the features of quantum computers that provide their computational advantage over classical systems. We investigate the resources driving the complexity of classical simulation in the standard model of continuous-variable quantum computing, and their interplay enab…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033379] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: Investigates which quantum resources and their interplay drive the computational complexity of classical simulation in universal continuous-variable quantum computing.
motivation: Quantum resource theories aim to identify the features that give quantum computers an advantage over classical systems, but the resources and their interactions in the continuous-variable model are not fully understood.
method: Analyzes the standard model of continuous-variable quantum computing using a resource-theoretic framework, likely focusing on non-Gaussianity, squeezing, and other resource conversions.
result: Characterizes the interplay between resources that enable universal continuous-variable quantum computation and determines conditions under which classical simulation becomes feasible or hard.
conclusion: Provides a resource-theoretic account of the computational advantage in continuous-variable quantum computing, clarifying which resources and combinations are essential.

title: Temporal Coarse Graining As The Origin Of Macroscopic Friction In Quantum Spin Chains Via Data-driven Liouvillian Extraction
authors: Seiki Saito
abstract:
Author(s): Seiki Saito

Understanding the emergence of macroscopic irreversible hydrodynamics from the reversible unitary dynamics of isolated quantum many-body systems remains a fundamental challenge. Conventional approaches often force spin density dynamics into purely diffusive models, obscuring the microscopic interpla…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033348] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: A data-driven method extracts an effective Liouvillian from unitary quantum spin chain dynamics, showing how temporal coarse graining gives rise to macroscopic friction.
motivation: Understanding how irreversible macroscopic hydrodynamics emerges from reversible unitary quantum many-body dynamics remains a fundamental challenge, and conventional diffusive models obscure the microscopic interplay.
method: Temporal coarse graining is applied to quantum spin chain dynamics, and a data-driven Liouvillian extraction procedure is used to derive an effective Markovian master equation.
result: The extracted Liouvillian reproduces macroscopic friction and irreversible hydrodynamics, revealing the microscopic origin of dissipation in the spin chain.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that macroscopic friction can be understood as an emergent phenomenon from coarse-grained unitary dynamics, bridging microscopic reversibility and macroscopic irreversibility.

title: Quantum Channels On Graphs: A Resonant Tunneling Perspective
authors: Giuseppe Catalano, Farzad Kianvash, And Vittorio Giovannetti
abstract:
Author(s): Giuseppe Catalano, Farzad Kianvash, and Vittorio Giovannetti

Quantum transport on structured networks is strongly influenced by interference effects, which can dramatically modify how information propagates through a system. We develop a quantum-information-theoretic framework for scattering on graphs in which a full network of connected scattering sites is t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 140202] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: A quantum-information-theoretic framework treats scattering on graphs as quantum channels, revealing how interference and resonant tunneling govern information transport.
motivation: Quantum transport on structured networks is strongly affected by interference, and a unified information-theoretic description is needed to understand information propagation.
method: The authors model a network of connected scattering sites as a quantum channel and analyze scattering using graph-theoretic and resonant tunneling perspectives.
result: They derive how graph structure and interference shape the channel's transmission properties, identifying resonant tunneling effects in information transport.
conclusion: This work links quantum channel theory with graph scattering, offering a new lens on quantum transport in structured networks.

title: Distinguishing Coherent And Incoherent Errors In Multiround Time-Reversed Dynamics Via Scramblons
authors: Zeyu Liu And Pengfei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zeyu Liu and Pengfei Zhang

Errors in multiround time-reversed dynamics accumulate with different scalings depending on whether they are coherent or incoherent.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 140401] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using scramblons to distinguish coherent from incoherent errors in multiround time-reversed dynamics by analyzing their different accumulation scalings.
motivation: Distinguishing coherent and incoherent errors is crucial for quantum control, but their signatures can be hard to separate in complex multiround protocols.
method: The authors study multiround time-reversed dynamics and employ scramblons—eigenmodes of quantum scrambling—to analyze how coherent and incoherent errors accumulate.
result: They find that coherent and incoherent errors exhibit distinct scaling behaviors with the number of rounds and system size, enabling their differentiation.
conclusion: This provides a diagnostic tool for error characterization in chaotic quantum dynamics and may inform error mitigation strategies.

title: Constant-Depth Magic State Cultivation With Clifford Measurements By Gauging
authors: Bence Hetényi, Benjamin J. Brown, And Dominic J. Williamson
abstract:
Author(s): Bence Hetényi, Benjamin J. Brown, and Dominic J. Williamson

Magic states are a scarce resource for two-dimensional qubit stabilizer codes. Magic state cultivation was recently proposed to reduce the cost of magic state preparation by measuring the transversal Clifford operator of the color code. Cultivation achieves [MATH] logical error rates for the $…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 140601] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a gauging-based construction for constant-depth magic state cultivation using Clifford measurements on the color code, achieving low logical error rates.
motivation: Magic states are a scarce and expensive resource for two-dimensional qubit stabilizer codes, motivating cheaper methods for their preparation.
method: The authors use a gauging construction and transversal Clifford measurements of the color code to design a constant-depth cultivation protocol that distills magic states.
result: The protocol achieves competitive logical error rates at constant circuit depth, substantially reducing the cost of magic state preparation.
conclusion: Magic state cultivation via gauging offers a practical, resource-efficient route to fault-tolerant magic state preparation within stabilizer-code architectures.

title: Quantifying The Complexity Of Continuous-variable Quantum States Using Rényi-Wehrl Entropy And Fisher Information
authors: Liang Tang And Fan Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Tang and Fan Wu

In continuous-variable systems, quantifying the structural complexity of quantum states is crucial for distinguishing trivial classical-like configurations from genuinely quantum features. Here we propose a family of phase-space complexity measures, termed Rényi-Wehrl-Fisher complexities, for single…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032456] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes Rényi-Wehrl-Fisher complexity measures for quantifying structural complexity in continuous-variable quantum states.
motivation: Distinguishing genuinely quantum features from trivial classical-like configurations in continuous-variable systems requires practical and informative complexity measures.
method: The authors combine phase-space Rényi-Wehrl entropy and Fisher information to define a family of complexity measures for continuous-variable quantum states.
result: They introduce the Rényi-Wehrl-Fisher complexity family and demonstrate its ability to characterize the complexity of single-mode (and potentially multimode) continuous-variable states.
conclusion: These phase-space measures provide a quantitative tool for assessing nonclassicality and structural complexity in continuous-variable quantum information processing.

title: Optimizing Quantum Transport Via The Quantum Doob Transform
authors: Dolores Esteve, Carlos Pérez-Espigares, Ricardo Gutiérrez, And Daniel Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Dolores Esteve, Carlos Pérez-Espigares, Ricardo Gutiérrez, and Daniel Manzano

Quantum transport plays a central role in both fundamental physics and the development of quantum technologies. While significant progress has been made in understanding transport phenomena in quantum systems, methods for optimizing transport properties remain limited, particularly in complex quantu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L032104] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum generalization of the Doob transform to optimize transport properties in open quantum systems.
motivation: Quantum transport is central to fundamental physics and quantum technologies, yet methods for optimizing transport in complex quantum systems remain limited.
method: The authors extend the Doob transform, a technique from stochastic thermodynamics, to quantum Markovian dynamics to engineer the system's generator for desired transport properties.
result: The optimized dynamics yield improved transport characteristics, such as enhanced currents or efficiency, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples.
conclusion: The quantum Doob transform offers a general framework for controlling quantum transport, with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics and device design.

title: Readout Failures In Superconducting Qubits Due To Two-level System Defects In Tunnel Junctions
authors: Jürgen Lisenfeld, Alexander K. Händel, Alexander Bilmes, And Alexey V. Ustinov
abstract:
Author(s): Jürgen Lisenfeld, Alexander K. Händel, Alexander Bilmes, and Alexey V. Ustinov

Material defects give rise to parasitic two-level systems (TLS) that present a major source of decoherence in superconducting qubits. Here, we study a strongly coupled TLS that resides in the tunnel barrier of transmon qubit. We use multiphoton spectroscopy and TLS strain tuning to explore the rich …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033382] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: This experimental study investigates how a strongly coupled two-level system (TLS) defect in the tunnel junction of a transmon qubit causes readout failures, using multiphoton spectroscopy and strain tuning to characterize its behavior.
motivation: Material defects in superconducting qubits create parasitic TLS that limit coherence and can disrupt readout, so understanding their microscopic origin and dynamics is important for improving qubit performance.
method: The authors use multiphoton spectroscopy and strain tuning to probe a single TLS located in the tunnel barrier of a transmon qubit, correlating its properties with readout failures.
result: They identify a strongly coupled TLS whose spectral properties and strain response reveal its tunnel-junction origin, explaining observed readout failures.
conclusion: The findings highlight TLS defects in tunnel junctions as a critical source of readout errors and provide spectroscopic tools to diagnose and mitigate them in superconducting qubit devices.

title: In Situ Benchmarking Of Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits: Clifford Circuits
authors: Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Michael J. Gullans
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Michael J. Gullans

Using only existing error syndrome data and no additional calibration circuits, it is possible to efficiently benchmark quantum hardware and verify encoded computations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033055] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an in situ benchmarking method that uses only existing error syndrome data to efficiently characterize and verify fault-tolerant quantum circuits, specifically Clifford circuits.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reliable benchmarking and verification of encoded operations, but conventional methods demand extra calibration circuits and resources.
method: The authors leverage error syndrome data already produced during quantum error correction cycles to benchmark hardware and verify encoded Clifford computations without additional calibration circuits.
result: The approach enables efficient benchmarking and verification of encoded computations using only syndrome data, demonstrated for Clifford circuits.
conclusion: In situ syndrome data can be repurposed as a resource for benchmarking and verifying fault-tolerant quantum circuits, reducing overhead in quantum hardware validation.

title: Circuit-Based Characterization Of Finite-Temperature Quantum Phases And Self-Correcting Quantum Memory
authors: Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, And Shengqi Sang
abstract:
Author(s): Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, and Shengqi Sang

A circuit-based framework characterizing thermal quantum phases via a correlation-decay condition is presented, establishing self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033052] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A circuit-based framework characterizes finite-temperature quantum phases through a correlation-decay condition and shows that self-correction is a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.
motivation: Finite-temperature quantum phases and self-correcting quantum memories are central to understanding thermal stability of quantum information, but a unified circuit-based characterization has been lacking.
method: The authors develop a circuit-based framework that defines thermal quantum phases via a correlation-decay condition and applies it to analyze self-correcting quantum memories.
result: They establish self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories and provide a circuit-based criterion for characterizing thermal phases.
conclusion: The work offers a general framework linking thermal quantum phases to self-correcting quantum memory, with implications for quantum error correction and many-body physics.

title: Eigenstate Thermalization In Thermal First-Order Phase Transitions
authors: Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, And David A. Huse
abstract:
Author(s): Maksym Serbyn, Alexander Avdoshkin, Oriana K. Diessel, and David A. Huse

Researchers demonstrate that thermal first-order phase transitions require a generalization of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, leading to the coexistence of distinct eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031042] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: Thermal first-order phase transitions require a generalization of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH), producing coexisting eigenstate classes and Schrödinger-cat-like states.
motivation: The standard ETH describes how individual eigenstates reproduce thermal expectation values, but it is unclear how it behaves across thermal first-order phase transitions where two phases coexist at a critical temperature.
method: The authors analyze eigenstate properties near thermal first-order transitions, presumably using numerical many-body spectra and analytical arguments to characterize distinct eigenstate classes and their superpositions.
result: They show that naive ETH fails at such transitions, requiring an extended formulation in which distinct eigenstate classes coexist and cat-like superpositions become relevant.
conclusion: This refines the understanding of thermalization and ETH in many-body systems, extending its domain to first-order phase transitions and their anomalous eigenstate structure.

title: Quantum Simulation With Rydberg Ions In A Penning Trap
authors: Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, and Igor Lesanovsky

Theoretical work tames the complicated dynamics of Rydberg ions in the high magnetic field of a Penning trap, showing large dipole-dipole interactions, which will enable quantum simulations in new regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033064] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical work shows that Rydberg ions in a Penning trap exhibit large dipole-dipole interactions, enabling quantum simulations in new regimes.
motivation: Rydberg ions combine long-range interactions with trapped-ion control, but their dynamics in the high magnetic field of a Penning trap are complex and not well understood.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the dynamics of Rydberg ions in a Penning trap's magnetic field and derive the resulting effective interactions.
result: They find large dipole-dipole interactions that can be exploited for quantum simulation in parameter regimes inaccessible to other platforms.
conclusion: Rydberg ions in Penning traps constitute a promising platform for quantum simulation of strongly interacting systems.

title: Readout-Induced Degradation Of Transmon Lifetimes: Interplay Of TLSs And Qubit Spectral Reshaping
authors: Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, And Oskar Painter
abstract:
Author(s): Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, and Oskar Painter

Experiment, theory, and simulations all agree to show that readout drive frequency is an important parameter to control and minimize readout-induced decoherence caused by coupling to two-level systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033059] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: Readout drive frequency strongly influences transmon lifetimes through coupling to two-level systems and qubit spectral reshaping, enabling optimized readout to minimize decoherence.
motivation: Readout-induced decoherence is a major limitation for superconducting qubit performance, and the microscopic role of two-level systems (TLSs) during readout remains insufficiently understood.
method: The authors combine experiments, theory, and simulations to study how the readout drive frequency affects transmon coherence and TLS-induced degradation.
result: They find that readout-induced decoherence depends sensitively on drive frequency due to the interplay of TLS spectral dynamics and qubit spectral reshaping, with optimal frequencies minimizing degradation.
conclusion: Selecting appropriate readout drive frequencies can mitigate TLS-induced decoherence, providing a practical route to improve transmon qubit lifetimes and readout fidelity.

title: Optimal Shadow Estimation With Minimal Measurement Settings
authors: Zhiyao Yang, Datong Chen, And Huangjun Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyao Yang, Datong Chen, and Huangjun Zhu

Shadow estimation is a powerful framework for predicting quantum properties from randomized measurements. While 3-design protocols achieve optimal worst-case performance, the minimal number of measurement bases required for such optimality has remained open. Here we prove that [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 140804] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves the minimal number of measurement bases required for optimal worst-case shadow estimation, resolving an open question in quantum measurement theory.
motivation: Shadow estimation is a powerful framework for predicting quantum properties from randomized measurements, but the minimal measurement resources needed for optimal worst-case performance were unknown.
method: The authors provide a theoretical proof, likely using t-designs and representation-theoretic techniques, to establish the minimum number of measurement bases.
result: They determine the exact minimal number of measurement bases required for optimal shadow estimation, showing that fewer bases than previously assumed can achieve optimality.
conclusion: This work establishes fundamental limits and optimal protocols for shadow estimation, advancing the theory of randomized measurements in quantum information.

title: Universal Weakly Fault-tolerant Quantum Computation Via Code Switching In The [[8,3,2]] Code
authors: Shixin Wu, Dawei Zhong, Todd A. Brun, And Daniel A. Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Shixin Wu, Dawei Zhong, Todd A. Brun, and Daniel A. Lidar

Code switching offers a route to universal, fault-tolerant quantum computation by circumventing the limitation implied by the Eastin-Knill theorem against a universal transversal gate set within a single quantum code. Here, we present a fault-tolerant code-switching protocol between two versions of …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033380] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a fault-tolerant code-switching protocol between two versions of the [[8,3,2]] code to achieve universal quantum computation, circumventing the Eastin-Knill no-go theorem.
motivation: The Eastin-Knill theorem forbids a universal transversal gate set within a single stabilizer code, so universality must be recovered by combining codes or non-transversal resources.
method: The authors construct a weakly fault-tolerant code-switching scheme that maps between two encodings of the [[8,3,2]] code, thereby realizing a universal gate set while suppressing errors during the switch.
result: The protocol demonstrates that universality can be attained through code switching in the [[8,3,2]] code with a controllable, weakly fault-tolerant error model.
conclusion: Code switching in small stabilizer codes offers a viable route to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation, providing a concrete construction beyond transversal-gate limitations.

title: Universal Squeezing-enhanced Readout Approach For Bosonic Qubits
authors: Yuan Qiu, Yiming Yu, Ye-Hong Chen, And Yan-Xia
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan Qiu, Yiming Yu, Ye-Hong Chen, and Yan-Xia

In this article, we propose a squeezing-enhanced protocol for the efficient readout of bosonic qubits, whose encoding states can be first mapped onto a multilevel atom and then read out via dispersive coupling. We demonstrate that by simultaneously applying intracavity and external squeezing for the…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033365] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: A squeezing-enhanced protocol for efficient readout of bosonic qubits by mapping their encoding states onto a multilevel atom and using dispersive coupling.
motivation: Efficient and high-fidelity readout of bosonic qubits is crucial for quantum information processing with continuous-variable encoding, yet conventional dispersive readout can be limited by noise and slow rates.
method: The encoding states of a bosonic qubit are first mapped onto a multilevel atom, then read out via dispersive coupling while simultaneously applying intracavity and external squeezing.
result: The authors demonstrate that the combined application of intracavity and external squeezing enhances the readout performance compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: The proposed universal squeezing-enhanced readout approach offers a promising route for improving measurements of bosonic qubits in hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Frequency- And Amplitude-Modulated Gates For Universal Quantum Control
authors: Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, And William D. Oliver
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, and William D. Oliver

A new theoretical framework based on Floquet analysis enables quantum gate optimization using frequency and amplitude modulations, finding high fidelity and fast gates in superconducting circuits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033066] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A new Floquet-based theoretical framework enables optimized quantum gates using frequency and amplitude modulation in superconducting circuits.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity and fast quantum gates, which are crucial for practical quantum computing in superconducting platforms.
method: The authors develop a Floquet analysis-based framework to design frequency- and amplitude-modulated control pulses for quantum gate optimization.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity and fast gates in superconducting circuits, validating the effectiveness of the approach.
conclusion: This framework provides a systematic method for quantum control optimization, potentially advancing gate performance in superconducting qubits.

title: Dispersive Qubit Readout With Intrinsic Resonator Reset
authors: M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. Divincenzo, R. Barends, And P. A. Bushev
abstract:
Author(s): M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. DiVincenzo, R. Barends, and P. A. Bushev

Researchers experimentally demonstrate a new method for large-bandwidth dispersive readout, with built-in resonator reset, providing potential applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033042] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: An experimental demonstration of a large-bandwidth dispersive qubit readout method with built-in resonator reset for superconducting qubits.
motivation: Fast, high-fidelity qubit readout and rapid resonator reset are essential for quantum error correction and scalable superconducting quantum computing.
method: The authors implement a dispersive readout protocol with an intrinsic reset mechanism, likely using engineered resonator dynamics or tunable coupling, and characterize its performance experimentally.
result: They achieve large-bandwidth readout and built-in resonator reset, showing improved measurement speed and potential for reducing crosstalk in qubit arrays.
conclusion: This method provides a practical building block for superconducting qubit architectures, particularly for quantum error correction applications.

title: Optical Depth Dictates Universal Bounds On Many-Body Decay In Atomic Ensembles
authors: Cosimo C. Rusconi, Eric Sierra, Wai-Keong Mok, Avishi Poddar, Simon B. Jäger, And Ana Asenjo-Garcia
abstract:
Author(s): Cosimo C. Rusconi, Eric Sierra, Wai-Keong Mok, Avishi Poddar, Simon B. Jäger, and Ana Asenjo-Garcia

Cooperative emission is well understood for idealized symmetric systems, but its fundamental limits in spatially extended, free-space ensembles remain an open question. Here, we derive a universal law for the scaling of the maximum photon emission rate with system size that unifies both ordered arra…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 143603] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a universal law governing how the maximum photon emission rate scales with system size in spatially extended, free-space atomic ensembles, showing that optical depth dictates the bound.
motivation: Cooperative emission such as superradiance and subradiance is well understood for idealized symmetric systems, but the fundamental limits of collective decay in realistic spatially extended free-space ensembles remained an open question.
method: The authors develop an analytical theory of many-body collective emission in free-space atomic ensembles, characterizing how the maximum photon emission rate scales with system size and identifying optical depth as the controlling parameter, unifying ordered arrays and disordered ensembles.
result: They obtain a universal bound on the maximum photon emission rate set by the optical depth, yielding a scaling law that interpolates between the regimes of ordered arrays and extended disordered ensembles.
conclusion: Optical depth provides a universal organizing principle for many-body decay in atomic ensembles, connecting collective radiative behavior across widely different geometries and providing fundamental limits for cooperative emission.

title: Quantum Thermal State Preparation For Near-Term Quantum Processors
authors: Jerome Lloyd And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): Jerome Lloyd and Dmitry A. Abanin

Researchers develop an algorithm that prepares many-body quantum thermal states accurately by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031053] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: Researchers propose an algorithm combining bath resetting and modulated coupling to prepare many-body quantum thermal states accurately on near-term quantum processors.
motivation: Accurate preparation of thermal states is challenging for near-term quantum devices but essential for studying quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The algorithm combines bath resetting, where the system repeatedly interacts with a reset bath, with modulated coupling to efficiently drive the system toward its thermal state.
result: The approach achieves accurate many-body thermal state preparation, making it suitable for implementation on near-term quantum processors.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route for quantum thermal state preparation on near-term hardware, advancing quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Universal Sample Complexity Bounds In Quantum Learning Theory Via Fisher Information Matrix
authors: Hyukgun Kwon, Seok Hyung Lie, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Hyukgun Kwon, Seok Hyung Lie, and Liang Jiang

A framework shows that the sample complexity of general quantum learning is governed by the inverse Fisher information matrix.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033063] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: A framework establishes universal sample complexity bounds for general quantum learning tasks in terms of the accessible information, covering both classical and quantum data.

title: High-Rate Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution Under Intense Noise
authors: Hong-Wei Li, Wei-Xin Xie, Chun-Mei Zhang, Guan-Jie Fan-Yuan, Yu-Long Wang, Yu-Xuan Fan, Shuang Wang, Zhen-Qiang Yin, Wei Chen, De-Yong He, Guang-Can Guo, And Zheng-Fu Han
abstract:
Author(s): Hong-Wei Li, Wei-Xin Xie, Chun-Mei Zhang, Guan-Jie Fan-Yuan, Yu-Long Wang, Yu-Xuan Fan, Shuang Wang, Zhen-Qiang Yin, Wei Chen, De-Yong He, Guang-Can Guo, and Zheng-Fu Han

Measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) is a promising path toward practical quantum communication, but current high-performance demonstrations come at prohibitive overhead and isolated environments. Here, we present a high-speed MDI-QKD system operating at an unprecedented…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 140803] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate a high-speed measurement-device-independent QKD system that maintains high key rates even under intense noise, enabling more practical deployment.
motivation: MDI-QKD is attractive for practical quantum communication because it removes detector side channels, but existing high-performance demonstrations require prohibitive experimental overhead and carefully isolated environments.
method: They build a high-speed MDI-QKD setup with optimized optics, fast clocking, and noise-tolerant protocol parameters, and characterize its performance under realistic intense-noise conditions.
result: The system achieves an unprecedented key rate while tolerating strong noise, showing that high-rate MDI-QKD can operate outside isolated laboratory conditions.
conclusion: The work brings MDI-QKD closer to field-deployable quantum networks by demonstrating robust, high-rate operation under adverse conditions.

title: Enhanced Charging In Open Rabi And Dicke Quantum Batteries
authors: A-Long Zhou, Nuo Xu, Ya-Wen Xiao, Li-Li Gao, Long-Jie Li, Zi-Min Li, And Chuan-Cun Shu
abstract:
Author(s): A-Long Zhou, Nuo Xu, Ya-Wen Xiao, Li-Li Gao, Long-Jie Li, Zi-Min Li, and Chuan-Cun Shu

We investigate open-system charging protocols for Rabi and Dicke quantum batteries under direct incoherent pumping. The charging dynamics follows a Lindblad master equation, while effective non-Hermitian generators describe the conditioned no-jump mechanism. For a single Rabi battery, this pumping s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043701] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies open-system charging protocols for Rabi and Dicke quantum batteries under direct incoherent pumping using Lindblad and effective non-Hermitian descriptions.
