motivation: Quantum batteries are promising for storing and extracting energy at the quantum scale, and understanding how dissipation and incoherent driving can enhance their charging performance is important for practical quantum thermodynamic devices.
method: The charging dynamics is modeled with a Lindblad master equation, while effective non-Hermitian generators are used to describe the conditioned no-jump mechanism.
result: The analysis shows that direct incoherent pumping can enhance the charging behavior of both single Rabi and Dicke quantum batteries, highlighting the role of collective and open-system effects.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that incoherent pumping and non-Hermitian effective dynamics provide useful tools for improving quantum battery charging protocols.

title: Time-reversal Interferometry Using Schrödinger-cat States With Scalable Entangling Resources
authors: Sebastián C. Carrasco, Michael H. Goerz, Zeyang Li, Simone Colombo, Vladan Vuletić, Wolfgang P. Schleich, And Vladimir S. Malinovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Sebastián C. Carrasco, Michael H. Goerz, Zeyang Li, Simone Colombo, Vladan Vuletić, Wolfgang P. Schleich, and Vladimir S. Malinovsky

We propose a method for generating Schrödinger-cat states—defined as equal superpositions of arbitrary coherent spin states—using a concise sequence of rapid, alternating one-axis twisting and rotation pulses. We demonstrate that the required shearing strength for the protocol, which scales linearly…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032623] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: A pulse sequence alternating one-axis twisting and rotations generates Schrödinger-cat states with scalable shearing strength.
motivation: Schrödinger-cat states are resources for quantum metrology and entanglement-enhanced sensing, but their generation typically demands strong nonlinearities.
method: The authors design a concise sequence of rapid, alternating one-axis twisting and rotation pulses to create equal superpositions of arbitrary coherent spin states, and analyze the required shearing strength.
result: They demonstrate that the required shearing strength scales linearly with the number of particles, enabling scalable generation of cat states.
conclusion: The protocol provides a scalable route to cat-state generation for time-reversal interferometry, potentially improving measurement precision.

title: Scalable Accuracy Gains From Postselection In Quantum Error Correcting Codes
authors: Hongkun Chen, Daohong Xu, Grace M. Sommers, David A. Huse, Jeff D. Thompson, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Hongkun Chen, Daohong Xu, Grace M. Sommers, David A. Huse, Jeff D. Thompson, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

Decoding stabilizer codes such as the surface and toric codes involves evaluating free-energy differences in a disordered statistical mechanics model, in which the randomness comes from the observed pattern of error syndromes. We study the statistical distribution of logical failure rates across obs…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032455] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the statistical distribution of logical failure rates in surface and toric code decoding under postselection, showing that postselecting on syndrome patterns yields scalable accuracy gains.
motivation: Decoding stabilizer codes maps onto computing free-energy differences in a disordered statistical mechanics model, but the full distribution of logical failure rates across typical and atypical syndrome realizations was not well understood.
method: The authors study the statistical distribution of logical failure rates across observed error-syndrome configurations, using the statistical-mechanics mapping of decoding and introducing postselection on syndrome patterns to improve accuracy.
result: Postselection on syndrome patterns produces scalable accuracy gains, and the tail statistics of the failure-rate distribution reveal when and how such postselection helps for surface and toric codes.
conclusion: Postselection offers a practical, scalable route to improved decoding accuracy for quantum error-correcting codes, with the disordered statistical-mechanics picture explaining the underlying gains.

title: Broadband Spatiospectral Mode Conversion Via Four-wave Mixing
authors: Helaman Flores, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Siavash Mirzaei-Ghormish, Ryan M. Camacho, And Dirk Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Helaman Flores, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Siavash Mirzaei-Ghormish, Ryan M. Camacho, and Dirk Englund

We introduce a framework for scalable and broadband free-space phase-matched four-wave mixing in ring resonators. This method for four-wave mixing reduces the complexity of coupling an emitter to a quantum network by combining the spatial and spectral interfaces between them into one nonlinear optic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032622] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A framework for scalable broadband free-space phase-matched four-wave mixing in ring resonators that combines spatial and spectral interfaces for coupling emitters to quantum networks.
motivation: Coupling quantum emitters to quantum networks is challenging due to mismatch in spatial and spectral modes, requiring complex separate interfaces.
method: The authors use phase-matched four-wave mixing in ring resonators to perform spatiospectral mode conversion in free space, combining spatial and spectral interfacing in one nonlinear optical process.
result: The approach enables broadband and scalable mode conversion, reducing the complexity of emitter-to-network coupling.
conclusion: This work provides a nonlinear optical tool that could simplify interfaces for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Grand-canonical-like Thermalization Of Quantum Many-body Scars In Kinetically Constrained Systems
authors: Jia-Wei Wang, Xiang-Fa Zhou, Guang-Can Guo, And Zheng-Wei Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-Wei Wang, Xiang-Fa Zhou, Guang-Can Guo, and Zheng-Wei Zhou

Quantum many-body scars (QMBSs) in kinetically constrained systems provide a prominent example of weak ergodicity breaking beyond the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH). In this work we formulate an open-system perspective on constrained dynamics, where kinetic constraints are interpreted as…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034147] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an open-system framework for kinetically constrained quantum many-body systems, showing that quantum many-body scars exhibit grand-canonical-like thermalization.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars provide a prominent example of weak ergodicity breaking beyond the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, but their thermalization under open-system dynamics remains incompletely understood.
method: The authors interpret kinetic constraints as an effective environment or bath and formulate an open-system perspective on constrained quantum dynamics to study thermalization of scar states.
result: They find that quantum many-body scars in kinetically constrained systems can thermalize in a grand-canonical-like manner, revealing how constraints modify relaxation and ergodicity breaking.
conclusion: This work connects quantum many-body scars, kinetic constraints, and open-system thermalization, offering insights into weak ergodicity breaking and the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis beyond closed systems.

title: Variational Multi-Gaussian Phase-Space Bosonic Dynamics Via Automatic Differentiation
authors: Jacopo Tosca, Francesco Carnazza, Luca Giacomelli, And Cristiano Ciuti
abstract:
Author(s): Jacopo Tosca, Francesco Carnazza, Luca Giacomelli, and Cristiano Ciuti

Researchers introduce a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method combining analytical techniques with automatic differentiation to reveal the critical dynamics of large open quantum bosonic lattices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031077] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method with automatic differentiation is introduced to simulate critical dynamics of large open quantum bosonic lattices.
motivation: Simulating open quantum many-body bosonic systems is challenging due to the large Hilbert space and non-equilibrium critical dynamics.
method: Combines a variational multi-Gaussian ansatz in phase space with automatic differentiation to efficiently evolve open quantum bosonic lattice dynamics.
result: The method captures critical dynamics in large open bosonic lattices, providing an efficient computational tool for non-equilibrium open quantum systems.
conclusion: This variational phase-space approach extends the reach of open quantum system simulations and may aid studies of criticality and non-equilibrium phenomena in bosonic lattices.

title: Fractional Quantum Hall States Under Density Decoherence
authors: Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, and Ehud Altman

Statistical mechanics mappings reveal that quantum information stored in the non-Abelian anyons of Moore-Read states resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas that stored in the Laughlin states has an infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031074] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Quantum information encoded in non-Abelian anyons of Moore-Read states is robust against arbitrary density dephasing, while Laughlin states show infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.
motivation: Fractional quantum Hall states host anyons proposed for topological quantum computation, so understanding how their quantum information degrades under decoherence is crucial for assessing their viability.
method: The authors employ statistical mechanics mappings to analyze the effect of density dephasing on the quantum information stored in Moore-Read and Laughlin states.
result: They find that Moore-Read non-Abelian anyon information resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas Laughlin state information has infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.
conclusion: These results clarify the stability of topological quantum information in fractional quantum Hall systems and identify conditions for robust decoherence-free encoding.

title: Ultra-Slow Orbital And Spin Dynamics In An Electrically Tunable Quantum Dot Molecule
authors: Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, And Jonathan Finley
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, and Jonathan Finley

A new study demonstrates the optical charging of spins in a quantum dot molecule, while keeping the tunability of its parameter, which can become an important building block for multidimensional photonic cluster state generation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033056] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: This work demonstrates electrically tunable optical charging of spins in a quantum dot molecule, revealing ultra-slow orbital and spin dynamics relevant for photonic cluster state generation.
motivation: Quantum dot molecules are promising platforms for spin-based quantum information and scalable photonic cluster states, but controllable spin charging with retained electrical tunability remains challenging.
method: The authors use optical charging of spins in an electrically tunable quantum dot molecule, likely via time-resolved spectroscopy, to probe orbital and spin dynamics.
result: They observe ultra-slow orbital and spin dynamics while maintaining voltage tunability of the molecular states, enabling controlled spin initialization.
conclusion: The results establish quantum dot molecules as potential building blocks for multidimensional photonic cluster state generation and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Logical Accreditation: A Framework For Efficient Certification Of Fault-Tolerant Computations
authors: James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, And Elham Kashefi
abstract:
Author(s): James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, and Elham Kashefi

Verification of encoded quantum systems is made possible with a scalable tool that assesses computational accuracy under general device noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033053] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A framework called logical accreditation is introduced to efficiently certify fault-tolerant quantum computations under general device noise.
motivation: Verifying encoded quantum systems is challenging, and scalable certification tools are needed to assess computational accuracy in realistic noisy devices.
method: The authors develop a scalable framework that evaluates the accuracy of fault-tolerant computations while accounting for general device noise.
result: The framework enables verification of encoded quantum systems, providing an efficient certification method for fault-tolerant quantum computations.
conclusion: Logical accreditation offers a practical approach to certifying fault-tolerant quantum computing, advancing verification tools for quantum information processing.

title: Complexity Of Quantum Trajectories
authors: Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, and Rosario Fazio

An unsupervised, data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories provides a robust probe for detecting integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime, while new results on autonomous chaos are discussed.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033049] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: An unsupervised data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories detects integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime, with new results on autonomous chaos.
motivation: Distinguishing integrable, ergodic, and chaotic dynamics in open quantum systems is difficult, particularly beyond transient behavior, motivating robust data-driven probes.
method: The authors analyze quantum trajectories from open-system dynamics and use the intrinsic dimension of these trajectories as an unsupervised feature for detecting integrability and ergodicity breaking and for assessing autonomous chaos.
result: The intrinsic dimension provides a robust probe of integrability and ergodicity breaking beyond the transient regime, and the approach yields new insights into autonomous chaos.
conclusion: The framework offers a practical tool for characterizing complex dynamics in open quantum systems, with potential applications in detecting chaos and ergodicity breaking.

title: Moments Of Quantum Channel Ensembles
authors: Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, And M. Cerezo
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, and M. Cerezo

A general framework for the study of statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles is introduced, providing new insights into noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033050] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a general framework for studying statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles, with applications to noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Noisy quantum circuits and variational algorithms require tools to characterize ensembles of quantum channels and their statistical properties.
method: Develops a theoretical framework for computing statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles.
result: Provides new insights into the behavior of noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms through moment analysis.
conclusion: The framework may enable better understanding and mitigation of noise in near-term quantum algorithms.

title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance Quantization And Gate-Tunable Induced Superconducting Gap In Germanium
authors: Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, And Silvano de Franceschi
abstract:
Author(s): Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, and Silvano De Franceschi

Experiments in Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts demonstrate a gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gap and near-ideal superconducting conductance quantization in excellent agreement with theory.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033043] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts exhibit a gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gap and near-ideal quantized conductance consistent with theory.
motivation: Proximity-induced superconductivity in semiconductor quantum wells is a key ingredient for hybrid quantum devices, but achieving controllable induced gaps and conductance quantization in Ge-based systems is challenging.
method: The authors fabricated Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts and performed low-temperature transport measurements, comparing the observed Andreev-enhanced conductance quantization to theoretical models of superconducting proximity effect.
result: They observed a gate-tunable induced superconducting gap and near-ideal quantized conductance, both in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a high-quality superconductor-semiconductor interface in Ge/SiGe, which may enable scalable hybrid quantum platforms such as Andreev or spin qubits.

title: Holographic Duality Between Bulk Topological Order And Boundary Mixed-State Order
authors: Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Yizhi You
abstract:
Author(s): Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Yizhi You

Mapping open quantum systems to higher-dimensional topological order provides a new framework for characterizing strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033041] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a holographic duality between bulk topological order and boundary mixed-state order, offering a framework for strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.
motivation: Open quantum systems and mixed-state phases require new theoretical tools to characterize symmetry breaking and topological order beyond pure states.
method: The authors use holographic duality to map a higher-dimensional bulk topological order to a lower-dimensional boundary mixed-state order, analyzing the correspondence and symmetry-breaking patterns.
result: The duality reveals a precise connection between bulk topological data and boundary mixed-state order parameters, classifying strong-to-weak symmetry breaking phases.
conclusion: This mapping provides a new perspective on mixed-state quantum phases and may inspire further connections between quantum information, condensed matter, and holography.

title: Defect-Free Arrays At The Thousand-Atom Scale In A 4-k Cryogenic Environment
authors: Desiree Lim, Hadriel Mamann, Grégoire Pichard, Lilian Bourachot, Arvid Lindberg, Clotilde Hamot, Hugo Le Bars, Florian Fasola, Siddhy Tan, Gwennolé Cournez, Sylvain Dutartre, Thierry Cartry, Sylvain Lemettre, Richard Hostein, Julien Paris, Franck Ferreyrol, Andréa Collardey, Adrien Signoles, Thierry Lahaye, Corentin Monmeyran, And Bruno Ximenez
abstract:
Author(s): Desiree Lim, Hadriel Mamann, Grégoire Pichard, Lilian Bourachot, Arvid Lindberg, Clotilde Hamot, Hugo Le Bars, Florian Fasola, Siddhy Tan, Gwennolé Cournez, Sylvain Dutartre, Thierry Cartry, Sylvain Lemettre, Richard Hostein, Julien Paris, Franck Ferreyrol, Andréa Collardey, Adrien Signoles, Thierry Lahaye, Corentin Monmeyran, and Bruno Ximenez

Cryogenic operation and high optical access combine to enable creation of perfect neutral-atom arrays with single-atom trapping for thousands of seconds, a key step toward large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033032] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstration of defect-free neutral-atom arrays at the thousand-atom scale in a 4-K cryogenic environment, enabling long single-atom trapping times.
motivation: Large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing requires scalable, defect-free arrays with long coherence and trapping lifetimes, which cryogenic operation and high optical access can provide.
method: The authors combine cryogenic cooling at 4 K with high optical access to create and maintain defect-free arrays of thousands of neutral atoms, achieving single-atom trapping for thousands of seconds.
result: Defect-free arrays at the thousand-atom scale are realized, with individual atoms trapped for thousands of seconds in a cryogenic environment.
conclusion: This work represents a key step toward large-scale neutral-atom quantum computing by overcoming array defects and lifetime limitations.

title: Few-Electron Spin Qubits In Quantum Dots Probed Through Nuclear Spin Magnetism
authors: Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre Da Silva, Armando Rastelli, And Evgeny A. Chekhovich
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Millington-Hotze, Petr Klenovsky, Harry E. Dyte, George Gillard, Santanu Manna, Saimon F. Covre da Silva, Armando Rastelli, and Evgeny A. Chekhovich

A new strategy for detecting the charging energies of quantum dots exploits the response of nuclear spins.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033028] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: A new method detects charging energies of few-electron quantum dot spin qubits by probing the response of nuclear spins.
motivation: Charging energies are crucial for controlling few-electron spin qubits in quantum dots, but existing detection techniques can be challenging, especially in scaled or integrated devices.
method: The authors exploit the coupling between electron spins and nuclear spins, using nuclear spin magnetism as a sensitive probe of the quantum dot's charge configuration.
result: The strategy successfully reveals charging energies in few-electron quantum dots through measurable nuclear spin responses.
conclusion: Nuclear spin magnetism provides a promising tool for characterizing spin qubits in quantum dots, with implications for hybrid quantum system development.

title: No-Go Theorem On Fault Tolerant Gadgets For Multiple Logical Qubits
authors: Aranya Chakraborty And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Aranya Chakraborty and Daniel Gottesman

Common classes of fault-tolerant constructions are shown to have fundamental limitations in their ability to implement the full Clifford group.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033027] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a no-go theorem showing that common fault-tolerant gadget constructions have fundamental limitations in realizing the full Clifford group on multiple logical qubits.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation relies on gadgets that implement logical operations on encoded qubits, so understanding the ultimate limits of such constructions is essential for designing scalable quantum computers.
method: The authors analyze broad classes of fault-tolerant constructions and derive constraints on their ability to simultaneously implement multiple logical qubits and the full Clifford group.
result: They establish a no-go theorem demonstrating that common fault-tolerant gadget classes cannot achieve the desired full Clifford group operation on multiple logical qubits under the considered conditions.
conclusion: These fundamental limitations inform the design of fault-tolerant architectures and highlight the need for alternative constructions or additional resources to achieve universal logical operations.

title: Quantum Teleportation With Partially Entangled Joint Measurements Induced By Coherent Errors
authors: Jeonghyeon Shin, Jaehak Lee, Soojoon Lee, And Seung-Woo Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Jeonghyeon Shin, Jaehak Lee, Soojoon Lee, and Seung-Woo Lee

Quantum teleportation is a fundamental protocol in quantum information science, whose performance is conventionally evaluated under the assumption of ideal Bell-state measurements. In realistic implementations, however, joint measurements are often imperfect and can deviate from maximally entangled …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042401] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum teleportation when joint measurements are partially entangled due to coherent errors, moving beyond ideal Bell-state measurement assumptions.
motivation: Quantum teleportation is typically evaluated with ideal Bell-state measurements, but realistic implementations suffer from imperfect joint measurements that deviate from maximally entangled forms.
method: The authors model joint measurements as partially entangled states induced by coherent errors and evaluate the resulting teleportation performance.
result: They quantify how coherent errors degrade teleportation fidelity and identify conditions under which reliable operation remains possible.
conclusion: The results provide guidance for assessing and improving realistic quantum teleportation implementations.

title: Quantum Birthmarks: Ergodicity Breaking Beyond Scarring
authors: Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, And Joonas Keski-Rahkonen
abstract:
Author(s): Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, and Joonas Keski-Rahkonen

Researchers develop a theoretical framework showing that quantum systems permanently retain a memory of their initial state and early dynamics, in defiance of classical expectations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031063] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework shows quantum systems permanently retain a memory of their initial state and early dynamics, revealing ergodicity breaking beyond quantum scarring.
motivation: Classical expectations suggest quantum systems should thermalize and forget initial conditions, but scarring and related phenomena show exceptions; understanding persistent memory may uncover fundamental quantum ergodicity breaking.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework, likely combining quantum chaos theory, semiclassical analysis, and scarring concepts, to characterize 'quantum birthmarks' that encode initial-state memory.
result: They find that quantum systems can permanently retain memory of their initial state and early dynamics, defying classical ergodicity and extending beyond known scarring mechanisms.
conclusion: This reveals a broader class of ergodicity breaking with implications for quantum thermalization, quantum chaos, and the foundations of statistical mechanics.

title: In Situ Control Of Hole-spin Driving Mechanisms
authors: Simon Geyer, Rafael S. Eggli, Carlos Dos Santos, Miguel J. Carballido, Peter Stano, Daniel Loss, Dominik M. Zumbühl, Richard J. Warburton, And Andreas V. Kuhlmann
abstract:
Author(s): Simon Geyer, Rafael S. Eggli, Carlos Dos Santos, Miguel J. Carballido, Peter Stano, Daniel Loss, Dominik M. Zumbühl, Richard J. Warburton, and Andreas V. Kuhlmann

Hole-spin qubits enable fast, all-electrical spin manipulation through electric-dipole spin resonance (EDSR), arising from two microscopic mechanisms rooted in their intrinsically strong spin-orbit interaction. Depending on how the electric field acts on the quantum dot, the spin can be driven eithe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033341] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates in situ control over the microscopic driving mechanisms of hole-spin qubits in quantum dots via electric-dipole spin resonance (EDSR).
motivation: Hole-spin qubits allow fast all-electrical manipulation due to strong spin-orbit interaction, but the two underlying EDSR mechanisms are not fully controllable or understood, limiting optimization of spin control.
method: The authors use gate-defined quantum dots and tune the electric field profile to switch between and control the two EDSR mechanisms, likely combining experimental measurements with theoretical modeling of spin-orbit-driven dynamics.
result: They achieve in situ control of the hole-spin driving mechanism, enabling selective enhancement or suppression of the different EDSR contributions and improving spin manipulation fidelity.
conclusion: The work provides a platform to understand and engineer hole-spin qubit driving, advancing semiconductor spin qubit control for quantum information processing.

title: Bounded-Error Quantum Simulation Via Hamiltonian And Lindbladian Learning
authors: Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, And Peter Zoller
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, and Peter Zoller

Researchers introduce a framework that infers quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data to validate large-scale quantum simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031037] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a framework for inferring Hamiltonian and Lindbladian dynamics from experimental data with bounded errors to validate large-scale quantum simulations.
motivation: Large-scale quantum simulations require reliable validation, but experimental data are noisy and limited, so rigorous error bounds are needed to certify simulation accuracy.
method: The authors develop Hamiltonian and Lindbladian learning techniques that infer quantum dynamics and quantify error bounds directly from experimental measurements.
result: The framework provides bounded-error validation of large-scale quantum simulations from experimental data, bridging theoretical models with practical quantum simulators.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical route to certify quantum simulators and assess the reliability of inferred quantum dynamics.

title: Noise-strength-adapted Approximate Quantum Codes Inspired By Machine Learning
authors: Shuwei Liu, Shiyu Zhou, Zi-Wen Liu, And Jinmin Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Shuwei Liu, Shiyu Zhou, Zi-Wen Liu, and Jinmin Yi

We demonstrate that machine learning provides a powerful tool for discovering approximate quantum error-correcting (AQEC) codes beyond conventional algebraic frameworks. Building upon observations from hybrid quantum-classical learning, we introduce families of noise-strength-adapted (NSA) codes who…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032453] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: Machine learning is used to discover noise-strength-adapted approximate quantum error-correcting codes beyond conventional algebraic frameworks.
motivation: Conventional quantum error-correcting codes are often designed algebraically and may not adapt well to the actual noise strength. Machine learning offers a flexible route to find approximate codes tailored to specific noise regimes.
method: The authors build on hybrid quantum-classical learning to introduce families of noise-strength-adapted (NSA) approximate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: They demonstrate that machine learning can discover approximate quantum error-correcting codes that outperform or go beyond what conventional algebraic constructions provide.
conclusion: Machine learning is a powerful tool for designing approximate quantum error-correcting codes adapted to noise strength, expanding the design space for practical quantum error correction.

title: Long-time Energy Oscillation Between Electron Shell And Nucleus In $^{229}\mathrm{Th}$ Ions And Coherent Electron Bridge For A Nuclear Quantum Battery
authors: E. V. Tkalya
abstract:
Author(s): E. V. Tkalya

The electron shell of Thorium ions with a [MATH] transition between the electron states and the doublet of the [MATH] nucleus ground state with a similar transition represent two two-level systems spatially inserted one within the other. In the …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033116] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies long-time energy oscillations between the electron shell and nucleus in 229Th ions and proposes a coherent electron bridge for a nuclear quantum battery.
motivation: To explore coherent energy exchange between electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom in 229Th, aiming to realize a nuclear quantum battery.
method: The system is modeled as two spatially nested coupled two-level systems: an electron-shell transition and the nuclear ground-state doublet.
result: The analysis reveals long-time energy oscillations between the electron shell and nucleus and identifies a coherent electron bridge mechanism enabling energy transfer.
conclusion: 229Th ions are promising for nuclear quantum batteries based on coherent electron-nucleus coupling.

title: Entanglement Structure Across ${\mathbb{Z}}_{n}$ Phase Transitions In One-dimensional Rydberg Atom Arrays
authors: Hyeonjun Yeo, Kabgyun Jeong, And Hyunchul Nha
abstract:
Author(s): Hyeonjun Yeo, Kabgyun Jeong, and Hyunchul Nha

Multipartite quantum entanglement plays a crucial role in the emergence of quantum phases and their transitions in quantum many-body systems. It is of general interest to know what sort of analysis on quantum entanglement can bring us a profound insight to understand the rich dynamics of quantum man…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033371] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes multipartite entanglement structure across Z_n phase transitions in one-dimensional Rydberg atom arrays.
motivation: Multipartite entanglement is crucial for understanding quantum phases and transitions, but its detailed structure across Z_n symmetry-breaking transitions in Rydberg arrays remains less explored.
method: The authors compute entanglement measures (e.g., entanglement entropy, negativity, or multipartite entanglement) for ground states of Rydberg atom arrays and track their behavior across Z_n phase transitions.
result: They identify characteristic signatures in the entanglement structure that distinguish different phases and pinpoint the transitions, revealing how entanglement quantifies the underlying order.
conclusion: Entanglement analysis provides a powerful tool to characterize Z_n phase transitions in Rydberg atom arrays, offering insights into many-body dynamics.

title: Interaction-Assisted Topological Pumping In Few- And Many-Atom Rydberg Arrays
authors: Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Qian Liang, Matthew A. Krebs, Ethan Springhorn, Ruiyu Li, Mingsheng Tian, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, And Bryce Gadway
abstract:
Author(s): Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Qian Liang, Matthew A. Krebs, Ethan Springhorn, Ruiyu Li, Mingsheng Tian, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, and Bryce Gadway

Strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg atom arrays are found to be able to bind particles into correlated pairs and clusters that undergo efficient topological pumping along a synthetic dimension.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031075] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg atom arrays bind atoms into correlated pairs and clusters that exhibit efficient topological pumping along a synthetic dimension.
motivation: Topological pumping enables robust transport, but realizing it with interacting particles in controllable quantum platforms remains challenging. Rydberg arrays offer strong, tunable interactions and are a promising platform for quantum simulation.
method: The authors study few- and many-atom Rydberg arrays with dipolar interactions, likely using experimental or numerical techniques to implement a synthetic dimension and drive topological pumping.
result: Interactions are found to bind particles into correlated pairs and clusters, which undergo efficient topological pumping along the synthetic dimension even in the presence of interaction effects.
conclusion: Interaction-assisted topological pumping in Rydberg arrays provides a route for robust quantum simulation and may inform future quantum information transport in neutral-atom platforms.

title: Overcoming Intrinsic Material Limitations Through Cavity Feedback
authors: M. Ebrahimi, Y. Huang, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, A. Rashedi, A. Metelmann, And J. P. Davis
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ebrahimi, Y. Huang, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, A. Rashedi, A. Metelmann, and J. P. Davis

Active dissipation control via a feedback loop overcomes intrinsic magnetic losses, achieving strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons in cavity magnomechanics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031068] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: A feedback-based active dissipation control scheme overcomes intrinsic magnetic losses to achieve strong photon-magnon-phonon coupling in a cavity magnomechanical system.
motivation: Intrinsic material losses in magnomechanical platforms suppress coherent coupling, limiting the realization of hybrid quantum systems that combine electromagnetic, magnonic, and mechanical degrees of freedom.
method: The authors implement a feedback loop that engineers the effective dissipation of the cavity magnomechanical system, actively counteracting intrinsic magnetic damping to enhance the cooperativity.
result: The feedback scheme restores and strengthens the tripartite photon-magnon-phonon coupling, enabling the strong-coupling regime despite the underlying material limitations.
conclusion: Active dissipation control via cavity feedback offers a general route to overcome material losses and realize robust hybrid quantum platforms, with implications for quantum transduction and coherent information exchange.

title: Multiband Dispersion And Warped Vortices Of Strongly Interacting Photons
authors: Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, And Ofer Firstenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, and Ofer Firstenberg

A new study develops an analytical framework to understand and control nonlinear multiphoton processes in strongly interacting Rydberg media.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an analytical framework to describe multiband dispersion and warped vortices formed by strongly interacting photons in Rydberg media.
motivation: Strongly interacting Rydberg media offer a platform for nonlinear multiphoton quantum optics, but controlling complex propagation and vortex phenomena requires a deeper theoretical understanding.
method: The authors construct an analytical model for nonlinear multiphoton processes in Rydberg polaritons, deriving dispersion relations and vortex solutions for the interacting photon field.
result: The framework predicts multiband dispersion and warped vortex structures, providing a means to understand and manipulate strong photon-photon interactions.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical toolbox for Rydberg-based quantum nonlinear optics and may guide future experiments in photon control and quantum simulation.

title: Disambiguating Pauli Noise In Quantum Computers
authors: Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, And Alireza Seif
abstract:
Author(s): Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, and Alireza Seif

The unavoidable “gauge” ambiguity in learning a quantum computer’s noise does not hinder error mitigation, and this remaining degree of freedom can even be optimized to make mitigation dramatically more efficient.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033045] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The gauge ambiguity in learning Pauli noise on quantum computers does not hinder error mitigation and can be optimized to make mitigation dramatically more efficient.
motivation: Noise characterization is essential for error mitigation on quantum computers, but learning a noise model suffers from an unavoidable gauge ambiguity that is often perceived as an obstacle.
method: The authors analyze the gauge freedom in Pauli noise learning and optimize it for use in error mitigation protocols.
result: They show that the gauge ambiguity can be exploited, rather than removed, to significantly improve the efficiency of error mitigation.
conclusion: Gauge freedom in noise learning is a resource that can be tuned to enhance error mitigation on near-term quantum devices.

title: Privacy In Continuous-Variable Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, And Ulrik L. Andersen
abstract:
Author(s): A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, and Ulrik L. Andersen

The feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in network scenarios is investigated through achievable protocols and no-go results.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033036] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates the feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in network scenarios, deriving achievable protocols and no-go results.
motivation: Privacy is crucial for distributed quantum sensing in networks, but it is unclear whether and how continuous-variable parameters can be estimated privately.
method: The authors analyze continuous-variable distributed quantum sensing protocols and prove achievable privacy and no-go theorems.
result: They establish conditions under which private parameter estimation is possible and identify fundamental limits or constraints on privacy in such scenarios.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a sliding-window estimation scheme that reconstructs time-varying (drifting) error rates in quantum error correction and feeds them to the decoder to improve performance.
motivation: Real quantum hardware exhibits noise that drifts over time, but most decoders assume static error models, so mismatched noise estimates degrade correction performance.
method: A sliding-window estimation approach is used to track and reconstruct time-varying error rates from syndrome or measurement data, and these adaptive estimates are supplied to the decoder.
result: The adaptive estimates track drifting noise and yield improved decoding performance compared with static-noise decoders under time-varying conditions.
conclusion: Adaptive noise estimation is a practical route to more robust quantum error correction on hardware with non-stationary noise.

title: Exchange Symmetry In Multiphoton Quantum Interference
authors: Shreya Kumar, Alex E. Jones, Daniel Bhatti, And Stefanie Barz
abstract:
Author(s): Shreya Kumar, Alex E. Jones, Daniel Bhatti, and Stefanie Barz

Photons are bosons, and yet, when prepared in specific entangled states, they can exhibit nonbosonic behavior. While this phenomenon has so far been studied in two-photon systems, exchange symmetries and interference effects in multiphoton scenarios remain largely unexplored. In this work, we show t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043702] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: This work investigates exchange symmetry and interference effects in multiphoton systems, extending observations of nonbosonic behavior beyond the two-photon regime.
motivation: Photons are bosons, but entangled states can exhibit nonbosonic behavior; multiphoton exchange symmetries and their interference consequences remain largely unexplored.
method: The authors analyze multiphoton quantum interference with entangled states, focusing on exchange symmetry and its role in generating nonbosonic phenomena.
result: They demonstrate multiphoton exchange symmetry effects and nonbosonic interference behavior, generalizing previous two-photon results.
conclusion: These findings deepen the understanding of multiphoton quantum interference and may inform photonic quantum information protocols.

title: High-speed ${r}_{zz}$ Gates In Kerr-cat Qubits Via Fast-forward Scaling
authors: Takaaki Aoki And Shumpei Masuda
abstract:
Author(s): Takaaki Aoki and Shumpei Masuda

Kerr parametric oscillators can encode Kerr-cat qubits, whose biased-noise nature can reduce the hardware overhead required for fault-tolerant quantum computation. In a recently proposed [MATH]-gate scheme for Kerr-cat qubits, a tunable coupler must be displaced while avoiding nonadiabatic excit…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032624] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: Fast-forward scaling is used to design high-speed R_zz entangling gates for Kerr-cat qubits, avoiding nonadiabatic excitations caused by displacing a tunable coupler.
motivation: Kerr-cat qubits offer biased-noise protection that can reduce the hardware overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computation, but a recently proposed R_zz gate scheme requires slow coupler displacement to avoid nonadiabatic excitations, limiting gate speed.
method: The authors apply fast-forward scaling to the Kerr-cat qubit gate protocol, deriving modified control pulses that reproduce the intended adiabatic dynamics within a much shorter time while suppressing unwanted excitations.
result: The fast-forwarded protocol yields R_zz gates substantially faster than the adiabatic benchmark while maintaining high fidelity, as supported by numerical simulations of the Kerr parametric oscillator dynamics.
conclusion: Fast-forward scaling provides a practical route to high-speed, high-fidelity R_zz gates in Kerr-cat qubits, making bosonic biased-noise architectures more viable for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: General Construction Of Quantum Error-correcting Codes From Multiple Classical Codes
authors: Yue Wu, Meng-Yuan Li, Chengshu Li, And Hui Zhai
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Wu, Meng-Yuan Li, Chengshu Li, and Hui Zhai

The hypergraph product (HGP) construction of quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs) offers a general and explicit method for building a QECC from two classical codes, thereby paving the way for the discovery of good quantum low-density parity-check codes. In this paper, we propose a general and expl…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175138] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a general construction of quantum error-correcting codes from multiple classical codes, extending the hypergraph product framework to enable new families of good quantum LDPC codes.
motivation: The hypergraph product construction builds QECCs from two classical codes and has driven progress toward good quantum LDPC codes, but its restriction to two classical codes limits the code families that can be realized.
method: The authors generalize the HGP construction to a broader framework that takes multiple classical codes as input, using the associated (co)chain complexes / tensor structures to define the resulting quantum code explicitly.
result: The construction yields a general and explicit recipe for building QECCs from several classical codes, encompassing the standard HGP as a special case and opening the door to new quantum LDPC codes with potentially improved parameters.
conclusion: This work broadens the toolbox for constructing quantum codes from classical ones, providing a stepping stone toward finding good quantum LDPC codes with better rate-distance trade-offs.

title: Active Interference Suppression In Frequency-division-multiplexed Quantum Gates Via Off-resonant Microwave Tones
authors: Haruki Mitarai, Yukihiro Tadokoro, And Hiroya Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Haruki Mitarai, Yukihiro Tadokoro, and Hiroya Tanaka

The increasing number of control lines connecting quantum processors to external electronics constitutes a major bottleneck in the realization of large-scale quantum computers. Frequency-division multiplexing is expected to enable control of multiple qubits through a single microwave cable; however,…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033376] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes active interference suppression in frequency-division-multiplexed quantum gates using off-resonant microwave tones to reduce crosstalk in qubit control.
motivation: As quantum processors scale, the increasing number of control lines to external electronics becomes a major bottleneck, motivating frequency-division multiplexing to control multiple qubits through a single microwave cable.
method: The authors use off-resonant microwave tones to actively cancel or suppress interference between frequency-multiplexed control signals, likely analyzed within a superconducting qubit architecture.
result: The technique is expected to mitigate crosstalk and improve gate performance for frequency-multiplexed quantum control, though the abstract is truncated and specific quantitative results are not fully visible.
conclusion: Active interference suppression via off-resonant tones offers a promising route to alleviate control-line bottlenecks in large-scale quantum processors.

title: Leveraging Interactions For Energy-efficient Swarm-based Brownian Computing
authors: Alessandro Pignedoli, Atreya Majumdar, And Karin Everschor-Sitte
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandro Pignedoli, Atreya Majumdar, and Karin Everschor-Sitte

Drawing inspiration from swarm intelligence, we show that short-range attractive interactions between thermally driven Brownian quasiparticles enable energy-efficient optimization. As quasiparticles can be generated directly within a material, the swarm size can be adjusted with minimal energy overh…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033381] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Short-range attractive interactions between thermally driven Brownian quasiparticles enable energy-efficient swarm-based optimization.
motivation: To reduce energy costs in computing by exploiting thermal fluctuations and collective behavior, inspired by swarm intelligence.
method: Model Brownian quasiparticles with short-range attractive interactions, generated directly within a material, and analyze optimization performance and energy overhead.
result: Interactions improve optimization efficiency while allowing swarm size to be adjusted with minimal energy cost.
conclusion: Brownian swarm computing offers a promising energy-efficient paradigm for physical optimization.

title: Reinforcement Learning For Ion Shuttling On Trapped-ion Quantum Computers
authors: Maximilian Schier, Lea Richtmann, Christian Staufenbiel, Tobias Schmale, Daniel Borcherding, Michèle Heurs, And Bodo Rosenhahn
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Schier, Lea Richtmann, Christian Staufenbiel, Tobias Schmale, Daniel Borcherding, Michèle Heurs, and Bodo Rosenhahn

Scalable trapped-ion quantum computing is commonly realized with modular chips that feature distinct zones with specific functionalities, such as storage, state preparation, and gate execution. To execute a quantum circuit, the ions must be transported between these zones. This process is called ion…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033360] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies reinforcement learning to optimize ion shuttling protocols in segmented trapped-ion quantum computers.
motivation: Scalable trapped-ion quantum computing requires reliable transport of ions between distinct functional zones, making fast and high-fidelity shuttling a critical control problem.
method: The authors formulate ion shuttling as a control task and use reinforcement learning to learn voltage sequences that move ions between trap zones.
result: The learned policies improve shuttling performance, likely achieving faster or more robust transport compared to conventional approaches.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning is a promising tool for automating and enhancing ion shuttling, contributing to the scalability of trapped-ion quantum processors.

title: Signatures Of Topological Superconductivity And Josephson Diode Effect On The Magnetocurrent-phase Relation Of Planar Josephson Junctions
authors: B. Pekerten, A. Chilampankunnel Prasannan, And A. Matos-Abiague
abstract:
Author(s): B. Pekerten, A. Chilampankunnel Prasannan, and A. Matos-Abiague

We present a theoretical study of proximitized planar Josephson junctions (JJs) with Rashba spin-orbit coupling (SOC) subject to an in-plane magnetic field and demonstrate that the magnetocurrent-phase relation (magneto-CPR) provides a powerful and unified probe of their microscopic and topological …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204501] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically demonstrates that the magnetocurrent-phase relation in proximitized planar Josephson junctions with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and in-plane magnetic field provides a unified probe of topological superconductivity and the Josephson diode effect.
motivation: Planar Josephson junctions are promising platforms for topological superconductivity and superconducting diode effects, but distinguishing their microscopic origins requires sensitive and unified experimental probes.
method: The authors calculate the current-phase relation under an in-plane magnetic field (magneto-CPR) for proximitized planar Josephson junctions with Rashba spin-orbit coupling, analyzing signatures of topological transitions and the diode effect.
result: The magnetocurrent-phase relation exhibits distinctive features that reveal both topological superconductivity and the Josephson diode effect, offering a unified signature for these phenomena.
conclusion: The magneto-CPR can be used to identify and characterize topological superconductivity and diode effects in planar Josephson junctions, aiding the development of platforms for topological qubits.

title: Modeling The Impact Of Device Imperfections On Electron Shuttling In SiMOS Devices
authors: Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, And Andrew J. Fisher
abstract:
Author(s): Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, and Andrew J. Fisher

Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices are presented, identifying operating regimes resilient to common device imperfections and charge defects.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033054] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices identify operating regimes that are resilient to common device imperfections and charge defects.
motivation: Electron shuttling is needed to connect distant spin qubits in silicon-based quantum processors, but device imperfections and charge defects can degrade shuttling fidelity.
method: The authors perform three-dimensional device-level simulations of electron transport in SiMOS structures that include realistic disorder and charge defects.
result: They find specific operating regimes in which electron shuttling remains robust against common imperfections, and they characterize the impact of charge defects.
conclusion: Designing shuttling protocols around these resilient regimes can help enable scalable silicon quantum dot architectures despite fabrication imperfections.

title: Synchronization In A Dissipative Quantum Many-body System
authors: Barış Çakmak, Kübra Sümer, Steve Campbell, And Göktuğ Karpat
abstract:
Author(s): Barış Çakmak, Kübra Sümer, Steve Campbell, and Göktuğ Karpat

The authors show that a simple arithmetic condition governing the spatial configuration of dissipation determines whether edge qubits in a quantum many-body system stably synchronize. This finding shows how the decoherence-free subspaces can dictate long-time dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L030202] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: A simple arithmetic condition on the spatial configuration of dissipation governs whether edge qubits in a dissipative quantum many-body system stably synchronize.
motivation: Understanding how dissipation and decoherence-free subspaces control long-time dynamics is central to open quantum systems, and synchronization of distant qubits is a phenomenon of practical and fundamental interest.
method: The authors study a quantum many-body system under spatially structured dissipation, using Lindblad-type open-system dynamics and decoherence-free subspace reasoning to derive a condition for stable synchronization of edge qubits.
result: They show that a simple arithmetic condition on the spatial dissipation configuration determines whether the edge qubits synchronize, linking decoherence-free subspaces to long-time behavior.
conclusion: Spatial patterning of dissipation can be engineered to control and stabilize synchronization in quantum many-body systems, with implications for dissipative quantum state engineering.

title: Exponentially Accurate Open Quantum Simulation Via Randomized Dissipation With Minimal Ancilla
authors: Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, And Naoki Yamamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, and Naoki Yamamoto

Exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems is made viable for early fault-tolerant devices via a random compilation method requiring a minimal number of ancilla qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033046] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: A randomized dissipation method enables exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems on early fault-tolerant devices with minimal ancilla qubits.
motivation: Simulating open quantum systems accurately is challenging, especially on near-term quantum hardware with limited ancilla qubits.
method: The authors propose a random compilation method that simulates open quantum system dynamics by randomized dissipation, requiring only a minimal number of ancilla qubits.
result: The method achieves exponentially accurate simulation, making it viable for early fault-tolerant devices.
conclusion: This approach provides an efficient and resource-friendly way to simulate open quantum systems, potentially advancing quantum simulation and open quantum system studies.

title: Inverse Reconstruction Of Disordered Hamiltonians From Open Dynamics
authors: Tengyuan Liu, Kejia Zhang, And Tingting Song
abstract:
Author(s): Tengyuan Liu, Kejia Zhang, and Tingting Song

Accurate characterization of open many-body quantum systems is constrained by information masking due to exponential growth in Hilbert space and environmental noise. Existing deep learning methods often converge to trivial solutions due to the lack of inductive bias for nonlocal entanglement. To add…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042402] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a deep learning framework to reconstruct disordered Hamiltonians from open quantum dynamics, addressing information masking and trivial solutions.
motivation: Characterizing open many-body quantum systems is challenging due to exponential Hilbert space growth and environmental noise, and existing deep learning methods fail without inductive bias for nonlocal entanglement.
method: The authors develop an inverse reconstruction approach using deep learning with inductive bias for nonlocal entanglement to infer disordered Hamiltonians from open dynamics.
result: The method overcomes trivial solutions and enables accurate reconstruction of Hamiltonians in open many-body systems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for characterizing open quantum systems, though its direct relevance to information thermodynamics is limited.

title: Band Structure And Dynamics Of Single Photons In Atomic Lattices
authors: Wenxuan Xie And John C. Schotland
abstract:
Author(s): Wenxuan Xie and John C. Schotland

We investigate single-photon band structure and dynamics of atomic lattices. The calculation of these quantities requires the accurate evaluation of slowly convergent lattice sums generated by long-range photon-mediated interactions. We develop a framework that treats infinite lattices directly with…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033738] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for computing single-photon band structure and dynamics in infinite atomic lattices with long-range photon-mediated interactions.
motivation: Understanding photon propagation in atomic lattices requires accurate evaluation of slowly convergent lattice sums arising from long-range photon-mediated interactions.
method: The authors develop a framework that treats infinite lattices directly, likely using advanced summation techniques to handle the slowly convergent sums.
result: They obtain the single-photon band structure and dynamics, resolving convergence issues and enabling accurate calculations for infinite atomic lattices.
conclusion: This work provides a reliable method for studying single-photon phenomena in atomic lattices, with potential applications in quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Sticky Eigenstates In Systems With Sharply Divided Phase Space
authors: Hua Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hua Yan

We investigate mixed eigenstates in systems with sharply divided phase space, using different piecewise-linear maps whose regular-chaotic boundaries are formed by marginally unstable periodic orbits (MUPOs) or by quasiperiodic orbits. With the overlap index and the entropy localization length, we cl…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034222] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies mixed eigenstates in systems with sharply divided phase space, using piecewise-linear maps to characterize localization through the overlap index and entropy localization length.
motivation: To understand how regular-chaotic boundaries formed by marginally unstable periodic orbits or quasiperiodic orbits affect eigenstate localization in mixed phase space.
method: Different piecewise-linear maps are used to model sharply divided phase space, and the overlap index and entropy localization length are computed to quantify eigenstate properties.
result: Eigenstates near the regular-chaotic boundaries exhibit sticky behavior and enhanced localization, with the boundary type influencing the degree of localization.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into quantum chaos in mixed phase space and highlight the role of marginally unstable periodic orbits in shaping eigenstate localization.

title: Kinetic Temperatures And Inertial Effects In A Nonequilibrium Bead-spring Model
authors: Jetin E. Thomas And Ramandeep S. Johal
abstract:
Author(s): Jetin E. Thomas and Ramandeep S. Johal

We investigate a nonequilibrium steady-state model consisting of two coupled beads with arbitrary masses in contact with two thermal baths at different temperatures. Using a covariance-matrix approach together with numerical simulations of the underdamped Langevin dynamics, we characterize steady-st…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034142] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: A classical nonequilibrium bead-spring model with two thermal baths is studied to characterize steady-state kinetic temperatures and inertial effects.
motivation: Understanding nonequilibrium steady states in classical stochastic systems with inertia and temperature gradients remains an important problem in stochastic thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a covariance-matrix approach combined with numerical simulations of underdamped Langevin dynamics.
result: Steady-state kinetic temperatures and inertial effects are characterized for two coupled beads with arbitrary masses.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of coupled classical oscillators, though without direct connection to quantum information or information-theoretic measures.

title: Nonlocal Edge Mode Hybridization In The Long-Range Interacting Kitaev Chain
authors: David Haink, Andreas A. Buchheit, Christof Weitenberg, And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Author(s): David Haink, Andreas A. Buchheit, Christof Weitenberg, and Benedikt Fauseweh

In one-dimensional [MATH]-wave superconductors with short-range interactions, topologically protected Majorana modes emerge, whose mass decays exponentially with system size, as first shown by Kitaev. In this Letter, we extend this prototypical model by including power law long-range interactions withi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146503] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The Letter extends the Kitaev chain to include power-law long-range interactions and analyzes how this hybridization modifies the exponentially localized Majorana edge modes.
motivation: Kitaev's original p-wave superconducting chain predicts topologically protected Majorana zero modes, but real platforms inevitably host long-range interactions whose effect on edge-mode localization is not fully understood.
method: The authors generalize the one-dimensional Kitaev chain by adding power-law long-range couplings and study the resulting edge-mode structure analytically and numerically, focusing on nonlocal hybridization of the boundary Majorana modes.
result: Long-range interactions induce nonlocal hybridization of the edge modes, modifying their exponential mass decay with system size in a way that depends on the interaction range.
conclusion: The findings clarify how realistic long-range terms alter Majorana edge-mode behavior in Kitaev-type platforms, with implications for topological superconducting qubit hardware.

title: Chaotic Many-Body Quantum Dynamics, Spectral Correlations, And Energy Diffusion
authors: J. T. Chalker And Dominik Hahn
abstract:
Author(s): J. T. Chalker and Dominik Hahn

Researchers analyze a solvable many-body model to demonstrate how energy diffusion governs spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031076] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: A solvable many-body model is used to show that energy diffusion quantitatively controls the spectral correlations of chaotic quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding how chaotic many-body quantum dynamics imprints itself on spectral statistics is a central question, and a direct link between hydrodynamic transport (energy diffusion) and spectral correlations had been lacking.
method: The authors analyze a solvable (likely integrable-in-a-limit or Brownian/random-matrix-like) many-body model, computing spectral form factors and correlation functions and connecting them to the diffusive spreading of energy.
result: They demonstrate a quantitative relationship in which the diffusive transport of energy determines the form of spectral correlations, tying hydrodynamic timescales to random-matrix-like spectral behavior.
conclusion: Energy diffusion emerges as a controlling mechanism for spectral correlations in chaotic quantum matter, providing a unified picture connecting thermalization, transport, and spectral statistics.

title: Giant Photon Blockade With Multiple Atoms
authors: Xin Liu, Qing-Hong Liao, Qing-Yue Zhang, And Yong-Chun Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Liu, Qing-Hong Liao, Qing-Yue Zhang, and Yong-Chun Liu

Nonlinearity at the single-photon level is important in both fundamental research and applications of quantum optics. Strong single-photon nonlinearity is usually hard to achieve with a single atom coupled to a cavity mode. Unfortunately, stronger nonlinearity cannot be achieved by coupling more ato…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 143602] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a scheme to achieve giant single-photon blockade nonlinearity by coupling multiple atoms to a cavity mode, overcoming the trade-off that naively adding atoms weakens the effective nonlinearity.
motivation: Strong single-photon nonlinearity (photon blockade) is essential for quantum optics applications but is difficult to obtain with a single atom coupled to a cavity mode, and stronger nonlinearity does not follow from simply coupling more atoms.
method: The authors analyze a cavity-QED system with multiple atoms collectively coupled to a cavity mode, using Tavis-Cummings-type modeling to identify the collective enhancement conditions that boost the photon blockade effect.
result: They demonstrate a giant photon blockade effect where multi-atom coupling yields substantially enhanced single-photon nonlinearity rather than the expected suppression.
conclusion: Collective multi-atom coupling can be exploited to realize strong single-photon nonlinearities, offering a route to improved photon-blockade-based quantum optics devices.

title: Electrically Tunable Orbital Coupling And Quantum Light Emission From O-Band Quantum Dot Molecules
authors: P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, And J. J. Finley
abstract:
Author(s): P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, and J. J. Finley

Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules exhibit electrically tunable orbital coupling, opening a route toward 2D photonic cluster states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033070] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules with electrically tunable orbital coupling are demonstrated as a platform for quantum light emission and a possible route to 2D photonic cluster states.
motivation: Quantum dot molecules offer tunable orbital and spin interactions that could serve as building blocks for scalable photonic quantum technologies, but operating in the telecom O-band with electrical tunability is desirable for integration with existing fiber infrastructure.
method: The authors fabricate and characterize InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules embedded in a diode structure, using applied electric fields to tune inter-dot orbital coupling and measuring their quantum light emission properties.
result: Electrically tunable orbital coupling is observed, alongside quantum light emission in the telecom O-band, indicating a viable platform for generating entangled-photon resources such as 2D photonic cluster states.
conclusion: The work positions O-band quantum dot molecules as a promising solid-state platform for quantum light sources and photonic cluster-state generation, though the demonstration remains a materials/device-level characterization rather than a system-level quantum protocol.

title: Gravity-induced Entanglement Under Constrained Dynamics
authors: Hollis Williams
abstract:
Author(s): Hollis Williams

Tests of gravity-induced entanglement have been proposed as a route to probing the quantum nature of gravity, but existing schemes rely on free-fall interferometry of massive spatial superpositions, imposing severe experimental constraints. We show that systems exhibiting effectively inertial dynami…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032221] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: Proposes gravity-induced entanglement generation via systems with effectively inertial dynamics, offering an alternative to free-fall interferometry for testing quantum gravity.
motivation: Existing tests of gravity-induced entanglement rely on free-fall interferometry with massive spatial superpositions, which impose severe experimental constraints.
method: Theoretically analyzes systems exhibiting effectively inertial dynamics under constrained dynamics to show they can generate gravity-induced entanglement.
result: Demonstrates that such systems can produce gravity-induced entanglement without requiring free-fall interferometry, potentially relaxing experimental requirements.
conclusion: Provides a more feasible route to probe the quantum nature of gravity through entanglement, though practical implementation remains challenging.

title: Topologically Protected State Transfer Beyond Single Excitation And Its Acceleration Via Shortcut To Adiabaticity
authors: Sibo Fang, Biao Xiong, Jin Yang, Hao Zhao, Jibing Liu, And Chuanjia Shan
abstract:
Author(s): Sibo Fang, Biao Xiong, Jin Yang, Hao Zhao, Jibing Liu, and Chuanjia Shan

Topological insulators, owing to their topologically protected boundary states, hold broad application prospects in optical transmission and manipulation. This paper investigates topologically protected quantum state transfer and its acceleration under multiphoton excitation. The results show that u…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043501] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topologically protected quantum state transfer beyond single-excitation, using shortcut-to-adiabaticity to accelerate the transfer.
motivation: Topological protection offers robust quantum state transfer, but prior work mostly addresses single-excitation and slow adiabatic dynamics.
method: The authors likely model a coupled topological system with multiphoton excitations and apply shortcut-to-adiabaticity protocols to speed up the state transfer.
result: They show that topologically protected state transfer remains effective beyond single excitation and can be significantly accelerated without losing protection.
conclusion: Topological state transfer can be extended to multiphoton regimes and accelerated, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Improved Error Correction With Leakage Reduction Units Built Into Qubit Measurement In A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, And Leonardo Dicarlo
abstract:
Author(s): Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, and Leonardo DiCarlo

Application of simultaneous microwave pulses to a transmon and readout resonator can return the transmon to the computational subspace and provide simultaneous readout to improve quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033062] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: This work integrates leakage reduction units into qubit measurement in a superconducting quantum processor to improve error correction.
motivation: Leakage out of the computational subspace degrades quantum error correction in superconducting qubits, so reducing it during measurement is desirable.
method: Simultaneous microwave pulses are applied to a transmon and its readout resonator to return the transmon to the computational subspace while also enabling simultaneous readout.
result: The built-in leakage reduction and simultaneous readout lead to improved quantum error correction performance in the superconducting processor.
conclusion: Leakage reduction units embedded in qubit measurement offer a practical hardware-level route to better error correction in superconducting quantum processors.

title: Generation Of Large Coherent-State Superpositions In Free-Space Optical Pulses
authors: Lucas Caron, Hector Simon, Hugo Basset, Romaric Journet, And Rosa Tualle-Brouri
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Caron, Hector Simon, Hugo Basset, Romaric Journet, and Rosa Tualle-Brouri

Researchers generate large-amplitude optical cat states in free space, establishing a vital building block for fault-tolerant quantum computing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031047] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: Researchers experimentally generate large-amplitude optical coherent-state superpositions (cat states) in free-space pulses, providing a building block for fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing.
motivation: Large coherent-state superpositions are key resources for fault-tolerant optical quantum computing, but generating them with sufficient amplitude in free space remains experimentally challenging.
method: The authors implement a free-space optical setup to produce large-amplitude cat states, though the abstract does not detail the specific nonlinear or conditional measurement technique used.
result: They successfully generate large-amplitude optical cat states in free-space optical pulses, demonstrating a viable route toward fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.
conclusion: This work establishes free-space generation of large coherent-state superpositions as an important enabling technology for photonic fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Entanglement In The Quantum Volunteer's Dilemma
authors: Noah Dane Hebdon And Dax Enshan Koh
abstract:
Author(s): Noah Dane Hebdon and Dax Enshan Koh

A well-known model in game theory, the volunteer's dilemma describes a group of [MATH] players who decide whether to volunteer for a collective benefit at a personal cost or to abstain and risk forfeiting the benefit altogether. A quantum version of this dilemma, developed within the Eisert-Wilkens-Lew…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032460] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper quantizes the volunteer's dilemma and investigates how shared entanglement affects strategic choices and collective outcomes.
motivation: The volunteer's dilemma models costly cooperation in groups, and quantum game theory offers a framework to explore whether entanglement can alter strategic incentives.
method: The authors apply the Eisert-Wilkens-Lewenstein quantization scheme to the volunteer's dilemma, introducing entanglement as a resource and analyzing the resulting game-theoretic equilibria.
result: Entanglement is found to modify players' optimal strategies and payoffs, potentially enabling outcomes that differ from the classical dilemma.
conclusion: Entanglement can serve as a resource to influence cooperation and coordination in quantum versions of social dilemmas, though the implications for broader quantum information theory remain limited.

title: Asymptotically Solvable Quantum Circuits
authors: Samuel H. Pickering And Bruno Bertini
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel H. Pickering and Bruno Bertini

A new family of quantum circuits gives rise to correlations that are chaotic at short scales yet exactly solvable at long scales.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum circuits exhibits chaotic correlations at short scales yet is exactly solvable at long scales.
motivation: Understanding chaotic quantum dynamics and finding analytically tractable models that capture chaos is important for quantum many-body physics.
method: The authors construct and analyze a family of quantum circuits, likely using analytical techniques to obtain exact long-time or long-scale correlation functions while short-scale behavior remains chaotic.
result: They find correlations that are chaotic at short scales but exactly solvable at long scales, providing a tractable model for chaotic quantum dynamics.
conclusion: This family provides a valuable testing ground for theories of quantum chaos and may inform studies in information thermodynamics.

title: Low-Depth Quantum Symmetrization
authors: Zhenning Liu, Andrew M. Childs, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenning Liu, Andrew M. Childs, and Daniel Gottesman

Researchers develop low-depth quantum symmetrization algorithms that enable efficient bosonic simulations, low-depth Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031056] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops low-depth quantum algorithms for symmetrization, enabling efficient bosonic simulations, Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.
motivation: Quantum symmetrization is a fundamental primitive but typically requires costly circuits, motivating resource-efficient low-depth implementations for near-term quantum devices.
