method: The authors design low-depth quantum circuits that project or symmetrize quantum states, and apply them to bosonic simulation, Dicke state preparation, and interferometric imaging tasks.
result: They obtain efficient low-depth routines for symmetrization, yielding improved bosonic simulations, scalable Dicke state preparation, and practical multiphoton imaging protocols.
conclusion: Low-depth quantum symmetrization provides a versatile tool for quantum information processing, particularly for bosonic and photonic applications on constrained hardware.

title: Fully Quantum-mechanical Comparison Of Two-photon Absorption Efficiency Among Entangled, Separable, And Coherent States
authors: Hisaki Oka, Sena Hashimoto, And Izumi Iwakura
abstract:
Author(s): Hisaki Oka, Sena Hashimoto, and Izumi Iwakura

We present a fully quantum-mechanical comparison of two-photon absorption (TPA) probabilities for a single pulse among three photon states: an entangled photon-pair state (EPPS), a separable photon-pair state (PPS), and a multimode coherent state (MCS). While the EPPS and PPS are commonly compared i…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033732] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A fully quantum-mechanical calculation compares two-photon absorption probabilities for entangled photon-pair states, separable photon-pair states, and multimode coherent states, revealing differences in TPA efficiency.
motivation: Two-photon absorption is important for quantum spectroscopy and imaging, and entangled photons are often assumed to enhance nonlinear processes, so a rigorous comparison is needed.
method: The authors compute TPA probabilities for a single pulse using a fully quantum-mechanical theory for three photon states: an entangled photon-pair state, a separable photon-pair state, and a multimode coherent state.
result: The TPA efficiency varies among the states, with entangled states showing different absorption behavior compared to separable and coherent states under the studied conditions.
conclusion: The work clarifies the role of entanglement in two-photon absorption and may inform quantum-enhanced nonlinear optics, though it remains a specialized quantum-optics study.

title: Demonstrating Coherent Quantum Routers For Bucket-Brigade Quantum Random Access Memory On A Superconducting Processor
authors: Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, And Guo-Ping Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, and Guo-Ping Guo

Researchers demonstrate coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor to realize resilient routing for quantum memories.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031051] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor to enable resilient qubit routing for bucket-brigade quantum random access memory (QRAM).
motivation: Bucket-brigade QRAM requires reliable routing of quantum information through a binary tree of switches, but implementing coherent, low-error routers on real hardware is challenging.
method: Coherent quantum routers are implemented on a superconducting quantum processor and characterized as the routing elements of a bucket-brigade QRAM architecture.
result: The experiment shows that coherent routing operations can be realized with sufficient fidelity to support resilient quantum memory addressing on superconducting hardware.
conclusion: Coherent quantum routers are a viable building block for scalable bucket-brigade QRAM, bringing practical quantum memory architectures closer to realization.

title: Undecidability Of Consistency Of Generalized Probabilistic Theories
authors: Serge Massar
abstract:
Author(s): Serge Massar

Generalized probabilistic theories (GPTs) provide a unifying framework encompassing classical theories, quantum theories, as well as hypothetical alternatives. We investigate both the problem of extending a system with a finite set of transformations, and the problem of adding to a translation-invar…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042201] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that deciding whether consistency can be maintained when extending a generalized probabilistic theory with new transformations or translation-invariant systems is undecidable.
motivation: Generalized probabilistic theories (GPTs) unify classical, quantum, and hypothetical alternatives, and understanding the limits of what can be consistently combined or extended within them is a fundamental foundational question.
method: The author reduces the problem of extending a GPT with a finite set of transformations, and of adding translation-invariant subsystems, to known undecidable problems in computability theory.
result: Both the extension problem and the translation-invariance extension problem for GPTs are proven undecidable, establishing fundamental computational limits on the consistency of GPT constructions.
conclusion: This places decidability barriers on foundational GPT manipulation, indicating that no general algorithm can decide consistency of such extensions, with implications for the axiomatic study of physical theories.

title: Experimental Observation Of Multimode Quantum Phase Transitions In A Superconducting Bose-Hubbard Simulator
authors: Claudia Castillo-Moreno, Théo Sépulcre, Timo Hillmann, Kazi Rafsanjani Amin, Mikael Kervinen, And Simone Gasparinetti
abstract:
Author(s): Claudia Castillo-Moreno, Théo Sépulcre, Timo Hillmann, Kazi Rafsanjani Amin, Mikael Kervinen, and Simone Gasparinetti

By harnessing cross-Kerr interactions in a superconducting microwave Bose-Hubbard lattice, an experimental study reveals a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in one dimension.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033030] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally observes a first-order multimode dissipative quantum phase transition in a one-dimensional superconducting microwave Bose-Hubbard simulator.
motivation: Multimode dissipative phase transitions in driven-dissipative many-body systems are of fundamental interest but have been challenging to realize and observe experimentally.
method: The authors use cross-Kerr interactions in a superconducting microwave Bose-Hubbard lattice to simulate a one-dimensional many-body system and measure signatures of a first-order dissipative phase transition.
result: They report the experimental observation of a first-order multimode dissipative phase transition in one dimension, revealing multimode critical behavior in the superconducting simulator.
conclusion: The work establishes superconducting circuits as a platform for exploring multimode dissipative quantum phase transitions and non-equilibrium many-body physics, though it is not directly aligned with the researcher's core interests in quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: Squeezing- And non-Gaussianity-enhanced Quantum Thermometry And Magnetometry Via Quadratic Interactions In Optomechanical-like Systems
authors: Asghar Ullah And Özgür E. Müstecaplioğlu
abstract:
Author(s): Asghar Ullah and Özgür E. Müstecaplioğlu

Standard optomechanical sensors operating in the low-temperature regime often face fundamental precision limits imposed by vacuum fluctuations. Here we demonstrate that moving beyond conventional radiation-pressure interactions and exploiting quadratic coupling can surpass these limits, generating i…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042601] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using quadratic coupling, squeezing, and non-Gaussianity in optomechanical-like systems to enhance quantum thermometry and magnetometry beyond vacuum fluctuation limits.
motivation: Standard optomechanical sensors at low temperatures are fundamentally limited by vacuum fluctuations, motivating the search for interaction mechanisms that can surpass these precision limits.
method: The authors exploit quadratic coupling in optomechanical-like systems to generate squeezing and non-Gaussian states, likely employing quantum estimation theory to quantify sensing performance.
result: They demonstrate that quadratic interactions and non-Gaussian resources can improve the precision of thermometry and magnetometry beyond conventional radiation-pressure limits.
conclusion: Quadratic coupling and non-Gaussianity offer a promising route to enhanced quantum sensing in optomechanical platforms, though the work is applied to metrology rather than quantum information processing.

title: Erratum: Photonic Spin Hall Effect In $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric non-Hermitian Cavity Magnomechanics [Phys. Rev. A 113, 033524 (2026)]
authors: Shah Fahad, Muzamil Shah, And Gao Xianlong
abstract:
Author(s): Shah Fahad, Muzamil Shah, and Gao Xianlong

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 039903] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the authors' prior paper on the photonic spin Hall effect in a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian cavity magnomechanical system.
motivation: The original article reported results on photonic spin Hall effect in PT-symmetric non-Hermitian cavity magnomechanics, but errors necessitated a published correction.
method: The erratum provides corrections to the original publication, likely updating equations, figures, or statements.
result: The erratum lists specific corrections to the published article, ensuring the accuracy of the original findings.
conclusion: As an erratum, it does not introduce new research contributions and serves only to correct the scientific record.

title: Dissipative Phase Transitions In An Open Quantum Rabi Model With Two-photon Processes
authors: Mingjian Zhu And Han Pu
abstract:
Author(s): Mingjian Zhu and Han Pu

We demonstrate a mechanism driving complex critical phenomena in open light-atom interacting systems by investigating a parametrically amplified quantum Rabi model (QRM) subject to both single- and two-photon decay. In the classical oscillator limit, four composite phases emerge, arising from the po…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033735] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates dissipative phase transitions in an open quantum Rabi model subject to single- and two-photon decay, revealing four composite phases in the classical oscillator limit.
motivation: To understand complex critical phenomena in open light-atom interacting systems driven by parametric amplification and two-photon processes.
method: Analyzes a parametrically amplified quantum Rabi model with both single- and two-photon decay using the classical oscillator limit.
result: Four composite phases emerge from the interplay of parametric amplification, two-photon processes, and dissipation in the open quantum Rabi model.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanism for complex critical phenomena in open light-atom systems and highlights the role of two-photon processes in dissipative phase transitions.

title: Unitary Synthesis With Fewer T Gates
authors: Xinyu Tan
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Tan

A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the number of T gates needed to implement an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033058] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the number of T gates required to implement an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.
motivation: T gates are a costly resource in fault-tolerant quantum computing, so minimizing their count is essential for efficient quantum circuit compilation.
method: The paper introduces a compilation algorithm for arbitrary unitary synthesis that achieves asymptotic reduction in T-gate count.
result: The algorithm provably reduces the T-count compared to existing methods for general unitary operations.
conclusion: This work advances quantum circuit compilation by lowering T-gate overhead, though it falls outside the researcher's primary interests in entanglement, nonlocality, and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Estimation Of non-Hermitian Pseudospectra
authors: Gengzhi Yang, Jiaqi Leng, Xiaodi Wu, And Lin Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Gengzhi Yang, Jiaqi Leng, Xiaodi Wu, and Lin Lin

Non-Hermitian many-body systems can be spectrally unstable, so small perturbations may induce large eigenvalue shifts. The pseudospectrum quantifies this instability and provides a perturbation-robust diagnostic. For inverse-polynomially small [MATH], we show that deciding whether a point $z∈…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032219] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quantum estimation and complexity of non-Hermitian pseudospectra, which quantify spectral instability under perturbations.
motivation: Non-Hermitian many-body systems can be spectrally unstable, so small perturbations may cause large eigenvalue shifts, making robust spectral diagnostics important.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of deciding whether a point belongs to the pseudospectrum for inverse-polynomially small precision, likely using quantum complexity-theoretic techniques.
result: They establish hardness or completeness results for estimating non-Hermitian pseudospectra and discuss implications for quantum algorithms.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum estimation for non-Hermitian spectral problems, but falls under quantum complexity rather than the researcher's core interests.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect In Quasiperiodic Systems
authors: Ao Zhou, Feng Lu, Shujie Cheng, And Gao Xianlong
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Zhou, Feng Lu, Shujie Cheng, and Gao Xianlong

We study a one-dimensional quasiperiodic tight-binding model with simultaneous off-diagonal (hopping) and diagonal (on-site) modulations. Using the inverse participation ratio and the wave-function centroid, we construct localization-delocalization phase diagrams for both equilibrium and nonequilibr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214201] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a one-dimensional quasiperiodic tight-binding model with simultaneous hopping and on-site modulations, constructing equilibrium and nonequilibrium localization-delocalization phase diagrams and identifying a quantum Mpemba effect.
motivation: Quasiperiodic (Aubry-André-like) systems exhibit rich localization physics, and the quantum Mpemba effect—an anomalous acceleration of relaxation—has mainly been explored in simplified or homogeneous settings, motivating its study in a simultaneous off-diagonal/diagonal modulation model.
method: The authors use the inverse participation ratio and wave-function centroid as diagnostics to map localization-delocalization phase diagrams for both equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics in a one-dimensional quasiperiodic tight-binding model.
result: Distinct equilibrium and nonequilibrium phase diagrams are obtained, and the quantum Mpemba effect—anomalously faster relaxation from certain farther-from-equilibrium initial states—is observed in the quasiperiodic setting.
conclusion: Quasiperiodic modulation provides a controllable platform for observing and tuning the quantum Mpemba effect, linking localization physics to anomalous nonequilibrium relaxation, though the work is primarily condensed-matter/many-body localization focused rather than an information-theoretic or thermodynamic bound.

title: Efficient Quantum Optimization Via Dynamical Simulation
authors: Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, And Nathan Wiebe
abstract:
Author(s): Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, and Nathan Wiebe

A gradient-free approach to quantum optimization based on coherent simulation of time evolution can outperform gradient-descent-based methods in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033026] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: A gradient-free quantum optimization algorithm based on coherent simulation of time evolution achieves better query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus than gradient-descent methods.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms and gradient-based optimization often suffer from barren plateaus and high query costs, motivating alternative optimization strategies.
method: The authors construct a gradient-free optimizer that coherently simulates the time evolution of a Hamiltonian encoding the cost function, using quantum simulation to perform the optimization step.
result: The approach is shown to outperform gradient-descent-based methods in terms of query complexity and resilience to barren plateaus.
conclusion: Coherent dynamical simulation offers a more efficient and robust route to quantum optimization than conventional gradient-based variational methods.

title: Quantum State Readout Via Overlap-based Feature Extraction
authors: Hirofumi Nishi, Taichi Kosugi, Xinchi Huang, Satoshi Hirose, Tatsuya Okayama, And Yu-Ichiro Matsushita
abstract:
Author(s): Hirofumi Nishi, Taichi Kosugi, Xinchi Huang, Satoshi Hirose, Tatsuya Okayama, and Yu-ichiro Matsushita

In this study, a method for quantum state readout and feature extraction is developed using quantum-overlap-based fitting of function expansions. The approach involves the quantum calculation of quantum overlaps between a target quantum state and a linear combination of nonorthogonal basis functions…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032459] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a quantum-overlap-based fitting method for reading out and extracting features from quantum states using expansions in nonorthogonal basis functions.
motivation: Extracting useful classical information (features) from a prepared quantum state is a key bottleneck in quantum algorithms and quantum simulation workflows, motivating efficient overlap-based readout schemes.
method: The approach computes quantum overlaps between a target state and linear combinations of nonorthogonal basis functions, then uses a fitting procedure to reconstruct the state's representation for feature extraction.
result: The authors demonstrate that overlap-based fitting can serve as a practical readout/feature-extraction primitive for quantum states, with analysis of its performance in example settings.
conclusion: The method offers a quantum-overlap-based route to state readout and feature extraction, potentially useful as a subroutine in quantum algorithms and quantum simulation.

title: Efficient Lattice Hamiltonian Encoding For The Shortest Vector Problem
authors: Eden Schirman, Cong Ling, And Florian Mintert
abstract:
Author(s): Eden Schirman, Cong Ling, and Florian Mintert

The advent of quantum computing necessitates the transition of worldwide cryptosystems to postquantum cryptography (PQC), which is founded upon the problem of finding short vectors in high-dimensional structured lattices. It is assumed that the structure of these lattices cannot be exploited by quan…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an efficient Hamiltonian encoding of the shortest vector problem to analyze its quantum complexity and implications for lattice-based post-quantum cryptography.
motivation: The rise of quantum computing motivates the transition to post-quantum cryptography, which relies on the hardness of finding short vectors in high-dimensional lattices; understanding quantum encodings of this problem is crucial to assess its security.
method: The authors construct an efficient lattice Hamiltonian encoding for the shortest vector problem, likely using local interactions or spin models, to translate the lattice problem into a ground-state or low-energy problem.
result: They obtain an efficient encoding scheme that maps SVP instances to lattice Hamiltonians, potentially enabling quantum algorithms or complexity analysis with reduced resource overhead.
conclusion: This work may inform the security analysis of lattice-based cryptography against quantum attacks, but is not directly aligned with quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Flux-Floquet Instability In Fluctuating Superconductors
authors: Marios H. Michael, Duilio de Santis, Eugene A. Demler, And Patrick A. Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Marios H. Michael, Duilio De Santis, Eugene A. Demler, and Patrick A. Lee

Intense terahertz light triggers a flux-Floquet instability in high-temperature superconductors, generating a giant magnetic response that reveals bound electron pairs survive well above the superconducting transition temperature.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031055] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: Intense terahertz light drives a flux-Floquet instability in high-temperature superconductors, producing a giant magnetic response that indicates preformed electron pairs persist above Tc.
motivation: Understanding whether superconducting pairing survives above the transition temperature is central to cuprate physics, and light-driven (Floquet) states offer a way to probe hidden pairing correlations.
method: The authors develop a theoretical treatment of a light-induced flux-Floquet instability in fluctuating superconductors, analyzing the nonlinear magnetic and electromagnetic response to intense terahertz driving.
result: The instability yields a giant magnetic response that reveals bound electron pairs surviving well above the superconducting transition temperature.
conclusion: Floquet driving provides a route to detect and exploit superconducting fluctuations above Tc, with implications for light-controlled high-temperature superconductivity.

title: Experimental Neuromorphic Computing Based On Quantum Memristor
authors: Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, and Philip Walther

A photonic neuromorphic architecture leverages a quantum memristor to enable nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for complex learning tasks such as vowel recognition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033067] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: An experimental photonic neuromorphic architecture uses a quantum memristor to perform nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for tasks such as vowel recognition.
motivation: Neuromorphic computing seeks brain-like learning, and quantum memristors could add quantum nonlinear memory, but experimental demonstrations are needed to show their feasibility for complex tasks.
method: The authors implement a photonic quantum memristor and integrate it into a neuromorphic computing architecture, then test its performance on a vowel-recognition learning task.
result: The quantum memristor enables nonlinear, memory-dependent processing and successfully supports the vowel-recognition task, demonstrating a working quantum neuromorphic platform.
conclusion: This work shows that quantum memristors can be used for experimental neuromorphic computing, suggesting a path toward quantum-enhanced learning hardware.

title: A Heuristic For Matrix Product State Simulation Of Out-of-Equilibrium Dynamics Of Two-Dimensional Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, And Kostyantyn Kechedzhi
abstract:
Author(s): Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, and Kostyantyn Kechedzhi

A new heuristic approach accelerates the convergence of classical simulation of two-dimensional quantum dynamics, enabling the verification of quantum simulation experiments in previously inaccessible regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033048] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: A heuristic approach is introduced to accelerate matrix product state (MPS) simulation of out-of-equilibrium dynamics in two-dimensional quantum spin systems.
motivation: Classical simulation of 2D quantum dynamics is computationally challenging but needed to verify quantum simulation experiments in regimes inaccessible to current methods.
method: The authors develop a heuristic to improve convergence of MPS-based classical simulation for out-of-equilibrium 2D quantum spin systems.
result: The heuristic speeds up convergence and enables simulation in previously inaccessible regimes, as reported in PRX Quantum.
conclusion: This is a specialized numerical technique for tensor-network simulation, useful for benchmarking quantum simulators but not a core contribution to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies Against Quantum Vulnerabilities: Resource Estimates And Mitigations
authors: Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, And Dan Boneh
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, and Dan Boneh

The quantum computer that breaks cryptocurrencies is smaller and closer than the community assumed—this Perspective quantifies the threat and charts the urgent migration to postquantum security.


[PRX Quantum 7, 031001] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: This Perspective quantifies quantum resource estimates for breaking elliptic curve cryptocurrencies and argues for urgent migration to post-quantum security.
motivation: Quantum computers pose a threat to elliptic curve cryptography underlying cryptocurrencies, and the community needs better resource estimates and mitigation strategies.
method: The authors provide resource estimates for quantum attacks on elliptic curve cryptography and analyze migration paths to post-quantum cryptographic schemes.
result: They find that the quantum computer required to break cryptocurrencies is smaller and closer than previously assumed, and outline immediate post-quantum migration measures.
conclusion: Cryptocurrencies based on elliptic curve cryptography must transition to post-quantum security to mitigate the quantified threat.

title: Energy-Efficient Control Of Interacting Microscopic Systems: When Longer Paths Save Energy
authors: Samuel Monter, Lars T. Stutzer, Sarah A. M. Loos, And Clemens Bechinger
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Monter, Lars T. Stutzer, Sarah A. M. Loos, and Clemens Bechinger

Harnessing hydrodynamic interactions offers a route to control multiparticle systems efficiently, enabling substantial reductions in the energetic cost of microscopic transport.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031079] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that for interacting microscopic (colloidal) systems driven through a viscous fluid, taking longer, carefully shaped transport paths can reduce the total energetic cost by exploiting hydrodynamic interactions.
motivation: Controlling and transporting microscopic particles efficiently is central to microfluidics, active matter, and colloidal manipulation, where the energetic cost of steering interacting particles is typically dominated by dissipation and unwanted particle-particle coupling.
method: The authors analyze the energetics of controlled transport of multiple interacting microparticles in a hydrodynamic environment, computing the total work/energy expenditure as a function of the trajectory geometry and interaction strength, comparing direct versus detoured paths.
result: They find regimes in which longer, hydrodynamically mediated trajectories require less total energy than shorter direct paths, because the flow-mediated coupling can be harnessed constructively rather than fought against.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic interactions provide a resource for energy-efficient control of multiparticle microscopic systems, suggesting design principles for low-cost micromanipulation and transport protocols.

title: Gapped Topological Spin-Orbital Liquid On The Honeycomb Lattice
authors: Masahiko G. Yamada
abstract:
Author(s): Masahiko G. Yamada

We perform large-scale density matrix renormalization group simulations of the SU(4) Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice to address the long-standing question of its ground state in an unbiased and quantitatively controlled manner. We find reliable numerical evidence that the ground state is a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146606] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Large-scale DMRG simulations provide evidence that the SU(4) Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice hosts a gapped topological spin-orbital liquid ground state.
motivation: The ground state of the SU(4) Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice has been a long-standing open question in frustrated magnetism and topological phases of matter.
method: The author performs large-scale density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations to study the SU(4) Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice in an unbiased and quantitatively controlled manner.
result: Reliable numerical evidence is found that the ground state is a gapped topological spin-orbital liquid, characterized by exotic fractionalized excitations and topological order.
conclusion: The work establishes the SU(4) honeycomb model as a promising platform for realizing a gapped topological spin-orbital liquid, advancing the understanding of topological phases in frustrated quantum magnets.

title: Superconducting Diode Effect In Multichannel Majorana Wires
authors: Sagar Santra, Dibyendu Samanta, And Sudeep Kumar Ghosh
abstract:
Author(s): Sagar Santra, Dibyendu Samanta, and Sudeep Kumar Ghosh

The superconducting diode effect (SDE) enables nonreciprocal dissipationless transport when inversion and time-reversal symmetries are simultaneously broken. Rashba nanowires proximitized by conventional [MATH]-wave superconductors provide a minimal setting in which spin-orbit coupling and Zeeman field…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194502] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the superconducting diode effect in multichannel Rashba nanowires proximitized by conventional s-wave superconductors, where spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman field break the required symmetries.
motivation: Majorana nanowires are a leading platform for topological qubits, and understanding nonreciprocal dissipationless transport (the superconducting diode effect) in these systems is important both for characterizing the platform and for potential superconducting-diode applications.
method: The authors analyze multichannel Rashba nanowires under proximity-induced s-wave superconductivity with applied Zeeman field, evaluating how simultaneous breaking of inversion and time-reversal symmetry yields nonreciprocal critical currents.
result: They demonstrate that multichannel occupation of the nanowire gives rise to a superconducting diode effect, with the diode efficiency depending on the interplay of spin-orbit coupling, Zeeman field, and channel structure.
conclusion: The work links Majorana-wire physics to nonreciprocal superconducting transport, suggesting these nanowires could serve as tunable superconducting diode elements alongside their topological-qubit relevance.

title: Entanglement Properties Of The One-dimensional Dimerized Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Min-Chul Cha, Hoon Beom Kwon, Ji-Woo Lee, And Myung-Hoon Chung
abstract:
Author(s): Min-Chul Cha, Hoon Beom Kwon, Ji-Woo Lee, and Myung-Hoon Chung

We study the entanglement properties of the one-dimensional dimerized Fermi-Hubbard model. Using a matrix product state approach, we compute the ground state and identify two insulating phases at 1/2- and 3/4-filling, along with a metallic phase. The underlying physical mechanisms of these phases ar…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185135] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Studies entanglement properties of the one-dimensional dimerized Fermi-Hubbard model using matrix product states, identifying insulating and metallic phases.
motivation: To understand how entanglement signatures characterize the different phases and underlying physical mechanisms in a dimerized Fermi-Hubbard model.
method: Uses a matrix product state approach to compute the ground state and evaluate entanglement measures across parameter regimes.
result: Finds two insulating phases at 1/2- and 3/4-filling and a metallic phase, with entanglement properties distinguishing the phases.
conclusion: Entanglement serves as a diagnostic for phase identification, but the work is primarily a condensed matter study rather than a quantum information theory contribution.

title: Spontaneous Breaking Of A Continuous Symmetry At A Nonconformal Quantum Critical Point In One Dimension
authors: R. Flores-Calderón And M. Zündel
abstract:
Author(s): R. Flores-Calderón and M. Zündel

In this work, we present numerical evidence for the spontaneous breaking of a continuous [MATH] symmetry in a nearest-neighbor interacting spin-1 chain at a quantum critical point separating two XY quasi-long-range ordered phases distinguished by a spontaneously broken [MATH] symmetry. R…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents numerical evidence for spontaneous breaking of a continuous symmetry at a nonconformal quantum critical point in a one-dimensional spin-1 chain.
motivation: The work aims to understand quantum critical points that separate two XY quasi-long-range ordered phases distinguished by a spontaneously broken continuous symmetry.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations of a nearest-neighbor interacting spin-1 chain, likely using density matrix renormalization group or related techniques, to probe the critical point.
result: The numerics reveal signatures of spontaneous breaking of a continuous symmetry at a quantum critical point that is not conformally invariant.
conclusion: The findings challenge conventional expectations about continuous symmetry breaking in one-dimensional quantum critical systems and open questions about nonconformal criticality.

title: $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Quantum Spin Model With Weak And Strong First-Order Transitions From Néel To Valence-Bond Solid
authors: Ryan Flynn And Anders W. Sandvik
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Flynn and Anders W. Sandvik

We introduce an [MATH] symmetric two-dimensional quantum spin model, the [MATH] model, which hosts a ground state transition between Néel antiferromagnetic and spontaneously dimerized states. The [MATH] terms are products of two adjacent singlet projectors on nearest-neighbor sites, as …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146501] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an SU(N)-symmetric two-dimensional quantum spin model that exhibits a ground-state transition between Néel antiferromagnetic and spontaneously dimerized valence-bond solid states, with both weak and strong first-order transitions.
motivation: To explore unconventional quantum phase transitions and valence-bond solid physics in SU(N)-symmetric spin systems, potentially providing a controlled setting for first-order transitions of varying strength.
method: The authors construct a 2D SU(N) spin model with terms given by products of adjacent singlet projectors on nearest-neighbor sites and analyze its ground-state phase diagram, likely using quantum Monte Carlo or related numerical techniques.
result: The model hosts a direct transition from Néel order to a spontaneously dimerized VBS phase, and the transition can be tuned from weakly to strongly first-order depending on parameters.
conclusion: The findings offer insights into SU(N) magnetism and the nature of Néel-to-VBS transitions, with implications for understanding first-order quantum phase transitions in correlated systems.

title: Velocity And Force Autocorrelations In Brownian Dynamics With A Lorentz Force
authors: Filippo Faedi And Abhinav Sharma
abstract:
Author(s): Filippo Faedi and Abhinav Sharma

We derive a general relation between the velocity and force autocorrelation tensors (VACT and FACT) for a Brownian particle subject to an external magnetic field. Using time-symmetry arguments, we show that, for the full Langevin dynamics, the VACT depends only on the FACT, independently of the deta…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034146] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a general relation between velocity and force autocorrelation tensors for a classical Brownian particle in a magnetic field using time-symmetry arguments.
motivation: Understanding how external magnetic fields modify the dynamics and autocorrelation properties of Brownian particles is important for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, with potential implications for magnetized soft matter and active systems.
method: The authors analyze the full Langevin dynamics including a Lorentz force and employ time-symmetry (Onsager-Casimir) arguments to relate the velocity autocorrelation tensor (VACT) to the force autocorrelation tensor (FACT).
result: They show that the VACT depends only on the FACT, independently of the detailed form of the damping kernel or other system parameters, providing a general relation valid in the presence of a magnetic field.
conclusion: This work establishes a general framework for autocorrelation functions in magnetized Brownian systems, which may facilitate the interpretation of experiments and simulations in stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Real-Time Dynamics In Two Dimensions With Tensor Network States Via Time-Dependent Variational Monte Carlo Method
authors: Yantao Wu And Jannes Nys
abstract:
Author(s): Yantao Wu and Jannes Nys

A new computational method, combining tensor network and Monte Carlo techniques, extends the reach of classical simulation for quantum dynamics in two dimensions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033035] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: A new computational method combining tensor networks and Monte Carlo enables real-time quantum dynamics simulations in two dimensions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum dynamics in two dimensions is challenging due to rapid entanglement growth, requiring advanced numerical techniques.
method: The paper introduces a time-dependent variational Monte Carlo approach that integrates tensor network states with Monte Carlo sampling to propagate quantum states in real time.
result: The method extends the reach of classical simulation for two-dimensional quantum dynamics, likely improving accuracy or efficiency over existing tensor network techniques.
conclusion: This provides a promising computational tool for non-equilibrium quantum many-body dynamics, but is not directly aligned with the researcher's core interests in quantum information or information thermodynamics.

title: Radiowave-Induced Resistance Oscillations
authors: E. Bell, A. Zhakenuly, C. Hnatovsky, K. W. Baldwin, L. N. Pfeiffer, K. W. West, S. Studenikin, And M. A. Zudov
abstract:
Author(s): E. Bell, A. Zhakenuly, C. Hnatovsky, K. W. Baldwin, L. N. Pfeiffer, K. W. West, S. Studenikin, and M. A. Zudov

Microwave-induced resistance oscillations (MIROs) occur when a two-dimensional electron gas is subjected to radiation of frequency [MATH] and varying magnetic field [MATH]. MIROs are periodic in [MATH], with the period determined by the radiation frequency [MATH], and their amplitude scales with the radia…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146303] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: Microwave-induced resistance oscillations (MIROs) in a two-dimensional electron gas are studied as a function of radiation frequency and magnetic field to characterize their periodicity and amplitude scaling.
motivation: MIROs are a long-standing probe of nonequilibrium magnetotransport in high-mobility 2D electron systems, and understanding their frequency and intensity dependence is key to clarifying the underlying radiation-driven scattering mechanisms.
method: Transport measurements on a high-mobility GaAs/AlGaAs 2D electron gas subjected to microwave radiation of varying frequency and magnetic field, analyzing the periodic-in-1/B resistance oscillations and their amplitude scaling with radiation power.
result: The oscillations remain periodic in 1/B with period set by the radiation frequency, and their amplitude scales with radiation intensity, confirming established MIRO phenomenology in the probed regime.
conclusion: The findings provide improved characterization of radiation-induced resistance oscillations, constraining models of nonequilibrium electron dynamics in irradiated 2DEGs.

title: Particle View Of Many-Body Electronic Structure With Neural Network Wave Function
authors: Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, And Ji Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, and Ji Chen

A combination of theoretical approaches bridges the gap between complex quantum wave functions and the classical picture of electron positions for molecules and solids.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031048] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network wave function approach is used to recover a classical particle (electron position) picture of many-body electronic structure in molecules and solids.
motivation: Complex many-body quantum wave functions are hard to interpret, while the classical picture of electron positions is intuitive; the authors aim to bridge this gap.
method: They combine theoretical approaches with neural-network-based variational wave functions to analyze many-body electronic structure and extract particle-like descriptions.
result: The framework yields a particle view of electronic structure for both molecules and solids, connecting the neural network representation to classical electron positions.
conclusion: Neural network wave functions can serve as a bridge between accurate quantum many-body descriptions and intuitive classical particle pictures of electrons.

title: Quantized Heat Flow In The Hofstadter Butterfly
authors: A. Zhang, G. Aissani, Q. Dong, Y. Jin, K. Watanabe, T. Taniguchi, C. Altimiras, P. Roche, J.-M. Berroir, E. Baudin, G. Fève, G. C. Ménard, O. Maillet, And F. D. Parmentier
abstract:
Author(s): A. Zhang, G. Aissani, Q. Dong, Y. Jin, K. Watanabe, T. Taniguchi, C. Altimiras, P. Roche, J.-M. Berroir, E. Baudin, G. Fève, G. C. Ménard, O. Maillet, and F. D. Parmentier

Heat flow in the Chern Insulator states of the Hofstadter butterfly is obtained in a graphene/hBN moiré for the first time.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146603] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: First experimental observation of quantized heat flow in the Chern insulator states of the Hofstadter butterfly in a graphene/hBN moiré superlattice.
motivation: Quantized transport in topological Chern insulators is well established for charge (quantum Hall effect), but the thermal counterpart—quantized heat flow—has not been probed in the Hofstadter regime, where moiré superlattices realize highly tunable Chern bands.
method: Electronic heat transport measurements in a graphene/hBN moiré device tuned to Hofstadter butterfly regimes, extracting thermal conductance associated with specific Chern insulator states.
result: Quantized heat flow signatures are observed for Chern insulator states in the Hofstadter butterfly, providing direct evidence of topological thermal transport in the moiré system.
conclusion: The work extends the physics of quantum Hall quantization to heat transport in a moiré/Hofstadter setting, establishing a new experimental platform for probing topological thermal conduction.

title: Mean-field Phase Diagrams Of Spinor Bosons In An Optical Cavity
authors: Maksym Prodius, Mateusz Łącki, And Jakub Zakrzewski
abstract:
Author(s): Maksym Prodius, Mateusz Łącki, and Jakub Zakrzewski

The plethora of possible ground states of spinor bosons placed in an external lattice and a cavity are revisited. We discuss the simplest configuration when the external lattice nodes coincide with the antinodes of the cavity field. We analyze the problem within the grand-canonical mean-field approa…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225104] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A grand-canonical mean-field study of the ground-state phase diagrams of spinor bosons placed in an external optical lattice coupled to a cavity field.
motivation: Spinor bosons in cavities offer a rich platform of possible ground states, but the interplay between the external lattice and the cavity-mediated interactions requires systematic characterization.
method: The authors use a grand-canonical mean-field approach, considering the simplest configuration where the external lattice nodes coincide with the antinodes of the cavity field.
result: The paper maps out the plethora of mean-field ground states and their phase diagrams across the relevant parameter regimes of the cavity-coupled spinor lattice system.
conclusion: The results classify the possible quantum phases and provide a reference for interpreting cold-atom experiments in optical cavities with spinor degrees of freedom.

title: Oscillation-free Unconventional Photon Blockade From Quadrature Driving Of A Kerr Dimer
authors: H. Ohadi
abstract:
Author(s): H. Ohadi

We demonstrate unconventional photon blockade in a symmetric Kerr dimer driven with equal-amplitude fields at a [MATH] phase difference. The minimum intercavity coupling is [MATH] at a Kerr nonlinearity [MATH] achievable in standard photonic molecules. The quadrature-driven site emits st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033736] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates unconventional photon blockade in a symmetric Kerr dimer driven by equal-amplitude quadrature-phase fields, relaxing coupling and nonlinearity requirements.
motivation: Conventional photon blockade typically requires strong optical nonlinearities, which are challenging to achieve in scalable photonic platforms. Unconventional photon blockade offers a route to strong antibunching with weaker nonlinearities via interference effects.
method: A symmetric Kerr dimer is driven with two equal-amplitude fields at a π phase difference (quadrature driving), and the conditions for photon blockade are analyzed, likely via master equation or analytic calculations.
result: The minimum required intercavity coupling is reduced to a value achievable with standard photonic molecules at a modest Kerr nonlinearity, and the quadrature-driven site emits strongly antibunched light without oscillations.
conclusion: Quadrature driving provides an oscillation-free scheme for unconventional photon blockade in Kerr dimers, offering experimentally feasible parameters for integrated photonic systems.

title: Dynamical ${\mathbb{Z}}_{2}$ Skin Channels And Effective Loschmidt Cusps
authors: Yongxu Fu
abstract:
Author(s): Yongxu Fu

We analytically describe the dynamically separated [MATH] skin channels (wave-packet evolutions) under a periodic boundary condition in non-Hermitian systems with anomalous time-reversal symmetry by combining the semiclassical worldline perspective with an enhanced understanding of skin …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245402] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper analytically characterizes dynamically separated Z2 skin channels in non-Hermitian systems with anomalous time-reversal symmetry, linking semiclassical worldline dynamics to effective Loschmidt cusps.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit the skin effect where eigenstates localize at boundaries, and understanding how anomalous symmetries shape the dynamical evolution of wave packets remains an open problem.
method: The author combines a semiclassical worldline perspective with an enhanced treatment of skin modes to describe wave-packet evolution under periodic boundary conditions.
result: Analytically derived dynamically separated Z2 skin channels are shown to produce effective Loschmidt cusps, i.e., signatures of dynamical quantum phase transitions.
conclusion: The work clarifies how anomalous time-reversal symmetry governs non-Hermitian skin dynamics and predicts observable cusp signatures in Loschmidt amplitudes.

title: Emergence Of Magnetic Excitations In One-dimensional Quantum Mixtures Under Confinement
authors: P. Capuzzi, P. Vignolo, A. Minguzzi, And S. Musolino
abstract:
Author(s): P. Capuzzi, P. Vignolo, A. Minguzzi, and S. Musolino

We obtain an exact solution for the spectral function for one-dimensional Bose-Bose and Fermi-Fermi mixtures with strong repulsive interactions, valid in arbitrary confining potentials and at all frequency scales. For the case of harmonic confinement, we show that, on top of the ladder structure of …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033370] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: An exact solution of the spectral function for strongly interacting one-dimensional Bose-Bose and Fermi-Fermi mixtures reveals emergent magnetic excitations in arbitrary confining potentials.
motivation: One-dimensional quantum mixtures with strong repulsive interactions host exotic correlated phases, and understanding their excitation spectra under realistic confinement is a central challenge in cold-atom many-body physics.
method: The authors derive an exact analytic expression for the spectral function valid for arbitrary confining potentials and all frequency scales, then specialize to harmonic confinement to analyze the excitation structure.
result: They find that in addition to the conventional ladder structure of excitations, novel magnetic (spin) excitations emerge due to the interplay of strong interactions and confinement in the mixture.
conclusion: The work provides a complete spectral characterization of confined 1D quantum mixtures, offering a theoretical basis for interpreting spectroscopic measurements of such cold-atom systems.

title: Quantum-enhanced Phase Sensing Via Spectral Noise Reduction
authors: Romain Dalidet, Anthony Martin, Audrey Dot, Inès Ghorbel, Loïc Morvan, Laurent Labonté, And Sébastien Tanzilli
abstract:
Author(s): Romain Dalidet, Anthony Martin, Audrey Dot, Inès Ghorbel, Loïc Morvan, Laurent Labonté, and Sébastien Tanzilli

We report a direct demonstration of quantum-enhanced sensing in the Fourier domain by comparing single- and two-photon interference in a fiber-based interferometer under strictly identical noise conditions. The simultaneous acquisition of both signals provides a common-mode reference that enables a …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033354] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: A fiber-based interferometer demonstrates quantum-enhanced phase sensing by comparing single- and two-photon interference under identical noise, using a common-mode reference to reduce spectral noise.
motivation: To achieve improved phase sensitivity in quantum sensing by exploiting two-photon interference and spectral noise reduction.
method: Single- and two-photon interference signals are simultaneously acquired in a fiber interferometer under strictly identical noise conditions, enabling a common-mode reference.
result: The two-photon interference signal shows enhanced phase sensing performance through reduced spectral noise compared to single-photon interference.
conclusion: Quantum-enhanced phase sensing via spectral noise reduction is directly demonstrated, highlighting the advantage of two-photon interference for metrological applications.

title: Microscopic Theory Of An Atomic Spin Diode
authors: William J. Huddie And Rembert A. Duine
abstract:
Author(s): William J. Huddie and Rembert A. Duine

We present a microscopic theory of an atomic spin diode. Our proposed system consists of two magnetic adatoms deposited on the surface of a two-dimensional electron gas with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. A local s-d type coupling between the local spins and the spins of the electrons induces a nonloca…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144428] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: A microscopic theory of an atomic spin diode based on two magnetic adatoms on a Rashba spin-orbit-coupled two-dimensional electron gas.
motivation: To understand how localized magnetic moments can rectify spin transport at the atomic scale and realize diode-like functionality.
method: The authors model local s-d exchange coupling between adatom spins and 2DEG electrons, deriving effective nonlocal interactions within a scattering or linear-response framework.
result: The coupling induces nonlocal spin transport with diode-like rectification, producing a directional spin current.
conclusion: The work provides a microscopic mechanism for an atomic-scale spin diode and highlights the role of Rashba spin-orbit coupling and magnetic adatoms.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Electronic Structure Via Quantum Fast Multipole Method
authors: Dominic W. Berry, Kianna Wan, Andrew D. Baczewski, Elliot C. Eklund, Arkin Tikku, And Ryan Babbush
abstract:
Author(s): Dominic W. Berry, Kianna Wan, Andrew D. Baczewski, Elliot C. Eklund, Arkin Tikku, and Ryan Babbush

An algorithm for fast summation of the Coulomb potential enables quantum simulation of electronic structure with the lowest known asymptotic complexity in particle number.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033025] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a quantum algorithm for simulating electronic structure based on a quantum fast multipole method for fast Coulomb potential summation, achieving the lowest known asymptotic complexity in particle number.
motivation: Simulating electronic structure on quantum computers is a central application of quantum computing, but existing algorithms are limited by the cost of summing the Coulomb potential among many electrons, which scales poorly with particle number.
method: They adapt the classical fast multipole method—a hierarchical technique for efficiently summing long-range Coulomb interactions—into a quantum algorithm, using it as a subroutine within a quantum simulation of electronic structure.
result: The resulting quantum fast multipole method reduces the asymptotic complexity of electronic-structure simulation to the lowest known scaling in particle number.
conclusion: This establishes a new state of the art for the asymptotic cost of quantum simulation of electronic structure, though it remains an algorithm-level complexity result rather than addressing information-theoretic or thermodynamic questions.

title: Many-Body Correlation Effects In Fröhlich Electron-Phonon Coupling
authors: Zien Zhu, Chih-En Hsu, Benran Zhang, Zhenfa Zheng, Mauro Del Ben, Antonios M. Alvertis, Hung-Chung Hsueh, And Zhenglu Li
abstract:
Author(s): Zien Zhu, Chih-En Hsu, Benran Zhang, Zhenfa Zheng, Mauro Del Ben, Antonios M. Alvertis, Hung-Chung Hsueh, and Zhenglu Li

In compound semiconductors and insulators, the polar electron-phonon coupling diverges at long range, known as the Fröhlich interaction. Modern first-principles electron-phonon calculations treat the Fröhlich interaction in a semiclassical electrostatic formalism based on density-functional perturba…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146401] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops improved first-principles methods for treating many-body correlation effects in the long-range Fröhlich electron-phonon coupling in polar semiconductors and insulators.
motivation: Standard semiclassical electrostatic treatments of the Fröhlich interaction in density-functional perturbation theory may miss correlation effects, motivating a more accurate description of polar electron-phonon coupling in real materials.
method: First-principles electron-phonon calculations, building on density-functional perturbation theory and going beyond semiclassical electrostatic formalisms to capture many-body correlation contributions to the Fröhlich interaction.
result: The authors demonstrate that many-body correlation effects modify the Fröhlich electron-phonon coupling relative to conventional semiclassical treatments in compound semiconductors and insulators.
conclusion: Accurate modeling of polar electron-phonon coupling requires incorporating many-body correlation effects beyond the standard semiclassical Fröhlich formalism.

title: Thouless Pumping Of Large Chern Numbers In Optical Floquet Quasicrystals
authors: Shien Wan, Zecheng Li, And Bo Song
abstract:
Author(s): Shien Wan, Zecheng Li, and Bo Song

Chern numbers are central to correlated and topological phenomena, yet most topological systems are associated with Chern numbers of order unity. Here we propose a scheme to achieve large Chern numbers in an optical Floquet quasicrystal with cold atoms, which can be directly measured via Thouless pu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043301] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an optical Floquet quasicrystal scheme with cold atoms to realize and measure large Chern numbers via Thouless pumping.
motivation: Chern numbers are central to topological phenomena, but most known topological systems exhibit Chern numbers of order unity, motivating the search for platforms hosting large Chern numbers.
method: A Floquet-engineered optical quasicrystal for cold atoms is designed to synthesize effective Hamiltonians with large Chern numbers, with Thouless pumping used as the direct measurement protocol.
result: The scheme demonstrates that large Chern numbers can be realized and directly detected through quantized Thouless pumping of atoms in the Floquet quasicrystal.
conclusion: Optical Floquet quasicrystals with cold atoms provide a viable route to exploring and measuring high-Chern-number topological phases.

title: Molecular-environment-sensitive Ultrafast Dephasing Via Hong-Ou-Mandel Interferometry
authors: T. I. Rajib, M. S. Pochechuev, A. Dharmasiri, K. Hatcher, X. Liu, A. M. Zheltikov, And G. S. Agarwal
abstract:
Author(s): T. I. Rajib, M. S. Pochechuev, A. Dharmasiri, K. Hatcher, X. Liu, A. M. Zheltikov, and G. S. Agarwal

Pairs of photons provide a gentle way to measure the impact of a molecule’s environment on its ultrafast dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033737] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometry with photon pairs to probe how a molecule's local environment affects its ultrafast dephasing dynamics.
motivation: Understanding environment-induced decoherence in molecules is important for ultrafast spectroscopy and light-matter interaction, and photon-pair interferometry offers a gentle, low-perturbation probe.
method: Pairs of photons are sent through a Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometer interacting with a molecule, and the resulting interference visibility is used to extract environment-sensitive dephasing timescales.
result: The interferometric signal is shown to be sensitive to the molecular environment, revealing ultrafast dephasing dynamics imprinted on the photon-pair correlation.
conclusion: Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometry provides a sensitive, non-invasive tool for characterizing molecular-environment-induced ultrafast dephasing.

title: Time-reversal Symmetry Obstruction To Helical Solitons From The Dimensional Extension Of One-dimensional Peierls Chains
authors: Sung-Hoon Lee And Kyusung Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Sung-Hoon Lee and Kyusung Hwang

Dimensional extension by adiabatic phase evolution connects one-dimensional (1D) Peierls chains to two-dimensional (2D) Chern insulators and identifies chiral solitons as the 1D analogs of quantum Hall edge states. Here, we show that this framework cannot generate the 1D counterparts of quantum spin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245403] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the dimensional-extension framework linking 1D Peierls chains to 2D Chern insulators cannot produce 1D analogs of quantum spin Hall edge states due to a time-reversal symmetry obstruction.
motivation: Dimensional extension has successfully connected 1D Peierls chiral solitons to quantum Hall edge states, motivating an attempt to extend this correspondence to the time-reversal-invariant (helical) case.
method: The authors analyze adiabatic phase evolution from 1D Peierls chains to 2D Chern insulators and examine whether time-reversal symmetry permits the analogous construction of helical solitons.
result: They demonstrate a time-reversal symmetry obstruction that prevents the framework from generating the 1D counterparts of quantum spin Hall edge states, i.e., helical solitons.
conclusion: The dimensional-extension approach has a fundamental symmetry-based limitation for helical systems, distinguishing chiral from helical solitons in this framework.

title: Core-hole Excitation Dynamics Of One-dimensional Ultracold Trapped Fermions
authors: A. Becker, G. M. Koutentakis, And P. Schmelcher
abstract:
Author(s): A. Becker, G. M. Koutentakis, and P. Schmelcher

We investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of core-hole excitations in a one-dimensional fermionic few-body system consisting of a spin-polarized Fermi bath coupled to a single heavy mobile impurity. The bath is initially prepared in a particle-hole configuration by emptying a selected bath single-p…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033346] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the nonequilibrium dynamics of core-hole excitations in a one-dimensional spin-polarized Fermi bath coupled to a single heavy mobile impurity.
motivation: Core-hole excitations are relevant to spectroscopic probes of correlated fermionic systems, and understanding their real-time dynamics in few-body ultracold settings can illuminate orthogonality catastrophe physics.
method: The authors prepare a particle-hole excitation by emptying a bath single-particle state and then track the resulting nonequilibrium time evolution of the fermionic few-body system plus heavy impurity, presumably via exact numerical methods.
result: The dynamics of the core-hole excitation and its interplay with the impurity are characterized, revealing the time scales and correlations associated with the excitation in the one-dimensional trap.
conclusion: The work provides insight into few-body nonequilibrium impurity physics, but does not address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platform characterization.

title: Observation Of End-to-end Pumping In A Quasiperiodic Fibonacci-type Photonic Chain
authors: Arnob Kumar Ghosh, Ang Chen, Ashraf El Hassan, Patric Holmvall, Mohamed Bourennane, And Annica M. Black-Schaffer
abstract:
Author(s): Arnob Kumar Ghosh, Ang Chen, Ashraf El Hassan, Patric Holmvall, Mohamed Bourennane, and Annica M. Black-Schaffer

End-to-end pumps utilizing edge-localized states offer a promising route to operate as connecting buses, supplying efficient and robust connectivity between non-neighboring elements in a network. Here, we investigate a finite quasiperiodic Fibonacci-type photonic chain and demonstrate its ability fo…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033347] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally observes end-to-end topological pumping in a finite quasiperiodic Fibonacci-type photonic chain, showing edge-state-mediated robust connectivity.
motivation: Edge-localized states may serve as efficient and robust connecting buses between non-neighboring elements in a network, motivating the study of pumping in quasiperiodic photonic systems.
method: The authors investigate a finite quasiperiodic Fibonacci-type photonic chain and demonstrate its ability to support end-to-end pumping via edge-localized states.
result: They observe end-to-end pumping across the chain, indicating robust and efficient connectivity between distant elements.
conclusion: Quasiperiodic Fibonacci photonic chains can act as connecting buses for network-like architectures, though the work is not directly tied to quantum information, thermodynamics, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Anomaly For Benchmarking Quantum Computing
authors: Tomoya Hayata And Arata Yamamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Tomoya Hayata and Arata Yamamoto

Given the rapid advances in quantum computing hardware, establishing strategies for verifying the correctness of quantum computations has become increasingly important. Exploiting the fact that the axial anomaly in gauge theories is exact to all orders in perturbation theory, we propose the axial an…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033349] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using the exact axial anomaly in gauge theories as a benchmark for verifying the correctness of quantum computations.
motivation: As quantum computing hardware rapidly advances, reliable strategies for verifying quantum computation outputs are increasingly important.
method: Exploiting the fact that the axial anomaly in gauge theories is exact to all orders in perturbation theory, the authors design a benchmarking protocol based on measuring this anomaly on a quantum computer.
result: The axial anomaly provides a theoretically exact reference value, enabling a precise check of quantum computation accuracy.
conclusion: Quantum anomaly benchmarking offers a promising route to validate quantum computations, though it falls outside the researcher's primary information-theoretic, thermodynamic, network, or hybrid-system interests.

title: Removing Nodal And Support-Mismatch Pathologies In Variational Monte Carlo Via Blurred Sampling
authors: Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, And Shiwei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, and Shiwei Zhang

A Monte Carlo postprocessing method called blurred sampling eliminates infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031059] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: A Monte Carlo postprocessing technique called blurred sampling eliminates infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations.
motivation: Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) can suffer from pathological infinite-variance estimators and systematic biases near nodal surfaces or when the sampling distribution mismatches the trial wavefunction, undermining accuracy in quantum many-body simulations.
method: The authors introduce a 'blurred sampling' postprocessing scheme that smooths the Monte Carlo sampling to remove nodal and support-mismatch pathologies while retaining unbiased energy and observable estimates.
result: Blurred sampling is shown to remove the infinite variance and systematic bias that plague standard VMC estimators, restoring well-behaved statistical behavior.
conclusion: The method provides a practical numerical fix for variational quantum many-body simulations, though it sits within computational many-body methodology rather than the researcher's information-theoretic, thermodynamic, networking, or hybrid-platform interests.

title: Revealing Electron-Ytterbium Interactions Through Rydberg Molecular Spectroscopy
authors: Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, And Matthew T. Eiles
abstract:
Author(s): Tangi Legrand, Xin Wang, Florian Pausewang, Wolfgang Alt, Eduardo Uruñuela, Sebastian Hofferberth, Milena Simić, and Matthew T. Eiles

Precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules provides a powerful new window into fundamental atomic properties, laying essential groundwork for future experiments with divalent atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031045] Published Thu Aug 20, 2026.
tldr: Precision spectroscopy of ytterbium Rydberg molecules reveals electron-ytterbium interactions and provides a new window into fundamental atomic properties.
motivation: Understanding electron-atom interactions in divalent atoms is essential for future experiments, but direct probes are challenging.
method: The authors perform precision spectroscopy of giant ytterbium Rydberg molecules to measure their spectral properties.
result: The spectroscopy reveals detailed electron-ytterbium interactions and yields precise molecular data for divalent Rydberg systems.
conclusion: This work establishes Rydberg molecular spectroscopy as a sensitive probe of electron-atom interactions in divalent systems.

title: Protocols For A Many-Body Phase Microscope: From Coherences And $d$-Wave Superconductivity To Green’s Functions
authors: Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, and Fabian Grusdt

New protocols allow extracting of relevant many-body observables, such as
[PRX Quantum 7, 033068] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents protocols for extracting many-body observables such as d-wave superconducting order parameters and Green's functions using quantum gas microscopes.
motivation: Understanding many-body phases like d-wave superconductivity requires direct access to coherences and correlation functions, which are challenging to measure in quantum simulators.
method: The authors develop measurement protocols for quantum gas microscopes to probe coherences, order parameters, and Green's functions in many-body systems.
result: These protocols enable the extraction of d-wave superconducting order parameters and other relevant observables from snapshots of quantum gas microscope experiments.
conclusion: The work expands the capabilities of quantum gas microscopes as many-body phase microscopes, bridging cold-atom quantum simulation and condensed-matter physics.

title: Probing False Vacuum Decay On A Cold-Atom Gauge-Theory Quantum Simulator
authors: Zi-Hang Zhu, Ying Liu, Gianluca Lagnese, Federica Maria Surace, Wei-Yong Zhang, Ming-Gen He, Jad C. Halimeh, Marcello Dalmonte, Siddhardh C. Morampudi, Frank Wilczek, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Hang Zhu, Ying Liu, Gianluca Lagnese, Federica Maria Surace, Wei-Yong Zhang, Ming-Gen He, Jad C. Halimeh, Marcello Dalmonte, Siddhardh C. Morampudi, Frank Wilczek, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

Researchers observe atoms trapped in an optical lattice mimicking particles created in a strong electric field.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 141601] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Researchers use a cold-atom gauge-theory quantum simulator to probe false vacuum decay, observing atoms in an optical lattice that mimic particle creation in a strong electric field.
motivation: False vacuum decay is a fundamental non-perturbative process in quantum field theory and cosmology, but direct experimental investigation is extremely challenging.
method: They trap ultracold atoms in an optical lattice to simulate a gauge theory and measure dynamics associated with false vacuum decay, effectively realizing a quantum simulator of the underlying field theory.
result: The experiment observes signatures of particle creation analogous to the Schwinger effect, providing a quantum simulation of false vacuum decay dynamics.
conclusion: This work demonstrates cold-atom quantum simulators as a powerful platform for studying non-perturbative quantum field theory phenomena, though it falls outside the researcher's primary interests in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Programming Coherent And Quantum Light With A Free-Electron Wavepacket
authors: Songyu Zhu, Yushan Zeng, Chenhao Pan, Yiming Pan, Ye Tian, And Ruxin Li
abstract:
Author(s): Songyu Zhu, Yushan Zeng, Chenhao Pan, Yiming Pan, Ye Tian, and Ruxin Li

The pursuit of programmable light sources with high coherence and spectral purity hinges on establishing a precise set of phase relationships in light-matter interactions. Here, we demonstrate that the quadratic dispersion of a freely propagating electron wave packet serves as a programmable quantum…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 143601] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that the quadratic dispersion of a freely propagating electron wavepacket can program coherent and quantum light.
motivation: To develop programmable light sources with high coherence and spectral purity for quantum technologies.
method: Utilizes the quadratic dispersion of a freely propagating electron wavepacket to control light-matter interactions and phase relationships.
result: The electron wavepacket's dispersion enables programming of coherent and quantum light states.
conclusion: This approach offers a new way to generate tailored quantum light, potentially advancing light sources for quantum applications.

title: Structural Phase Separation Couples To Charge-Density-Wave Formation In Kagome Metal FeGe
authors: Boyang Zhao, Youngjun Ahn, Qinwen Deng, Yidai Liu, Sijie Xu, Donald A. Walko, Stephan O. Hruszkewycz, Pengcheng Dai, Liang Wu, And Haidan Wen
abstract:
Author(s): Boyang Zhao, Youngjun Ahn, Qinwen Deng, Yidai Liu, Sijie Xu, Donald A. Walko, Stephan O. Hruszkewycz, Pengcheng Dai, Liang Wu, and Haidan Wen

Temperature-dependent high-resolution synchrotron X-ray diffraction reveals structural Bragg peak splits in FeGe at the charge-density-wave transition temperature suggesting that its quantum states may be manipulated with strain.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146102] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: Temperature-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction on the kagome metal FeGe reveals structural Bragg peak splitting at the charge-density-wave transition, indicating structural phase separation that couples to CDW formation.
motivation: The interplay between structural inhomogeneity and charge-density-wave order in kagome metals is poorly understood, and clarifying it could enable strain-based manipulation of their quantum states.
method: High-resolution temperature-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction was used to track structural Bragg peak splitting across the CDW transition temperature in FeGe.
result: Bragg peak splits appear at the CDW transition temperature, evidencing a structural phase separation that is coupled to the onset of charge-density-wave order.
conclusion: The coupling between structural phase separation and CDW formation suggests that strain could be used as a knob to control the quantum states of kagome metals.

title: Emergent Andreev Reflection From A Lattice Duality Defect
authors: Atsushi Ueda, Tokiro Numasawa, Boris de Vos, And Masataka Watanabe
abstract:
Author(s): Atsushi Ueda, Tokiro Numasawa, Boris De Vos, and Masataka Watanabe

Andreev reflection converts an incoming fermion into an outgoing hole and is usually tied to a superconducting interface. We show that an analogous charge-conjugating boundary condition emerges from a purely lattice duality defect. Starting from a Majorana representation of the transverse-field Isin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146504] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that an Andreev-reflection-like charge-conjugating boundary condition can emerge from a purely lattice duality defect in a Majorana representation of the transverse-field Ising model, without a superconducting interface.
motivation: Andreev reflection is conventionally tied to superconducting interfaces; this work asks whether its essential particle-hole conversion can be realized from a purely lattice or topological defect.
method: The authors study a lattice duality defect in the Majorana representation of the transverse-field Ising model and analyze the resulting boundary condition.
result: The duality defect induces an emergent Andreev-like reflection, converting an incoming fermion into an outgoing hole.
conclusion: This provides a purely lattice realization of charge-conjugating boundaries, broadening the contexts in which Andreev reflection can appear.

title: Multiphoton Heralding Generates Large-amplitude Squeezed Schrödinger Cat States And Parity-selective Fock Superpositions From Squeezed Vacuum Via An Optical Parametric Amplifier
authors: Yusuf Turek, Ming-Yan Sun, And Xiao-Xi Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuf Turek, Ming-Yan Sun, and Xiao-Xi Yao

We propose a multiphoton heralding scheme using an optical parametric amplifier (OPA) that can generate two families of non-Gaussian states from a squeezed vacuum into: large-amplitude squeezed Schrödinger cat states and low-order parity-selective Fock superpositions. By injecting [MATH] photons into t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043703] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A multiphoton heralding scheme using an optical parametric amplifier is proposed to generate large-amplitude squeezed Schrödinger cat states and parity-selective Fock superpositions from squeezed vacuum.
motivation: Non-Gaussian quantum states such as Schrödinger cat states are valuable for quantum information processing, but their reliable generation with large amplitude remains challenging.
method: The scheme employs an optical parametric amplifier and multiphoton heralding by injecting a certain number of photons into the squeezed vacuum to conditionally produce the target states.
result: The protocol yields two families of non-Gaussian states: large-amplitude squeezed Schrödinger cat states and low-order parity-selective Fock superpositions.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a promising all-optical route to engineer non-Gaussian states, though its direct relevance to the user's core research interests is limited.

title: Plateau Reshaping In Solid-state High-harmonic Generation Driven By The Photon Statistics Of A Bright Squeezed Vacuum
authors: Shidong Yang, Jianbin Lin, Xiwang Liu, Yu Jiang, Torsten Meier, Xiaohong Song, And Weifeng Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Shidong Yang, Jianbin Lin, Xiwang Liu, Yu Jiang, Torsten Meier, Xiaohong Song, and Weifeng Yang

The emerging generation of high brightness quantum light sources opens up new avenues for exploring ultrafast nonlinear optics beyond the classical field regime. Here we study high-harmonic generation (HHG) in ZnO driven by a bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) and show that the photon statistics of the dr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043101] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies high-harmonic generation in ZnO driven by bright squeezed vacuum, showing that photon statistics reshape the HHG plateau.
motivation: Quantum light sources with nonclassical photon statistics offer new routes to control ultrafast nonlinear optical processes beyond the classical-field regime.
method: The authors theoretically investigate solid-state HHG in ZnO under bright squeezed vacuum driving, analyzing how the photon statistics influence the harmonic plateau.
result: The photon statistics of the bright squeezed vacuum modify and reshape the high-harmonic plateau in ZnO compared to classical driving fields.
conclusion: Nonclassical photon statistics provide an additional control knob for solid-state high-harmonic generation, linking quantum optics with strong-field physics.

title: Critical Reexamination Of A Recent Challenge To Bohmian Mechanics
authors: S. Di Matteo And C. Mazzoli
abstract:
Author(s): S. Di Matteo and C. Mazzoli

We reanalyze a recent experiment by Sharoglazova et al. [
tldr: The paper reexamines a recent experiment that challenged Bohmian mechanics and shows that the experimental data can be interpreted within Bohmian mechanics in the stationary evanescent regime.
motivation: To address a recent experimental challenge to Bohmian mechanics and assess its validity.
method: Reanalysis of the experiment by Sharoglazova et al., focusing on the transient regime and the evanescent state in the stationary regime.
result: The experimental data can be interpreted in terms of Bohmian quantum mechanics, contrary to the original challenge.
conclusion: The experiment does not falsify Bohmian mechanics, and the transient regime plays a crucial role in the interpretation.

title: Universal Spin-squeezing Dynamical Phase Transitions Across Lattice Geometries, Dimensions, And Microscopic Couplings
authors: Arman Duha And Thomas Bilitewski
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Duha and Thomas Bilitewski

Recent work has identified a dynamical squeezing phase transition in power-law interacting bilayer XXZ spin models, separating a fully collective phase with Heisenberg-limited squeezing from a partially collective phase with universal critical scaling.
