Here we test and establish the universality of …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032458] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes the universality of a dynamical spin-squeezing phase transition across lattice geometries, dimensions, and microscopic couplings in power-law interacting bilayer XXZ spin models.
motivation: Recent work identified a dynamical squeezing phase transition in specific bilayer XXZ models, but it was unclear whether this phenomenon is universal or model-dependent.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and analytical arguments to study the dynamical spin-squeezing phase transition in bilayer XXZ models with power-law interactions, varying lattice geometry, dimension, and microscopic couplings.

title: Modulation Of Electron Wave Packets By Scattering On Time-harmonic Potentials
authors: Mads Brøndum Carlsen And Lars Bojer Madsen
abstract:
Author(s): Mads Brøndum Carlsen and Lars Bojer Madsen

The coherent interaction between free electrons and optical near-fields enables the active modulation of electron wave packets, which is a mechanism central to photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM). While existing theories effectively describe these interactions at high kinetic energ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033117] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical description of how free-electron wave packets are modulated by scattering from time-harmonic potentials, extending PINEM theory to lower kinetic energies.
motivation: Existing theories for free-electron/optical near-field interactions effectively describe high kinetic energies but are inadequate for low-energy regimes relevant to photon-induced near-field electron microscopy.
method: The authors analyze electron scattering by a time-harmonic potential, likely using quantum scattering theory or perturbative approaches to compute the resulting wave packet modulation and sideband generation.
result: The work predicts how the electron wave packet acquires sidebands and phase modulation, providing a formalism for low-energy electron-light interactions beyond previous high-energy approximations.
conclusion: This framework may enable better interpretation and design of PINEM experiments at low electron energies, though it remains a specialized electron-optics result with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Normal Forms Of Unidirectional Coupling In Quasi-phase-matched non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Kestutis Staliunas
abstract:
Author(s): Kestutis Staliunas

The optimum conditions for unidirectional coupling in quasi-phase-matched non-Hermitian systems are analyzed for both autonomous and externally driven configurations. The quasi-phase-matched coupling mechanism is due to periodic modulation of the real and imaginary parts of the coupling interface, w…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 032218] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes optimal conditions for unidirectional coupling in quasi-phase-matched non-Hermitian systems for autonomous and driven configurations.
motivation: Unidirectional coupling is important for non-Hermitian photonic devices and asymmetric light propagation, but the optimal quasi-phase-matching conditions are not fully understood.
method: The author derives normal forms for unidirectional coupling and studies periodic modulation of the real and imaginary parts of the coupling interface in autonomous and externally driven regimes.
result: Optimal quasi-phase-matching conditions are identified that enable unidirectional coupling in non-Hermitian systems.
conclusion: The results provide design principles for non-Hermitian photonic systems requiring directional coupling, though the work is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Phase Transitions And Intermediate Phases Induced By Nearest-neighbor Dipolar Interaction In A Nonreciprocal non-Hermitian Extended Bose-Hubbard Model
authors: Zhen-Qi Guo And Ji-Guo Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Qi Guo and Ji-Guo Wang

The interplay of non-Hermiticity, nonreciprocal hopping, and interparticle interactions provides new possibilities for tuning localization and emergent phase transitions in quasiperiodic systems. Here we investigate, within the two-body Fock space, the effects of nearest-neighbor dipolar interaction…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214301] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates phase transitions and intermediate phases induced by nearest-neighbor dipolar interactions in a nonreciprocal non-Hermitian extended Bose-Hubbard model.
motivation: Non-Hermiticity, nonreciprocal hopping, and interparticle interactions may enable novel localization and emergent phase transitions in quasiperiodic systems.
method: The authors analyze the two-body Fock space of an extended Bose-Hubbard model with nearest-neighbor dipolar interaction and nonreciprocal hopping, likely using numerical diagonalization or mean-field techniques.
result: They find phase transitions and intermediate phases driven by the interplay of dipolar interactions and non-Hermitian nonreciprocal hopping.
conclusion: The work reveals rich phase diagrams in a non-Hermitian many-body system, but it does not directly address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Valley-dependent Electron Optics Using Quantum Dots In Bilayer Graphene
authors: Fereshte Ildarabadi And Stephen R. Power
abstract:
Author(s): Fereshte Ildarabadi and Stephen R. Power

Electrostatically defined quantum dots (QDs) with layer-antisymmetric gating in Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene (BLG) open a local gap and generate a masslike term with opposite sign in the two valleys, producing strongly valley-dependent scattering without magnetic fields, strain, or spin-orbit cou…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245404] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses electrostatically defined quantum dots in bilayer graphene to achieve valley-dependent electron scattering and electron optics without external fields.
motivation: Valley-dependent control of electrons in graphene could enable valleytronic devices and novel electron optics, but existing methods often require magnetic fields, strain, or spin-orbit coupling.
method: Layer-antisymmetric gating in Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene opens a local gap and creates mass terms of opposite sign in the two valleys, leading to valley-dependent scattering that is studied via theoretical modeling.
result: The quantum dots produce strongly valley-dependent scattering, enabling valley beam splitting, filtering, or routing in a controllable all-electrostatic manner.
conclusion: This work establishes a platform for valleytronics and electron optics in bilayer graphene, with potential applications in valley-based information processing.

title: Graded Hopping Screens Nonreciprocity And Reorganizes Stark Asymptotics In A non-Hermitian Stark Chain
authors: Y. S. Liu And X. Z. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Y. S. Liu and X. Z. Zhang

We study a one-dimensional non-Hermitian Stark chain with nonreciprocal, linearly graded hopping. A diagonal similarity transformation eliminates the bond asymmetry and changes the usual exponential skin factor into an algebraic accumulation, [MATH], with [MATH]. At fixed spectral …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194301] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: A non-Hermitian Stark chain with linearly graded nonreciprocal hopping is shown to screen nonreciprocity and convert the usual exponential skin effect into algebraic accumulation, reorganizing Stark asymptotics.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems with nonreciprocal hopping exhibit the skin effect, and understanding how inhomogeneous or graded couplings modify this behavior is of broad interest in non-Hermitian physics.
method: The authors use a diagonal similarity transformation to eliminate bond asymmetry in a one-dimensional non-Hermitian Stark chain with linearly graded hopping.
result: The transformation changes the conventional exponential skin factor into an algebraic accumulation with modified Stark asymptotics, effectively screening the nonreciprocity.
conclusion: Graded hopping provides a mechanism to control and reorganize non-Hermitian skin effects and Stark localization, with potential implications for non-Hermitian lattice design.

title: Dissipative Quantum Mechanics Of Andreev Bound States
authors: Mikhail S. Kalenkov And Andrei D. Zaikin
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail S. Kalenkov and Andrei D. Zaikin

Microscopic description of ac Josephson effect in superconducting junctions beyond the tunneling limit should account for subtle nonequilibrium effects. Here, the authors demonstrate that this problem can be fully resolved by analyzing dissipative quantum dynamics of Andreev bound states inside the junction. Within this analysis, the authors identify Landau-Zener tunneling between subgap Andreev levels and quantum escape of quasiparticles from such levels into continuum of states above the gap as the dominant processes for the problem under consideration.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214502] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes dissipative quantum dynamics of Andreev bound states to resolve nonequilibrium effects in the ac Josephson effect beyond the tunneling limit.
motivation: A microscopic description of the ac Josephson effect in superconducting junctions beyond the tunneling limit must account for subtle nonequilibrium processes.
method: The authors study dissipative quantum dynamics of Andreev bound states, identifying Landau-Zener tunneling between subgap levels and quasiparticle escape into the continuum.
result: Landau-Zener tunneling and quantum escape of quasiparticles are found to be the dominant processes governing the nonequilibrium behavior.
conclusion: This provides a complete resolution of the problem beyond the tunneling limit through the dynamics of Andreev bound states.

title: Sequential Circuits As Generalized Symmetry On The Lattice
authors: Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Xinyu Liu, And Xie Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Xinyu Liu, and Xie Chen

Generalized symmetry extends the usual notion of symmetry to ones that are of higher form, acting on subsystems, noninvertible, etc. The concept was defined in the field theory context using the idea of topological defects. On the lattice, an immediate consequence is that a symmetry twist is moved a…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225101] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores how sequential circuits can be understood as a form of generalized symmetry on the lattice, extending higher-form and noninvertible symmetry concepts from field theory to lattice models.
motivation: Generalized symmetry generalizes ordinary symmetry to higher-form, subsystem, and noninvertible actions, and has been primarily formulated in field theory via topological defects. A lattice formulation could clarify its physical consequences and connect to concrete models.
method: The authors likely analyze sequential quantum circuits on a lattice and interpret them as generalized symmetry transformations, using topological defect ideas to characterize symmetry twists and their movement.
result: They show that sequential circuits realize generalized symmetries on the lattice, with implications for how symmetry defects can be moved and how such symmetries act on subsystems.
conclusion: The work provides a lattice perspective on generalized symmetries and suggests that sequential circuits offer a useful framework for studying higher-form and noninvertible symmetries in condensed matter systems.

title: Millisecond-long Electron Spin Lifetime In ${\mathrm{CsPbI}}_{3}$ Perovskite Nanocrystals Revealed By Optically Detected Magnetic Resonance
authors: Vasilii V. Belykh, Mikhail M. Glazov, Sergey R. Meliakov, Dmitri R. Yakovlev, Evgeniya V. Kulebyakina, Mikhail L. Skorikov, Mikhail V. Kochiev, Maria S. Kuznetsova, Elena V. Kolobkova, And Manfred Bayer
abstract:
Author(s): Vasilii V. Belykh, Mikhail M. Glazov, Sergey R. Meliakov, Dmitri R. Yakovlev, Evgeniya V. Kulebyakina, Mikhail L. Skorikov, Mikhail V. Kochiev, Maria S. Kuznetsova, Elena V. Kolobkova, and Manfred Bayer

Here, the authors reveal millisecond-long electron spin relaxation in CsPbI
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225301] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports millisecond-long electron spin lifetimes in CsPbI3 perovskite nanocrystals measured via optically detected magnetic resonance, attributing low-field relaxation to nuclear spin fluctuations and high-temperature behavior to a two-LO-phonon Raman process.
motivation: Long electron spin lifetimes in semiconductor nanocrystals are valuable for spintronics and quantum technologies, but the relaxation mechanisms in perovskite nanocrystals are not well understood.
method: The authors use the resonant spin inertia technique based on optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) at low temperatures, supported by theoretical modeling of nuclear spin fluctuations and phonon-assisted relaxation.
result: They observe electron spin relaxation times reaching milliseconds, reveal the role of slowly fluctuating nuclear spins at low magnetic fields, and show that a two-LO-phonon Raman process governs the temperature dependence.
conclusion: CsPbI3 perovskite nanocrystals exhibit exceptionally long electron spin lifetimes, with the dominant relaxation mechanisms identified, suggesting potential for spin-based applications.

title: Spin-orbit-entangled ${J}_{\mathrm{eff}}=\frac{1}{2}$ Magnetism And Unconventional Spin Freezing In The Bond-disordered Pyrochlore Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{NaCdCo}}_{2}{\mathrm{F}}_{7}$
authors: A. Kancko, H. Sakai, J. Herrero-Martín, A. Berlie, M. Uhlarz, T. Haidamak, M. Klicpera, Y. Tokunaga, And R. H. Colman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Kancko, H. Sakai, J. Herrero-Martín, A. Berlie, M. Uhlarz, T. Haidamak, M. Klicpera, Y. Tokunaga, and R. H. Colman

Here, the authors establish NaCdCo
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 154431] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a spin-orbit-entangled Jeff=1/2 pyrochlore antiferromagnet NaCdCo2F7 where bond disorder and frustration lead to unconventional spin freezing with persistent dynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to explore how strong geometric frustration and bond disorder affect the magnetic ground state in a spin-orbit-entangled pyrochlore antiferromagnet.
method: They use thermodynamic, muon spin relaxation, and neutron scattering measurements to characterize the magnetic properties and spin dynamics of NaCdCo2F7.
result: NaCdCo2F7 exhibits a frozen magnetic state at low temperatures but retains persistent spin dynamics, revealing an unusual coexistence of static and dynamic magnetism.
conclusion: The work establishes NaCdCo2F7 as a new platform for studying disorder-induced frustration and unconventional spin freezing in Jeff=1/2 pyrochlore magnets.

title: Signatures Of The Quantum Geometric Dipole Of Interlayer Excitons In Counterflow Conductivity
authors: Fanuel I. Mendez, Luis Brey, And H. A. Fertig
abstract:
Author(s): Fanuel I. Mendez, Luis Brey, and H. A. Fertig

Collective excitations of many-body electron systems can carry internal structure, supporting novel quantum geometric and topological properties. Among these are a quantum geometric dipole (QGD), which for excitons have direct significance as an internal polarization. For interlayer excitons of a bi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175415] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies signatures of a quantum geometric dipole carried by interlayer excitons in the counterflow conductivity of a bilayer electron system.
motivation: Collective excitations like excitons can possess internal quantum geometric structure, and the authors ask whether exciton dipoles leave observable imprints on transport measurements.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework computing the quantum geometric dipole of interlayer excitons and its contribution to counterflow conductivity, based on the bilayer band structure and exciton internal polarization.
result: The quantum geometric dipole produces distinctive features in the counterflow conductivity that serve as experimental signatures of the excitonic internal structure.
conclusion: Counterflow transport provides a measurable probe of quantum geometric properties of excitons, connecting many-body collective excitations to quantum geometry.

title: Graphon Spin Systems As Exactly Solvable Models
authors: Artem Alexandrov And Georgi S. Medvedev
abstract:
Author(s): Artem Alexandrov and Georgi S. Medvedev

Graphons are measurable functions used to describe the asymptotic behavior of convergent graph families. Originally motivated by problems in combinatorics and graph theory, graphons have found numerous applications in the modeling and analysis of dynamical processes on networks. In this work, we use…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044102] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses graphons to define and solve spin systems on dense graph limits, providing exactly solvable models for statistical mechanics on networks.
motivation: Graphons characterize the asymptotic behavior of convergent graph families and have been applied to dynamical processes on networks, motivating their use for spin systems.
method: The authors formulate spin models on graphons and derive exact solutions, likely through mean-field or operator techniques, for thermodynamic quantities.
result: Exact solutions are obtained for the partition function and other observables, revealing the thermodynamic behavior of these graphon-based spin systems.
conclusion: Graphon spin systems offer a tractable framework for studying statistical mechanics on complex networks and may enable further analytical insights.

title: Finite-time Observability Of Oscillatory Instabilities In Synchronous P-bit Dynamics
authors: Naoya Onizawa, Shunsuke Koshita, And Takahiro Hanyu
abstract:
Author(s): Naoya Onizawa, Shunsuke Koshita, and Takahiro Hanyu

Synchronous update schemes in p-bit annealing offer a natural route to massive parallelism, but they can also induce period-2 oscillations that degrade optimization performance. In practical solvers, such oscillations matter only if they become observable within the finite runtime of the device or s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034143] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes when period-2 oscillations in synchronously updated p-bit annealing become observable within finite runtime, affecting optimization performance.
motivation: Synchronous p-bit updates enable parallelism but can induce oscillatory instabilities that degrade solver performance, and practical relevance depends on whether these oscillations appear within device runtime.
method: The authors study the dynamics of synchronous p-bit networks and derive finite-time observability conditions for period-2 oscillations, likely using stability analysis and numerical simulations.
result: They characterize parameter regimes and time scales under which oscillatory instabilities become observable, showing how finite runtime constrains their impact on optimization.
conclusion: The work provides criteria for predicting and mitigating harmful oscillations in synchronous p-bit solvers, helping design more reliable probabilistic annealing hardware.

title: Finite-size Clocks In Quantum Field Theory And The Twin Paradox
authors: Matheus H. Zambianco And T. Rick Perche
abstract:
Author(s): Matheus H. Zambianco and T. Rick Perche

Vacuum fluctuations in quantum field theory impose fundamental limitations on our ability to measure time at arbitrarily short scales. To investigate the impact of universal quantum field theory effects on observer-dependent time measurements, we introduce a clock model based on the vacuum decay pro…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043003] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a finite-size clock model in quantum field theory to study fundamental limitations on time measurement and the twin paradox.
motivation: Vacuum fluctuations in quantum field theory are expected to impose fundamental limits on measuring time at short scales, motivating an investigation of how universal QFT effects influence observer-dependent time measurements.
method: The authors construct a clock model based on the vacuum decay process and analyze its behavior within quantum field theory, applying it to the twin paradox scenario.
result: The model reveals finite-size corrections and fundamental bounds on clock precision arising from vacuum fluctuations, with implications for relativistic time dilation.
conclusion: Quantum field theory effects set intrinsic limits on time measurement that must be accounted for in observer-dependent timing, refining our understanding of the twin paradox.

title: Learning Parameter Curves In Feedback-based Quantum Algorithms
authors: Vicente Peña Pérez, Matthew D. Grace, Christian Arenz, And Alicia B. Magann
abstract:
Author(s): Vicente Peña Pérez, Matthew D. Grace, Christian Arenz, and Alicia B. Magann

Feedback-based quantum algorithms (FQAs) operate by iteratively growing a quantum circuit to optimize a given task. At each step, feedback from qubit measurements is used to inform the next quantum circuit update. In practice, the sampling cost associated with these measurements can be significant. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033378] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a method to learn parameter curves for feedback-based quantum algorithms, aiming to reduce the measurement sampling cost associated with iterative circuit updates.
motivation: Feedback-based quantum algorithms iteratively grow a quantum circuit using qubit measurements to guide updates, but the required sampling can be prohibitively expensive in practice.
method: The authors propose learning parameter curves that prescribe how circuit parameters should change across algorithm iterations, likely using interpolation or regression to avoid repeated optimization from measurements.
result: The learned parameter curves are shown to maintain algorithmic performance while substantially reducing the number of measurements needed compared to standard feedback-based optimization.
conclusion: Learning parameter curves offers an efficient strategy for implementing feedback-based quantum algorithms with lower sampling overhead, making them more practical for near-term devices.

title: Tunable Two-dimensional Energy Orbital Angular Momentum Synthetic Lattices With Free Electrons
authors: Jing Li, Yuhan Jiang, Wu Wen, Dixuan Wu, And Yunquan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Li, Yuhan Jiang, Wu Wen, Dixuan Wu, and Yunquan Liu

Free-electron interactions with optical near fields are conventionally described as one-dimensional energy ladders, in which multicolor photon-exchange pathways can become spectrally degenerate. In this work, we show that coupling a single free electron to commensurate two-color optical vortices can…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033355] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: Coupling a single free electron to commensurate two-color optical vortices creates a tunable two-dimensional synthetic lattice in energy-orbital angular momentum space, generalizing the usual 1D energy ladder picture.
motivation: Free-electron interactions with optical near fields are conventionally described as one-dimensional energy ladders where multicolor photon-exchange pathways can become spectrally degenerate, limiting the achievable control over electron spectral states.
method: The authors couple a free electron to commensurate two-color optical vortices (beams carrying orbital angular momentum) and analyze the resulting photon-exchange dynamics, showing it generates a synthetic two-dimensional lattice spanned by energy and OAM quantum numbers.
result: The scheme yields a tunable 2D energy-OAM synthetic lattice whose structure and degeneracies can be controlled via the vortex parameters, lifting the degeneracies of the conventional 1D ladder description.
conclusion: Free electrons interacting with structured two-color light provide a versatile platform for engineering higher-dimensional synthetic lattices and controlling electron quantum states, with potential applications in free-electron quantum optics and electron-beam spectroscopy.

title: Unified Framework For Photon Dynamics In non-Euclidean Polygonal Cavities
authors: Yechun Ding, Yongsheng Wang, Peng Li, Yaxin Guo, Yanpeng Zhang, Feng Yun, Ce Shang, Run-Qiu Yang, Caigui Jiang, And Feng Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yechun Ding, Yongsheng Wang, Peng Li, Yaxin Guo, Yanpeng Zhang, Feng Yun, Ce Shang, Run-Qiu Yang, Caigui Jiang, and Feng Li

We extend the concept of polygonal resonators to curved spaces through a unified model governed by a joint curvature parameter. This framework uncovers unique dynamics, including dissipative states defined by hyperbolic fixed points that yield phase diagrams in the curvature space. We find that stab…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033334] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A unified framework extends polygonal resonators to curved spaces, revealing photon dynamics and dissipative states governed by a curvature parameter.
motivation: To generalize the concept of polygonal resonators to non-Euclidean geometries and understand how curvature affects photon dynamics.
method: The authors introduce a joint curvature parameter to model photon dynamics in polygonal cavities on curved surfaces, analyzing fixed points and phase diagrams.
result: They identify dissipative states defined by hyperbolic fixed points and construct phase diagrams in the curvature space, uncovering stable regimes.
conclusion: The framework provides new insights into photon dynamics in curved geometries, with potential implications for optical and photonic device design.

title: Geometrically Frustrated Quadrupoles On The Pyrochlore Lattice And Generalized Spin Liquids
authors: Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, And Paul Mcclarty
abstract:
Author(s): Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, and Paul McClarty

A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors, showing how angular-momentum-dependent geometries dictate generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated magnets.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031065] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors to study geometrically frustrated magnetism and generalized spin-liquid phases on the pyrochlore lattice.
motivation: Understanding how angular-momentum-dependent geometries give rise to exotic nematic and spin-liquid states in frustrated magnets.
method: Semiclassical treatment of quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors on the pyrochlore lattice, with analysis of the resulting phase behavior.
result: The framework reveals generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids driven by geometric frustration.
conclusion: The work extends the theory of spin liquids and frustration to quadrupolar degrees of freedom, highlighting the role of lattice geometry.

title: Observing The Spatial And Temporal Evolution Of Exciton Wave Functions In Organic Semiconductors
authors: Marcel Theilen, Siegfried Kaidisch, Monja Stettner, Sarah Zajusch, Eric Fackelman, Alexa Adamkiewicz, Robert Wallauer, Andreas Windischbacher, Christian S. Kern, Michael G. Ramsey, François C. Bocquet, Serguei Soubatch, F. Stefan Tautz, Ulrich Höfer, And Peter Puschnig
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Theilen, Siegfried Kaidisch, Monja Stettner, Sarah Zajusch, Eric Fackelman, Alexa Adamkiewicz, Robert Wallauer, Andreas Windischbacher, Christian S. Kern, Michael G. Ramsey, François C. Bocquet, Serguei Soubatch, F. Stefan Tautz, Ulrich Höfer, and Peter Puschnig

Femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography tracks photoelectron profiles to reconstruct the real-space distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons in an organic semiconductor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031054] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: Femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography reconstructs the real-space distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons in an organic semiconductor.
motivation: Understanding how exciton wave functions evolve in space and time is key to charge and energy transport in organic semiconductors, but direct experimental access to their internal quantum phase has been lacking.
method: The authors use femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography to track photoelectron momentum profiles and invert them into real-space exciton wave functions.
result: The measurements reveal the spatial distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons, following their evolution on ultrafast timescales in an organic semiconductor film.
conclusion: Time-resolved orbital tomography provides a new window into exciton quantum dynamics in molecular materials, with implications for organic optoelectronics.

title: Theory Of Quantum-Enhanced Interferometry With General Markovian Light Sources
authors: Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, And Rahul Trivedi
abstract:
Author(s): Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, and Rahul Trivedi

A new framework for designing and evaluating quantum light sources clarifies where realistic devices can provide a quantum advantage in interferometry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033069] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for quantum-enhanced interferometry using general Markovian light sources to clarify when realistic devices can provide a quantum advantage.
motivation: Realistic quantum light sources are noisy and imperfect, so it is crucial to determine under which conditions they outperform classical sources in interferometric measurements.
method: The authors formulate a general Markovian model for quantum light sources and analyze the achievable precision limits, likely using quantum Fisher information or related metrological tools.
result: The framework identifies regimes where realistic Markovian light sources can provide a genuine quantum advantage in interferometry, despite imperfections.
conclusion: This work offers design principles for quantum light sources intended for interferometry and clarifies the boundary between classical and quantum-enhanced performance.

title: Theory Of Trotter Errors For Time-Dependent Product And Multi-product Formulas
authors: Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, and Keisuke Fujii

A Floquet-based analysis derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, sharpening gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033061] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: A Floquet-based analysis derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, sharpening gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.
motivation: Trotterization and product formulas are standard tools for Hamiltonian simulation, but error bounds for time-dependent and multiproduct cases need sharper analysis to optimize gate counts.
method: The authors use Floquet theory to analyze how Trotter errors scale with commutators for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas.
result: They obtain commutator-scaling error bounds that improve gate-count estimates for simulating driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.
conclusion: The work provides practical guidance for designing efficient quantum simulation algorithms based on product formulas.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm For Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics With Bounded Quantum Advantage
authors: David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, And Stephen Rolston
abstract:
Author(s): David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, and Stephen Rolston

A detailed resource analysis identifies the fundamental bottlenecks and achievable speedups for nonlinear fluid simulations on a fault-tolerant quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033060] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A resource analysis of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics on fault-tolerant quantum computers, identifying bottlenecks and bounded speedups.
motivation: Nonlinear fluid dynamics is computationally demanding classically, motivating assessment of whether fault-tolerant quantum computers can provide practical speedups.
method: The authors perform a detailed resource analysis of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for simulating nonlinear fluid dynamics, estimating fault-tolerant resource requirements and achievable quantum advantage.
result: They identify fundamental bottlenecks and bound the achievable speedup, showing limited quantum advantage for this application.
conclusion: The results temper expectations for quantum fluid simulations and highlight resource constraints in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Imaginary Time Evolution And Ground State Preparation Using Unitary Multi-Copy Protocols
authors: Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, And H. R. Sadeghpour
abstract:
Author(s): Tal Schwartzman, Torsten V. Zache, Hannes Pichler, and H. R. Sadeghpour

Real-time evolution and sᴡᴀᴘ operations are combined to efficiently suppress excited-state populations using multiple copies of the quantum system.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033033] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper combines real-time evolution and swap operations in unitary multi-copy protocols to suppress excited-state populations for ground state preparation.
motivation: Ground state preparation is a key task, but imaginary time evolution is non-unitary; emulating it with unitary operations requires novel approaches.
method: They use multiple copies of a quantum system and combine real-time evolution with swap operations to implement an effective imaginary time evolution that filters out excited states.
result: The protocol efficiently suppresses excited-state populations, enabling ground state preparation without non-unitary operations.
conclusion: Unitary multi-copy protocols provide a viable route to ground state preparation and imaginary time evolution in quantum systems.

title: Pauli Propagation: A Computational Framework For Simulating Quantum Systems
authors: Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, and Zoë Holmes

A comprehensive account of the Pauli propagation method for simulating quantum systems, from theory framework to software implementation and applications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 032001] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a comprehensive computational framework for simulating quantum systems using the Pauli propagation method.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum systems is essential for benchmarking quantum devices and exploring quantum dynamics that are difficult to access experimentally.
method: The authors develop the theory of Pauli propagation, implement it as software, and demonstrate its applications to various quantum simulation tasks.
result: The framework provides an efficient and scalable approach to propagate Pauli operators and estimate observables in quantum circuits and many-body systems.
conclusion: Pauli propagation offers a versatile tool for classical simulation, with potential applications in quantum algorithm development and error analysis.

title: Unconventional Superconductivity From Lattice Quantum Disorder
authors: Yu-Cheng Zhu, Jia-Xi Zeng, And Xin-Zheng Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Cheng Zhu, Jia-Xi Zeng, and Xin-Zheng Li

Unconventional superconductivity presents a defining challenge in physics. Prevailing theoretical frameworks have predominantly emphasized electrons, largely neglecting the rich physics inherent in the lattice. Conventional phonon theory omits quantum many-body effects of the nuclei, leading to misl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Lattice quantum disorder and nuclear quantum many-body effects are proposed as a mechanism for unconventional superconductivity, going beyond purely electronic theories.
motivation: Unconventional superconductivity remains a major challenge, and conventional phonon theory neglects quantum many-body effects of nuclei, potentially missing key physics.
method: Theoretical modeling of lattice quantum disorder and electron-nuclear quantum many-body effects to derive superconducting pairing.
result: The work shows that lattice quantum disorder can drive unconventional superconductivity, offering a new perspective beyond electron-centric frameworks.
conclusion: Incorporating lattice quantum effects is crucial for a complete understanding of unconventional superconductivity.

title: General Construction From Topological Loop States To Topological Invariants In Exactly Flat Bands
authors: Rui-Heng Liu, Jiangping Hu, And Chen Fang
abstract:
Author(s): Rui-Heng Liu, Jiangping Hu, and Chen Fang

Electronic flat bands have localized Wannier-like orbitals as zero modes. In the Lieb or kagome models, the localized orbitals satisfy a topological condition that entails two noncontractible loop eigenstates along the [MATH] axis in real space and one topological band touchin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146601] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a general construction linking topological loop states (noncontractible loop eigenstates) in exactly flat bands to topological invariants, exemplified by the Lieb and kagome lattice models.
motivation: Electronic flat bands host localized Wannier-like zero modes, and understanding how their real-space topological conditions translate into band topological invariants is an open question relevant to the classification of topological flat-band systems.
method: The authors analyze localized orbitals in Lieb and kagome models that satisfy a topological condition, deriving noncontractible loop eigenstates in real space and a topological band-touching structure, then generalize this to a construction relating loop states to topological invariants.
result: They establish a general mapping from topological loop states to topological invariants in exactly flat bands, showing that the loop eigenstates along a real-space axis encode the nontrivial band topology.
conclusion: The work provides a unified real-space framework for characterizing topological flat bands, clarifying the connection between localized loop modes and topological invariants in lattice models.

title: Quantum-Geometry-Enabled Landau-Zener Tunneling In Singular Flat Bands
authors: Xuanyu Long And Feng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xuanyu Long and Feng Liu

Flat-band materials have attracted substantial interest for their intriguing quantum geometric effects. Here we investigate how singular flat bands (SFBs) respond to a static, uniform electric field in the weak-field regime and whether they can support single-particle dc transport. By constructing a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146302] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how singular flat bands under a weak uniform electric field exhibit quantum-geometry-enabled Landau-Zener tunneling and whether they can support single-particle DC transport.
motivation: Flat-band materials have attracted interest for quantum geometric effects, but their response to static electric fields and their potential for single-particle DC transport remain poorly understood.
method: The authors construct and analyze a model of singular flat bands in the weak-field regime, likely computing Landau-Zener transition rates and transport properties.
result: They find that quantum geometry enables Landau-Zener tunneling in singular flat bands, and this mechanism may allow single-particle DC transport.
conclusion: Quantum geometry plays a central role in the electric-field response and transport of singular flat bands, offering a new route for DC conduction in flat-band systems.

title: Bilayer Crystals In A Polar-molecule System
authors: Vinicius Zampronio, Matteo Ciardi, And Fabio Cinti
abstract:
Author(s): Vinicius Zampronio, Matteo Ciardi, and Fabio Cinti

We investigate the finite-temperature phase diagram of polar molecules confined in a quasi-two-dimensional geometry by a harmonic potential along the polarization axis. We employ quantum Monte Carlo simulations to explore the strongly correlated regime accessible with current experimental setups. By…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033325] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses quantum Monte Carlo simulations to map the finite-temperature phase diagram of polar molecules confined in a quasi-two-dimensional bilayer geometry.
motivation: Polar molecules in reduced dimensions offer a platform for exploring strongly correlated phases, but their finite-temperature phase behavior under harmonic confinement is not fully understood.
method: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations are employed to study a quasi-two-dimensional system of polar molecules with a harmonic potential along the polarization axis.
result: The phase diagram reveals bilayer crystal phases and the boundaries between them in the strongly correlated regime accessible to current experiments.
conclusion: The work characterizes how confinement and dipolar interactions stabilize crystalline order in bilayer polar-molecule systems, guiding future cold-atom experiments.

title: Dimensionality Of A Strongly Interacting Two-dimensional–three-dimensional Fermi-Fermi Mixture From The Perspective Of Superfluid Instability And Excitation Properties
authors: Haruka Takeda, Saki Hirai, Shumpei Iwasaki, And Yoji Ohashi
abstract:
Author(s): Haruka Takeda, Saki Hirai, Shumpei Iwasaki, and Yoji Ohashi

We theoretically investigate strong-coupling properties of an attractively interacting Fermi atomic gas, where the Cooper-pair formation occurs between atoms belonging to different dimensional bands. Including pairing fluctuations within the framework of the self-consistent [MATH]-matrix approximation,…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033326] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically studies a strongly interacting two-dimensional–three-dimensional Fermi-Fermi mixture using a self-consistent T-matrix approach to analyze superfluid instability and excitation properties.
motivation: Ultracold Fermi gases with mixed dimensionality are interesting for exploring how dimensional mismatch affects Cooper pairing and superfluidity in the strong-coupling regime.
method: The authors include pairing fluctuations within the self-consistent T-matrix approximation to describe an attractively interacting Fermi atomic gas where Cooper pairs form between atoms in different dimensional bands.
result: The analysis reveals how the 2D–3D dimensionality influences superfluid instability and the excitation spectrum of the strongly interacting mixture.
conclusion: The paper clarifies the role of dimensionality in determining the superfluid phase and excitation properties of a strongly correlated Fermi-Fermi mixture.

title: Non-Hermitian Topology Driven By An Identity Term: An Exactly Solvable Paradigm
authors: Lingfang Li, Yating Wei, Yang Ruan, Gangzhou Wu, Jun Wang, Shihua Chen, Tong Lin, Ching Hua Lee, And Zhenhua Ni
abstract:
Author(s): Lingfang Li, Yating Wei, Yang Ruan, Gangzhou Wu, Jun Wang, Shihua Chen, Tong Lin, Ching Hua Lee, and Zhenhua Ni

An identity term in the Hamiltonian is conventionally regarded as spectrally inert; it shifts energies but does not alter eigenstate topology. We show that under non-Hermitian skin pumping, this paradigm fails: a momentum-dependent identity term actively deforms the generalized Brillouin zone, there…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245102] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that a momentum-dependent identity term in a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian can actively deform the generalized Brillouin zone and alter eigenstate topology under non-Hermitian skin pumping, contrary to the conventional view that identity terms are spectrally inert.
motivation: Identity terms are usually considered to shift energy levels without affecting eigenstate topology, but non-Hermitian skin effects may invalidate this assumption.
method: The authors construct an exactly solvable non-Hermitian model and analyze how a momentum-dependent identity term modifies the generalized Brillouin zone and skin pumping.
result: The identity term is shown to deform the generalized Brillouin zone and drive topological transitions, revealing a mechanism absent in Hermitian systems.
conclusion: The work provides an analytically tractable paradigm for identity-term-driven non-Hermitian topology, expanding the understanding of topological phases in non-Hermitian systems.

title: Phonon-renormalized Noncollinear Rkky Interaction In Rashba Altermagnets
authors: Bui D. Hoi
abstract:
Author(s): Bui D. Hoi

Altermagnets, characterized by time-reversal symmetry breaking without net magnetization and momentum-dependent spin-split bands, offer a promising platform for spintronics due to their anisotropic spin textures and potential for tunable magnetic interactions. Here, we theoretically investigate the …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204403] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of how phonons renormalize the noncollinear RKKY interaction in Rashba altermagnets for spintronics applications.
motivation: Altermagnets, which break time-reversal symmetry without net magnetization and feature momentum-dependent spin-split bands, are promising for spintronics, but the role of lattice vibrations in their magnetic exchange interactions is underexplored.
method: The author theoretically investigates the effective RKKY interaction in a Rashba altermagnet, incorporating phonon-mediated renormalization effects to derive the resulting noncollinear magnetic coupling.
result: Phonon renormalization is shown to modify the noncollinear RKKY interaction, affecting the anisotropic spin texture and the resulting magnetic ordering in the Rashba altermagnet.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of electron-phonon coupling and spin-orbit effects for tunable magnetic interactions in altermagnets, with potential implications for spintronic device design.

title: Restoring Information In Aged Gene Regulatory Networks By Single Knock-ins
authors: Ryan Lefebre, Tyler Schutt, Fabrisia Ambrosio, And Andrew Mugler
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan LeFebre, Tyler Schutt, Fabrisia Ambrosio, and Andrew Mugler

Recent analyses have demonstrated that aging is associated with a loss of information within gene regulatory networks. In this article, a simple theoretical framework is developed for information transmission in gene regulatory networks and this framework is applied to gene expression data from muscle cells in young and old mice. The authors predict how much of the lost information is restored by “knocking in” (exogenously expressing) each gene and find that single knock-ins can restore network information by up to 10%.

#BiophysicsSpotlight #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044401] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for information transmission in gene regulatory networks is applied to aging mouse muscle data, predicting that single gene knock-ins can restore up to 10% of lost network information.
motivation: Aging is associated with a loss of information in gene regulatory networks, and it is unclear how much of this loss can be reversed by targeted interventions such as gene knock-ins.
method: The authors develop a simple information-theoretic framework for gene regulatory networks and apply it to gene expression data from young and old mouse muscle cells, calculating the restoration of information from exogenously expressing each gene individually.
result: Single knock-ins are predicted to restore network information by up to 10%, depending on the gene targeted.
conclusion: The framework provides a quantitative way to assess information recovery in aging gene networks and suggests that single-gene interventions can partially mitigate age-related information loss.

title: Inference Of Thermodynamic Conditions In Convergent High-energy-density-physics Experiments
authors: E. A. Smith, J. J. Ruby, D. A. Chin, D. T. Bishel, M. E. Signor, T. E. Evans, K. N. Lofton, N. V. Kabadi, J. R. Rygg, And G. W. Collins
abstract:
Author(s): E. A. Smith, J. J. Ruby, D. A. Chin, D. T. Bishel, M. E. Signor, T. E. Evans, K. N. Lofton, N. V. Kabadi, J. R. Rygg, and G. W. Collins

Laser-driven spherical implosion experiments create some of the most extreme states of matter accessible in the laboratory. However, experimental observables in implosion experiments are highly integrated, meaning that measurements cannot be straightforwardly inverted to characterize the thermodynam…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035216] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an inference approach to characterize thermodynamic conditions from highly integrated observables in laser-driven high-energy-density implosion experiments.
motivation: Laser-driven spherical implosions produce extreme states of matter, but their experimental observables are highly integrated, making direct thermodynamic characterization difficult.
method: The authors use inference techniques to extract thermodynamic conditions from integrated implosion measurements, likely combining experimental data with models of convergent high-energy-density physics.
result: The work demonstrates that thermodynamic conditions in convergent HED experiments can be inferred despite the non-invertibility of raw observables.
conclusion: This provides a practical framework for diagnosing extreme-state plasma experiments, though it is outside quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Liquid And Solid Layers In A Thermal Deep-learning Machine
authors: Gang Huang, Lai Shun Chan, Hajime Yoshino, Ge Zhang, And Yuliang Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Gang Huang, Lai Shun Chan, Hajime Yoshino, Ge Zhang, and Yuliang Jin

We study generalization in overparameterized deep neural networks using a thermal deep learning machine with a well-defined Hamiltonian. We find that learning dynamics organize the network into a solid–liquid–solid structure, where boundary layers are constrained while central layers remain flexible…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035309] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies generalization in overparameterized deep neural networks using a thermal deep-learning machine, revealing a solid-liquid-solid layer structure.
motivation: Understanding how learning dynamics and thermal effects shape network organization can provide physical insight into generalization in deep learning.
method: A thermal deep-learning machine with a well-defined Hamiltonian is used to simulate learning dynamics and analyze the rigidity or flexibility of network layers.
result: Learning organizes the network into a solid-liquid-solid structure, where boundary layers become constrained while central layers remain flexible.
conclusion: The emergent solid-liquid-solid structure offers a physical picture linking thermal dynamics and layer-wise constraints to generalization in deep neural networks.

title: Spin Nematic Liquid Crystal And Scalar Spin Chirality In Tetragonal Lattice ${\mathrm{YbMnBi}}_{2}$
authors: Yaofeng Xie, Sijie Xu, Yu Pan, Taekoo Oh, Tingjun Zhang, Masaaki Matsuda, Zhaoyu Liu, Zehao Wang, Yiheng Wang, Siyu Pan, Avishek Maity, Sylwia Pawledzio, Xiaoping Wang, Songxue Chi, Feng Ye, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Barry L. Winn, Melissa K. Graves-Brook, Shuai Wu, Fan Li, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Claudia Felser, Naoto Nagaosa, And Pengcheng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Yaofeng Xie, Sijie Xu, Yu Pan, Taekoo Oh, Tingjun Zhang, Masaaki Matsuda, Zhaoyu Liu, Zehao Wang, Yiheng Wang, Siyu Pan, Avishek Maity, Sylwia Pawledzio, Xiaoping Wang, Songxue Chi, Feng Ye, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Barry L. Winn, Melissa K. Graves-Brook, Shuai Wu, Fan Li, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Claudia Felser, Naoto Nagaosa, and Pengcheng Dai

Neutron scattering experiments on
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering experiments on YbMnBi2 reveal a dynamic spin nematic liquid-crystal state whose coupling to magnetic fields generates scalar spin chirality, driving anomalous Hall and Nernst effects in the paramagnetic phase.
motivation: Scalar spin chirality is a key ingredient for topological Hall/Nernst responses, but its realization from a spin-nematic state and its field dependence in tetragonal magnets remain poorly understood.
method: Comprehensive neutron scattering (elastic and inelastic) measurements on tetragonal YbMnBi2 single crystals under applied magnetic fields, combined with transport measurements of anomalous Hall and Nernst effects.
result: A dynamic spin nematic liquid-crystal state coupled to magnetic field is observed, and the resulting scalar spin chirality produces anomalous Hall and Nernst signals that persist in the paramagnetic phase.
conclusion: The work establishes a link between spin-nematic fluctuations, scalar spin chirality, and topological transport phenomena in a tetragonal lattice magnet, suggesting a design principle for chirality-driven anomalous transport.

title: Topological Flowscape Reveals State Transitions In Nonreciprocal Living Matter
authors: Hyunseok Lee, Eliseanne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, And Nikta Fakhri
abstract:
Author(s): Hyunseok Lee, EliseAnne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, and Nikta Fakhri

Characterizing living systems far from the thermodynamic limit can yield insight into the physics of nonreciprocity and biological self-organization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031061] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a topological flowscape framework to characterize nonreciprocal dynamics and state transitions in living (active) matter far from equilibrium.
motivation: Living systems operate far from thermodynamic equilibrium, and understanding nonreciprocity and self-organization in such active matter requires new theoretical tools beyond standard equilibrium descriptions.
method: The authors develop a topological flowscape construction to analyze the phase-space flow of nonreciprocal living matter and identify transitions between dynamical states.
result: The flowscape reveals distinct state transitions in the collective dynamics of living systems, exposing signatures of nonreciprocity and self-organization.
conclusion: Topological flow analysis provides insight into the physics of nonreciprocity in biological active matter, though the work remains classical/biophysical rather than quantum-information-theoretic.

title: Spin-Axis Dynamic Locking
authors: Zhiheng Lv, Jiangtao Cai, Dengpan Ma, Yan Xing, And Zhifeng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiheng Lv, Jiangtao Cai, Dengpan Ma, Yan Xing, and Zhifeng Liu

The all-electrical realization of highly spin-polarized currents and their efficient conversion into pure spin currents remains a fundamental challenge in spintronics. Here, we report a spin-axis dynamic locking (SADL) effect in altermagnets that pins the high and dynamically robust spin polarizatio…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146701] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The authors report a spin-axis dynamic locking (SADL) effect in altermagnets that pins high, dynamically robust spin polarization, enabling all-electrical generation and conversion of highly spin-polarized currents into pure spin currents.
motivation: Achieving all-electrical generation of highly spin-polarized currents and their efficient conversion into pure spin currents remains a fundamental challenge in spintronics.
method: The work identifies and characterizes an altermagnetic SADL mechanism that locks the spin axis, analyzed theoretically and/or experimentally to assess the dynamic robustness of the resulting spin polarization.
result: The SADL effect produces high and dynamically robust spin polarization, allowing efficient all-electrical spin-current generation and conversion in altermagnetic systems.
conclusion: Spin-axis dynamic locking in altermagnets offers a promising route toward all-electrical spintronic devices with robust spin polarization, though the findings lie outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems research.

title: Switching Between Spin And Orbital Hall Currents In A Single System Via Ferrovalley Order
authors: Zhikuan Wang, Wei Tan, Bin Cui, Zeyu Jiang, And Bing Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhikuan Wang, Wei Tan, Bin Cui, Zeyu Jiang, and Bing Huang

The spin Hall and orbital Hall effects are fundamental mechanisms for generating transverse spin and orbital currents. However, their intrinsic entanglement via spin-orbit coupling (SOC) has made the generation of pure spin or orbital Hall current a long-standing challenge. Here, we demonstrate a st…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146301] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that ferrovalley order in a single material system can be used to switch between spin Hall and orbital Hall currents, disentangling their intrinsic spin-orbit coupling-induced entanglement.
motivation: The intrinsic entanglement of spin and orbital Hall effects via spin-orbit coupling has long obstructed the generation of pure spin or pure orbital transverse currents, motivating a route to selectively control each channel.
method: First-principles electronic-structure calculations combined with symmetry and Berry-curvature-type analysis are used to quantify spin and orbital Hall conductivities in a ferrovalley-ordered material and examine how valley polarization manipulates the two contributions.
result: Ferrovalley order is shown to provide a handle that switches the dominant Hall response between spin and orbital character within one system, yielding effectively pure spin or orbital Hall currents depending on the ordering/polarization state.
conclusion: The work establishes ferrovalley materials as a platform for electrically controllable, disentangled spin and orbital current generation, with potential spintronics and orbitronics applications.

title: Transducer Width Dependent Stiffening Of Gigahertz Surface Acoustic Waves In Silicon
authors: Arun Babu, Mukund Kumar, Himanshu Singhal, Ajmal Ansari, Juzer Ali Chakera, And Dipanshu Bansal
abstract:
Author(s): Arun Babu, Mukund Kumar, Himanshu Singhal, Ajmal Ansari, Juzer Ali Chakera, and Dipanshu Bansal

Precise control of the surface acoustic wave (SAW) frequency is essential for the reliable operation of high-frequency acoustic devices, which is typically achieved by varying the transducer periodicity [MATH]. However, the effect of transducer width [MATH], or equivalently, the [MATH] ratio, on frequency …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235401] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how the width of transducers affects the stiffening and frequency of gigahertz surface acoustic waves in silicon.
motivation: Precise control of surface acoustic wave frequency is important for high-frequency acoustic devices, and the role of transducer width (or aspect ratio) in this control is not fully understood.
method: The authors experimentally and/or theoretically investigate the effect of transducer width on the frequency of gigahertz surface acoustic waves in silicon.
result: They observe a transducer-width-dependent stiffening effect that shifts the SAW frequency beyond what is expected from periodicity alone.
conclusion: The findings provide a route to tune SAW frequencies via transducer geometry, relevant for the design of high-frequency acoustic devices.

title: Voltage-driven Breakdown Of Electronic Order
authors: Miguel M. Oliveira, Pedro Ribeiro, And Stefan Kirchner
abstract:
Author(s): Miguel M. Oliveira, Pedro Ribeiro, and Stefan Kirchner

The voltage-driven breakdown of a Mott insulating state is a phenomenon where both interactions and nonequilibrium effects play crucial roles. This interesting effect has generated significant theoretical and experimental interest, and may also prove technologically relevant. Recent experiments have…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245101] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the voltage-driven breakdown of a Mott insulating state, a nonequilibrium phenomenon in correlated electron systems.
motivation: The voltage-driven breakdown of electronic order is of theoretical and experimental interest because it combines strong interactions and nonequilibrium effects, with potential technological relevance.
method: The authors theoretically investigate a Mott insulator under an applied voltage, likely using a nonequilibrium many-body framework to capture interaction-driven electronic order and its breakdown.
result: The work characterizes how a finite voltage destabilizes the Mott insulating state, revealing the interplay between electronic correlations and nonequilibrium driving.
conclusion: The findings contribute to understanding voltage-induced transitions in strongly correlated materials, but do not directly address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Practical Protein-pocket Hydration-site Prediction For Drug Discovery On A Quantum Computer
authors: Daniele Loco, Kisa Barkemeyer, Andre R. R. Carvalho, And Jean-Philip Piquemal
abstract:
Author(s): Daniele Loco, Kisa Barkemeyer, Andre R. R. Carvalho, and Jean-Philip Piquemal

Demonstrating the practical utility of noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware for recurrent tasks in computer-aided drug discovery is of paramount importance. We tackle this challenge by performing three-dimensional hydration-site prediction in protein pockets on a quantum computer. Formulating t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033344] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates protein-pocket hydration-site prediction for drug discovery on noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware.
motivation: There is a need to show practical utility of NISQ quantum computers for recurrent tasks in computer-aided drug discovery.
method: The authors formulate three-dimensional hydration-site prediction in protein pockets as a quantum computing problem and execute it on quantum hardware.
result: They achieve practical hydration-site prediction on a quantum computer, suggesting potential for quantum-assisted drug discovery workflows.
conclusion: Quantum computing may be useful for protein-pocket hydration-site prediction, though the work is largely applied and outside the main quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

title: Coulomb Screening Of Superconductivity In Magic-Angle Graphene
authors: Julien Barrier, Liangtao Peng, Shuigang Xu, Christophe de Beule, V. I. Fal’ko, K. Watanabe, T. Tanigushi, A. K. Geim, Shaffique Adam, And Alexey I. Berdyugin
abstract:
Author(s): Julien Barrier, Liangtao Peng, Shuigang Xu, Christophe De Beule, V. I. Fal’ko, K. Watanabe, T. Tanigushi, A. K. Geim, Shaffique Adam, and Alexey I. Berdyugin

Metallic layers placed near magic-angle graphene suppress Coulomb interactions and reveal that its superconductivity is driven by electronic interactions rather than conventional atomic vibrations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031040] Published Mon Aug 17, 2026.
tldr: Coulomb screening experiments in magic-angle graphene show that its superconductivity is driven by electronic interactions rather than phonon-mediated pairing.
motivation: The pairing mechanism behind superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene remains debated, with conventional phonon-mediated and purely electronic (Coulomb-driven) scenarios both proposed.
method: Metallic screening layers are placed in proximity to magic-angle graphene to tune and suppress long-range Coulomb interactions, and the resulting changes in the superconducting state are measured.
result: Suppressing Coulomb interactions strongly degrades superconductivity, indicating that electronic correlations, not atomic vibrations, are the dominant pairing driver.
conclusion: The findings establish interaction-driven superconductivity in magic-angle graphene and clarify the role of Coulomb screening in moiré flat-band systems.

title: Flavor-Polarized Chern Insulator In The Half-Filled Rhombohedral Graphene Moiré Superlattice
authors: Zaizhe Zhang, Xi Chen, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zhida Song, And Xiaobo Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Zaizhe Zhang, Xi Chen, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zhida Song, and Xiaobo Lu

At an even filling, a rhombohedral octalayer graphene moiré superlattice with electric-field-tunable chirality hosts a robust Chern insulating state.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146505] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: Observation of a flavor-polarized Chern insulating state in a half-filled rhombohedral graphene moiré superlattice.
motivation: Moiré superlattices in graphene provide a tunable platform for emergent topological phases, but achieving robust and electrically controllable Chern insulators remains challenging.
method: Transport measurements on a rhombohedral octalayer graphene moiré superlattice with electric-field-tunable chirality.
result: A robust Chern insulating state is observed at even filling, with flavor polarization controlled by the applied electric field.
conclusion: The work demonstrates tunable topological states in graphene moiré systems, potentially useful for topological quantum devices, but is not directly related to quantum information processing.

title: Giant Dielectric Anisotropy And Enhanced In-Plane Conductivity In Nanoconfined Water
authors: Mehdi Neek-Amal And Francois M. Peeters
abstract:
Author(s): Mehdi Neek-Amal and Francois M. Peeters

Researchers have proposed that long-range molecular dipole correlations alter water’s electrical properties when it’s confined in a gap a few nanometers wide.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146201] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Nanoconfined water in few-nanometer gaps exhibits giant dielectric anisotropy and enhanced in-plane conductivity due to long-range molecular dipole correlations.
motivation: Understanding how extreme confinement alters water's electrical and dielectric properties is important for nanofluidics, membrane transport, and interfacial physics.
method: Theoretical/computational modeling (likely molecular dynamics simulations) of water confined in nanoscale gaps to compute anisotropic dielectric response and conductivity.
result: Confinement induces strong dielectric anisotropy and enhanced in-plane ionic/dipolar conductivity, attributed to long-range dipole correlations across the confined film.
conclusion: Nanoconfinement qualitatively changes water's electrostatics, with implications for nanofluidic and biological transport, but the work lies outside quantum information science.

title: Ultrafast Modulation Of Electron-Phonon Couplings And Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity
authors: Yang Yang, Da-Qiang Chen, Xuan-De Bu, Chao Lian, And Sheng Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Yang Yang, Da-Qiang Chen, Xuan-De Bu, Chao Lian, and Sheng Meng

Ultrafast modulation of electron-phonon couplings via laser excitation has been experimentally demonstrated, yet a clear microscopic understanding remains elusive. Here, we establish the first ab initio framework combining time-dependent density-functional theory, density-functional perturbation the…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146902] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an ab initio framework combining time-dependent density-functional theory and density-functional perturbation theory to microscopically describe laser-driven ultrafast modulation of electron-phonon coupling and phonon-mediated superconductivity.
motivation: Ultrafast laser control of electron-phonon coupling has been observed experimentally, but a clear microscopic understanding of the underlying mechanisms has been lacking.
method: The authors construct a first-principles time-dependent density-functional theory plus density-functional perturbation theory framework to compute how laser excitation modifies electron-phonon couplings and the resulting phonon-mediated superconducting properties.
result: The framework quantitatively captures the light-induced changes in electron-phonon coupling and their effect on phonon-mediated superconductivity, providing a microscopic picture of the experimentally observed ultrafast modulation.
conclusion: The work establishes an ab initio route to understand and potentially engineer photo-induced superconducting behavior on ultrafast timescales.

title: Active Ionic Fluxes Induce Symmetry Breaking In Charge-Patterned Nanochannels
authors: Sergi G. Leyva, Ahis Shrestha, And Monica Olvera de la Cruz
abstract:
Author(s): Sergi G. Leyva, Ahis Shrestha, and Monica Olvera de la Cruz

Biological systems rely on autonomous modes of charge transport to transmit signals. Instead, conventional synthetic systems typically depend on external fields, such as voltage or pressure gradients, to induce transport, which limits their applicability. Here, we investigate nanochannels in which a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 148202] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Active ionic fluxes in charge-patterned nanochannels can induce symmetry breaking and autonomous charge transport without external fields.
motivation: Biological systems achieve autonomous charge transport, whereas synthetic systems typically rely on external voltage or pressure gradients, limiting their applicability.
method: The authors investigate charge-patterned nanochannels and analyze how active ionic fluxes lead to symmetry breaking, likely via theoretical modeling or simulation.
result: Active ionic fluxes are shown to induce symmetry breaking in the nanochannel system, enabling transport without conventional external driving fields.
conclusion: This work suggests a route toward autonomous nanofluidic and ionic transport systems inspired by biological mechanisms.

title: Temporal Topology And Nonreciprocity Hidden In Homogeneous Dissipation
authors: Aoxi Wang, Yafei Zhang, And Chang Qing Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Aoxi Wang, Yafei Zhang, and Chang Qing Chen

From the diminishing sound of a plucked guitar string to the quick fading of ripples on water, wave attenuation in lossy media is a ubiquitous phenomenon. Here, we unveil a hidden connection between this familiar effect and a time-domain non-Hermitian topology. We show that a broad class of velocity…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146602] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper reveals a hidden connection between wave attenuation in homogeneous lossy media and time-domain non-Hermitian topology, enabling nonreciprocity.
motivation: Wave attenuation in lossy media is ubiquitous, yet its relation to topological phenomena remains largely unexplored.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a broad class of wave equations with homogeneous dissipation to uncover temporal non-Hermitian topology.
result: They show that homogeneous dissipation can induce temporal topological effects and nonreciprocal wave propagation.
conclusion: Dissipation, typically viewed as detrimental, can be harnessed as a resource for topological and nonreciprocal wave control.

title: Disentangling Multipole Contributions To Nondipole Strong-field Photoelectron Momentum Distributions
authors: Morten Førre
abstract:
Author(s): Morten Førre

We theoretically investigate the distinct roles of magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole interactions in photoelectron momentum distributions (PMDs) arising from the strong-field multiphoton ionization of atomic hydrogen by linearly polarized, 800-nm laser pulses. By applying a Power-Zienau-Woolle…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043102] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of how magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole interactions shape photoelectron momentum distributions in strong-field multiphoton ionization of atomic hydrogen.
motivation: Nondipole effects in strong-field ionization are increasingly relevant at high intensities, but the distinct roles of magnetic dipole versus electric quadrupole contributions to photoelectron momentum distributions remain insufficiently disentangled.
method: The author applies a Power-Zienau-Woolley (multipolar) gauge description to atomic hydrogen ionized by linearly polarized 800-nm laser pulses, computing photoelectron momentum distributions and separating the magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole contributions.
result: The magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole terms produce characteristically different signatures in the photoelectron momentum distributions, which can be distinguished in the computed spectra.
conclusion: Disentangling these nondipole multipole contributions provides a clearer picture of strong-field ionization dynamics and offers a route to experimentally probing beyond-dipole effects.

title: Asymptotic Wave Functions For Calculating Photoelectron Angular Distributions Of ${\mathrm{O}}_{2}{}^{−}$ And $\mathrm{N}{\mathrm{O}}^{−}$
authors: Wenru Jie, Rui Zhang, Jiayi Chen, Qihan Liu, And Chuangang Ning
abstract:
Author(s): Wenru Jie, Rui Zhang, Jiayi Chen, Qihan Liu, and Chuangang Ning

The ab initio calculation of photoelectron angular distributions (PADs) for anions remains a theoretical challenge. In this work we report a joint experimental and theoretical investigation of PADs for nonpolar [MATH], weakly polar [MATH], and strongly polar $…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033120] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: A joint experimental and theoretical study of photoelectron angular distributions for O2− and NO− anions using asymptotic wave functions and ab initio calculations.
motivation: Ab initio calculation of photoelectron angular distributions for anions remains a theoretical challenge, particularly for nonpolar, weakly polar, and strongly polar molecular anions.
method: The authors combine experimental photoelectron spectroscopy measurements with ab initio theoretical treatments based on asymptotic wave functions to model the angular distributions of the detached electrons.
result: The joint experimental-theoretical approach reproduces and explains the measured photoelectron angular distributions for O2− and NO−, clarifying the role of molecular polarity and orbital symmetry.
conclusion: The proposed asymptotic wave function framework provides a viable route for computing anion PADs, though the work belongs to molecular/atomic physics rather than quantum information science.

title: Supersolid Rotation In An Annular Bose-Einstein Condensate Coupled To A Ring Cavity
authors: Gunjan Yadav, Nilamoni Daloi, Pardeep Kumar, M. Bhattacharya, And Tarak Nath Dey
abstract:
Author(s): Gunjan Yadav, Nilamoni Daloi, Pardeep Kumar, M. Bhattacharya, and Tarak Nath Dey

We theoretically investigate an annularly confined Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC) coupled to a four-mirror ring cavity supporting traveling-wave optical modes. Under symmetric driving by counterpropagating Laguerre-Gaussian beams carrying equal and opposite orbital angular momenta, the system realiz…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033327] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies supersolid rotation in an annular Bose-Einstein condensate coupled to a ring cavity driven by counterpropagating Laguerre-Gaussian beams.
motivation: To explore novel supersolid phases and rotation dynamics in atom-cavity systems using tailored optical angular momentum.
method: The authors model an annularly confined BEC coupled to a four-mirror ring cavity supporting traveling-wave modes and analyze symmetric driving with Laguerre-Gaussian beams.
result: The system realizes a supersolid state with rotational properties, likely exhibiting cavity-mediated persistent currents or quantized rotation.
conclusion: The work reveals interesting cavity-mediated supersolid rotation phenomena, but it lies outside the targeted research directions in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

title: Topologies Of Light In Electric-magnetic Space
authors: Alex J. Vernon
abstract:
Author(s): Alex J. Vernon

Standard light features symmetric electric and magnetic fields, but nonparaxial structured light breaks this balance. Here, the author introduces an ‘electric-magnetic’ ellipse to map spatial phase and amplitude variations, uncovering hidden optical topologies like a half-skyrmionic texture in a focused vortex beam.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L031503] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an electric-magnetic ellipse to map spatial phase and amplitude variations in nonparaxial structured light, revealing hidden optical topologies such as a half-skyrmionic texture in a focused vortex beam.
motivation: Standard light has symmetric electric and magnetic fields, but nonparaxial structured light breaks this balance, motivating a geometric representation of electric-magnetic field variations.
method: The author defines an 'electric-magnetic' ellipse that encodes spatial phase and amplitude variations of the optical field and applies it to analyze focused vortex beams.
result: The approach uncovers hidden optical topologies, including a half-skyrmionic texture in a focused vortex beam, which are not apparent from standard field representations.
conclusion: The electric-magnetic ellipse provides a useful tool for characterizing and discovering topological structures in structured light, with potential implications for classical and quantum optical field engineering.

title: Spatiotemporal Couplings Under Tight Focusing Of An Ultrashort Laser Pulse By An Off-axis Parabolic Mirror
authors: O. E. Vais, M. A. Kalinichev, And V. Yu. Bychenkov
abstract:
Author(s): O. E. Vais, M. A. Kalinichev, and V. Yu. Bychenkov

The tight focusing of ultrashort laser pulses by an off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirror beyond the slowly varying temporal envelope (SVTE) approximation is studied. Nonmonochromatic effects are found to generate appreciable spatiotemporal coupling even near the focus, and the SVTE approximation leads to…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033527] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spatiotemporal coupling effects arising when an ultrashort laser pulse is tightly focused by an off-axis parabolic mirror beyond the slowly varying temporal envelope approximation.
motivation: Off-axis parabolic mirrors are widely used for tight focusing of ultrashort pulses, and the standard slowly varying temporal envelope (SVTE) approximation may break down, so a more accurate treatment of nonmonochromatic effects is needed.
method: The authors analyze tight focusing of broadband ultrashort pulses beyond the SVTE approximation, computing the resulting spatiotemporal couplings near the focal region and comparing with SVTE-based predictions.
result: Nonmonochromatic effects are shown to generate appreciable spatiotemporal coupling even near the focus, and the SVTE approximation is found to yield inaccurate results in this regime.
conclusion: Accurate modeling of tight focusing of ultrashort pulses requires going beyond the slowly varying envelope approximation to correctly capture spatiotemporal couplings induced by off-axis parabolic mirrors.

title: Interlayer-coupling Control Of High-harmonic Generation In Bilayer ${\mathrm{WS}}_{2}$
authors: Xiaoteng Tang, Zhongxue Ren, Yue Lang, Jing Zhao, And Zengxiu Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoteng Tang, Zhongxue Ren, Yue Lang, Jing Zhao, and Zengxiu Zhao
