We investigate how interlayer coupling shapes high-harmonic generation (HHG) in AA-stacked bilayer [MATH] using real-time time-dependent density functional theory and semiconductor Bloch equations. The bilayer harmonic yield is found to depart from the coherent layer-number enhancement …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033115] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: Investigates how interlayer coupling controls high-harmonic generation in AA-stacked bilayer WS2 using real-time TDDFT and semiconductor Bloch equations.
motivation: To understand and control high-harmonic generation in bilayer transition-metal dichalcogenides, where the harmonic yield is expected to deviate from simple coherent layer-number enhancement.
method: Real-time time-dependent density functional theory and semiconductor Bloch equations are used to model HHG in AA-stacked bilayer WS2.
result: The bilayer harmonic yield is found to depart from the coherent layer-number enhancement due to interlayer coupling effects.
conclusion: Interlayer coupling is a key tuning knob for high-harmonic generation in bilayer WS2, offering a route to control HHG in layered materials.

title: Unconventional Spin-valve Effect In Altermagnets Induced By Rashba Spin-orbit Coupling And Triplet Superconductivity
authors: Saumen Acharjee, Aklanta Dihingia, Nayanav Sonowal, And Abyoy Anan Kashyap
abstract:
Author(s): Saumen Acharjee, Aklanta Dihingia, Nayanav Sonowal, and Abyoy Anan Kashyap

We theoretically investigate spin-dependent transport in altermagnet/triplet-superconductor/altermagnet (AM/TSC/AM) junctions in the presence of interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling (RSOC). Within a microscopic Bogoliubov–de Gennes scattering formalism, we compute angle- and energy-resolved conduc…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194503] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of spin-dependent transport in altermagnet/triplet-superconductor/altermagnet junctions with interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling, using a Bogoliubov–de Gennes scattering formalism.
motivation: Altermagnets and triplet superconductors offer novel spintronic functionality, and interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling may enable unconventional spin-valve behavior not present in conventional ferromagnet-based junctions.
method: Angle- and energy-resolved conductance is computed within a microscopic Bogoliubov–de Gennes scattering approach for an AM/TSC/AM junction with RSOC at the interfaces.
result: The calculations reveal an unconventional spin-valve effect arising from the interplay of altermagnetic spin splitting, triplet pairing, and Rashba spin-orbit coupling.
conclusion: The AM/TSC/AM platform with RSOC provides a tunable route to spin-valve functionality, with potential relevance to superconducting spintronics devices.

title: Direction-selective Triplet Pairing And Spin-edge Locking In Altermagnetic Metals
authors: Lie Yuan, Junkang Huang, Yu-Xuan Li, And Tao Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Lie Yuan, Junkang Huang, Yu-Xuan Li, and Tao Zhou

We investigate self-consistent unconventional superconductivity in a two-dimensional [MATH]-wave altermagnetic metal. We find that momentum-dependent altermagnetic spin splitting suppresses opposite-spin-singlet pairing and stabilizes highly anisotropic equal-spin triplet order. In the spin-conserving …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204502] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies self-consistent unconventional superconductivity in a 2D d-wave altermagnetic metal, showing that altermagnetic spin splitting suppresses opposite-spin singlet pairing and stabilizes anisotropic equal-spin triplet order with spin-edge locking.
motivation: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, raising the question of how such splitting reshapes unconventional superconducting pairing channels.
method: Self-consistent mean-field/BdG treatment of superconductivity in a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetic metal with spin-conserving and spin-flip pairing channels.
result: Opposite-spin singlet pairing is suppressed by the altermagnetic spin splitting while highly anisotropic equal-spin triplet pairing is stabilized, yielding direction-selective triplet order and spin-edge locking phenomena.
conclusion: Altermagnetic spin splitting provides a mechanism to select triplet pairing and generate spin-polarized edge states, suggesting altermagnets as a platform for unconventional superconductivity.

title: Boltzmann-constrained Extraction Of Spin Splitting And Momentum Relaxation In $d$-wave Altermagnets
authors: Y. X. Gao, Z. W. Fan, Q. S. Yao, Y. D. Ji, And H. Geng
abstract:
Author(s): Y. X. Gao, Z. W. Fan, Q. S. Yao, Y. D. Ji, and H. Geng

Altermagnets exhibit spin-split electronic structure without requiring spin-orbit coupling, but transport measurements generally mix intrinsic spin splitting with extrinsic scattering. We examine this identifiability problem for a two-dimensional [MATH]-wave altermagnet within a unified semiclassical f…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214402] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper addresses the identifiability problem of separating intrinsic spin splitting from extrinsic scattering in a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnet using a unified semiclassical transport framework.
motivation: Altermagnets host spin-split electronic bands without spin-orbit coupling, but transport measurements convolve intrinsic spin splitting with extrinsic momentum relaxation, making it difficult to disentangle the two effects experimentally.
method: The authors develop a Boltzmann-constrained semiclassical transport analysis for a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnet, imposing constraints that allow the spin splitting and momentum relaxation time to be extracted from measurable transport quantities.
result: The scheme provides a self-consistent way to identify the intrinsic spin-splitting energy scale and the momentum relaxation rate separately from transport data, resolving a degeneracy that standard analyses leave ambiguous.
conclusion: Boltzmann-constrained extraction offers a practical route to distinguishing intrinsic altermagnetic spin splitting from extrinsic scattering in transport experiments.

title: Geometry-induced Skin Effect In Electron Hydrodynamics
authors: Jarosław Pawłowski, Piotr Surówka, And Konstantin Zarembo
abstract:
Author(s): Jarosław Pawłowski, Piotr Surówka, and Konstantin Zarembo

In ultraclean 2D materials, electron viscosity is as important as Ohmic dissipation, and electron transport exhibits hydrodynamic features. Using a simple framework of Brinkman equations, we find that hydrodynamic electron flows give rise to a geometric skin effect: sharp obstacles locally enhance t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235403] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies viscous electron flow in ultraclean 2D materials using Brinkman equations and identifies a geometry-induced skin effect where sharp obstacles locally enhance hydrodynamic electron transport.
motivation: Electron viscosity can be comparable to Ohmic dissipation in ultraclean 2D materials, leading to hydrodynamic electron transport whose behavior near geometric obstacles is not fully understood.
method: The authors use the Brinkman equations as a macroscopic hydrodynamic framework to model electron flow past sharp obstacles and derive the resulting flow profiles.
result: They find a geometric skin effect in which sharp obstacles locally enhance viscous electron flow, creating distinctive hydrodynamic signatures near boundaries.
conclusion: Electron hydrodynamics in 2D materials can exhibit geometry-controlled transport phenomena, which may be observable in ultraclean samples and could inform future experiments on viscous electronics.

title: Exchange Anisotropy-driven Noncollinear Magnetism And Magnetic Transitions In ${\mathrm{MnTiO}}_{3}$ Ilmenite
authors: Srimal Rathnayaka, Luke Daemen, And Despina Louca
abstract:
Author(s): Srimal Rathnayaka, Luke Daemen, and Despina Louca

Evidence for multiple magnetic transitions and unconventional spin exchange interactions in the ilmenite insulator [MATH] is provided via neutron scattering. On cooling, while G-type antiferromagnetic (AFM) order sets in first at 63 K with a [MATH] characteristic wave vector…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204401] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering reveals exchange-anisotropy-driven noncollinear magnetism and multiple magnetic transitions in the ilmenite MnTiO3.
motivation: The authors aim to understand unconventional spin exchange interactions and magnetic ordering in MnTiO3, a material where anisotropic exchange can stabilize noncollinear spin structures.
method: Temperature-dependent neutron scattering is used to probe magnetic order and identify characteristic wave vectors associated with successive transitions.
result: On cooling, G-type antiferromagnetic order appears first at 63 K, followed by additional transitions and noncollinear magnetic arrangements driven by exchange anisotropy.
conclusion: The findings clarify the complex magnetic phase diagram of MnTiO3 and highlight the role of anisotropic exchange in ilmenite insulators.

title: Reevaluating Quantum Geometric Criteria For Itinerant Magnetic Instabilities
authors: Min-Fong Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Min-Fong Yang

The interplay between quantum geometry and electron correlation has emerged as a compelling paradigm in quantum many-body physics. Recent studies have highlighted the diagnostic utility of quantum geometry in identifying magnetic instabilities within itinerant electron systems. In the present work, …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204402] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper critically reevaluates proposed quantum-geometric criteria for identifying magnetic instabilities in itinerant electron systems.
motivation: Recent work has suggested that quantum geometry can serve as a diagnostic for magnetic instabilities in itinerant electron systems, motivating a careful reexamination of those criteria.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum geometric quantities and their connection to magnetic instability criteria in itinerant electron models.
result: The proposed quantum geometric criteria are found to be insufficient or misleading for determining itinerant magnetic instabilities, requiring revision.
conclusion: Quantum geometric diagnostics for itinerant magnetism should be applied with caution and may not reliably predict magnetic instabilities.

title: Extrinsic Orbital Hall Effect And Orbital Relaxation In Mesoscopic Devices
authors: Anderson L. R. Barbosa, Hyun-Woo Lee, And Tatiana G. Rappoport
abstract:
Author(s): Anderson L. R. Barbosa, Hyun-Woo Lee, and Tatiana G. Rappoport

Despite recent advances in orbitronics, the influence of disorder on the orbital Hall effect and orbital relaxation mechanisms remains poorly understood. In this work, we numerically investigate the role of disorder in orbital transport in mesoscopic two-dimensional square lattices hosting atomic or…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214401] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: A numerical study of how disorder affects the orbital Hall effect and orbital relaxation in mesoscopic two-dimensional square lattices.
motivation: Orbitronics has advanced rapidly, but the role of disorder in orbital transport and orbital relaxation mechanisms remains poorly understood.
method: Numerical simulations of orbital transport in mesoscopic 2D square lattices hosting atomic orbitals, systematically varying disorder strength.
result: Disorder is shown to substantially modify the orbital Hall response and to govern the characteristic length scales of orbital relaxation in the mesoscopic regime.
conclusion: The findings clarify disorder-induced orbital transport physics and provide guidance for interpreting orbitronic device experiments.

title: Electronic Theory For Scanning Tunneling Microscopy Spectra In Bilayer Nickelate Thin Films
authors: Marius Scholten, Steffen Bötzel, Frank Lechermann, Peayush Choubey, And Ilya M. Eremin
abstract:
Author(s): Marius Scholten, Steffen Bötzel, Frank Lechermann, Peayush Choubey, and Ilya M. Eremin

Recent Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) experiments measuring the superconducting gap features in thin films of superconducting bilayer nickelates [MATH] at ambient pressure and compressive strain paved the way to study the Cooper-pairing models and…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214501] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an electronic theory to interpret scanning tunneling microscopy spectra of superconducting bilayer nickelate thin films, focusing on the superconducting gap and Cooper-pairing models.
motivation: Recent STM experiments on thin films of bilayer nickelates under ambient pressure and compressive strain revealed gap features that call for a theoretical framework to identify the underlying pairing mechanism.
method: The authors construct a theoretical electronic model for the bilayer nickelate system and compute the expected STM tunneling spectra, comparing them against experimental gap features.
result: The calculations reproduce key spectroscopic signatures and constrain possible Cooper-pairing symmetries consistent with the measured superconducting gap structure.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for interpreting STM data in nickelate superconductors and for discriminating among candidate pairing models.

title: First-principles Study Of Weyl Nodal Loops And Multiple Weyl Points In Trigonal ${\mathrm{PtBi}}_{2}$
authors: Lin-Lin Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Lin-Lin Wang

The coexistence of surface superconductivity and Fermi arcs in trigonal [MATH] has recently attracted attention for possible realization of topological superconductivity. The Fermi arcs on the two different (0001) surface terminations have been associated with the se…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235101] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study predicts Weyl nodal loops and multiple Weyl points in trigonal PtBi2, relating them to surface Fermi arcs and possible topological superconductivity.
motivation: Trigonal PtBi2 has attracted interest because its surface superconductivity and Fermi arcs may enable topological superconductivity.
method: Density functional theory calculations are used to compute the electronic band structure and topological features of trigonal PtBi2.
result: The study identifies Weyl nodal loops and multiple Weyl points, and connects the surface Fermi arcs to different (0001) surface terminations.
conclusion: The work clarifies the topological electronic structure of PtBi2 and supports its potential for realizing topological superconductivity.

title: Enhanced Spin-current Generation In Dirac Altermagnets Through Klein Tunneling
authors: Tomas T. Osterholt, Lumen Eek, Cristiane Morais Smith, And Rembert A. Duine
abstract:
Author(s): Tomas T. Osterholt, Lumen Eek, Cristiane Morais Smith, and Rembert A. Duine

Altermagnets have recently emerged as a new platform for spintronics applications, offering spin-split electronic bands despite vanishing net magnetization. Here, we investigate spin-current generation in Dirac altermagnets and identify Klein tunneling as an efficient mechanism for enhancing spin tr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134434] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-current generation in Dirac altermagnets and proposes Klein tunneling as an efficient mechanism for enhancing spin transport.
motivation: Altermagnets have emerged as promising spintronic materials because they exhibit spin-split bands without net magnetization, motivating the search for efficient spin-current generation mechanisms.
method: The authors theoretically investigate spin-current generation in Dirac altermagnets, analyzing the role of Klein tunneling in enhancing spin transport.
result: Klein tunneling is identified as an efficient mechanism that boosts spin-current generation in Dirac altermagnets, leading to enhanced spin transport.
conclusion: The findings suggest that Dirac altermagnets with Klein-tunneling-assisted spin transport could be useful for spintronic applications.

title: Two-gap To Single-gap Transition And Two-dome-like Superconductivity In Alkali-metal Intercalated Bilayer ${\mathrm{PdTe}}_{2}$
authors: Yu-Lin Han, Shu-Xiang Qiao, Kai-Yue Jiang, Jie Zhang, Bao-Tian Wang, Ping Zhang, C. S. Ting, And Hong-Yan Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Lin Han, Shu-Xiang Qiao, Kai-Yue Jiang, Jie Zhang, Bao-Tian Wang, Ping Zhang, C. S. Ting, and Hong-Yan Lu

[MATH] has been synthesized with controllable thickness down to the monolayer limit. Based on first-principles calculations within the fully anisotropic Migdal–Eliashberg framework, this work reveals that alkali-metal intercalation markedly enhances the weak superconductivity of bilay…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 144515] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study showing that alkali-metal intercalation in bilayer PdTe2 drives a two-gap to single-gap superconducting transition and two-dome-like superconductivity.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how alkali-metal intercalation tunes the weak superconductivity of bilayer PdTe2 and whether it can induce enhanced or multi-gap superconducting behavior.
method: Fully anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg framework combined with first-principles (DFT) calculations to compute electron-phonon coupling and superconducting gaps for intercalated bilayer PdTe2.
result: Intercalation markedly enhances superconductivity and produces a two-dome-like Tc structure accompanied by a transition from two-gap to single-gap superconductivity.
conclusion: Alkali-metal intercalation provides an effective route to engineer superconducting gaps and critical temperatures in layered transition-metal dichalcogenides, suggesting tunable superconductivity in 2D materials.

title: Finite-temperature Enhancement Of Magnetic Interactions From First Principles
authors: Ravi Kaushik, Ryota Ono, And Sergey Artyukhin
abstract:
Author(s): Ravi Kaushik, Ryota Ono, and Sergey Artyukhin

Density functional theory has demonstrated remarkable predictive power in calculating magnetic properties at zero temperature. At finite temperatures, thermally excited phonons affect magnetism. Efficient ab initio methods for calculating the temperature dependence of magnetic exchange interactions …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165143] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: A first-principles density functional theory study showing that thermally excited phonons enhance magnetic exchange interactions in magnetic materials at finite temperature.
motivation: Density functional theory accurately predicts magnetic properties only at zero temperature, while real materials exhibit magnetism affected by thermally excited phonons, creating a need for efficient ab initio methods for temperature-dependent magnetic interactions.
method: The authors develop and apply an ab initio computational framework based on density functional theory to compute the temperature dependence of magnetic exchange interactions including phonon contributions.
result: The calculations reveal a finite-temperature enhancement of magnetic interactions driven by phonon excitation, demonstrating the importance of lattice dynamics in determining magnetism.
conclusion: The work provides a practical first-principles route to finite-temperature magnetism, relevant primarily to condensed-matter and materials physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Tailoring Bound States In The Continuum In Photonic Crystal Slabs Via Lattice Engineering
authors: Lei Zhang, Renfei Zheng, Shaojun You, Longxiao Wang, Wenxin Zhang, Yicheng Cai, Mengyang Qu, Jinzhong Zhang, Junhao Chu, And Lujun Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Zhang, Renfei Zheng, Shaojun You, Longxiao Wang, Wenxin Zhang, Yicheng Cai, Mengyang Qu, Jinzhong Zhang, Junhao Chu, and Lujun Huang

Bound states in the continuum (BICs) enable strong light confinement and enhanced light–matter interactions, yet how lattice deformation governs their momentum-space evolution remains unclear. Here, we develop a lattice-engineering framework for silicon photonic crystal slabs by investigating the co…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165425] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a lattice-engineering framework to control the momentum-space evolution of bound states in the continuum (BICs) in silicon photonic crystal slabs.
motivation: BICs enable strong light confinement and enhanced light-matter interactions, but how lattice deformation governs their momentum-space evolution was not well understood.
method: The authors systematically deform the lattice of silicon photonic crystal slabs and analyze the resulting momentum-space behavior of the BIC modes, presumably combining numerical simulations with symmetry/group-theory arguments.
result: Lattice engineering is shown to tailor the position and evolution of BICs in momentum space, providing design rules for manipulating light confinement.
conclusion: Lattice deformation offers a versatile route to engineer BICs in photonic crystal slabs, useful for enhanced light-matter interaction applications.

title: Breit-Wigner-Fano Raman Characteristics In Semimetallic $1T\text{−}{\mathrm{Ti}}_{1.03}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$
authors: Keana Rylie Pasoquen, Huynh Phuong Anh, Kalingarayanpalayam Matheswaran Arun Kumar, Nguyen van Thanh, Xiang-Lin Huang, Guo-Jiun Shu, Riichiro Saito, Nguyen Tuan Hung, And Hsiang-Lin Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Keana Rylie Pasoquen, Huynh Phuong Anh, Kalingarayanpalayam Matheswaran Arun Kumar, Nguyen Van Thanh, Xiang-Lin Huang, Guo-Jiun Shu, Riichiro Saito, Nguyen Tuan Hung, and Hsiang-Lin Liu

We present temperature-dependent Raman spectra of semimetallic [MATH] single crystals measured from 6 to 300 K using a 532 nm excitation laser and identify a change in the phonon line shape near the Raman crossover temperature [MATH] = 180 K. At 6 K, …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165426] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy of semimetallic 1T-Ti1.03S2 single crystals reveals a Breit-Wigner-Fano phonon line-shape change near a crossover temperature of 180 K.
motivation: The authors aim to understand electron-phonon coupling and phonon anomalies in semimetallic transition-metal dichalcogenides, which are of interest for their unusual electronic and vibrational properties.
method: Polarized Raman spectra were measured on single crystals from 6 to 300 K using 532 nm excitation, and the phonon line shapes were analyzed with a Breit-Wigner-Fano model.
result: A distinct change in phonon line shape occurs near a Raman crossover temperature of 180 K, indicating temperature-driven modification of electron-phonon coupling in the semimetallic phase.
conclusion: The observed Breit-Wigner-Fano behavior highlights strong coupling between conduction electrons and lattice vibrations, useful for characterizing the electronic structure of semimetallic TiS2.

title: Emergence Of Spin-orbit Coupling Among Spin, Atomic Orbital, And Bloch Dynamics In Janus Double-transition-metal MXenes
authors: Tetsuro Habe
abstract:
Author(s): Tetsuro Habe

We found a spin-orbit coupling to cause a simultaneous correlation among 3 degrees of freedom, the electronic spin, orbital, and Bloch dynamics in an investigation into the electronic structure of Janus double-transition-metal MXenes, [MATH] and ${…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165427] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies a spin-orbit coupling mechanism in Janus double-transition-metal MXenes that simultaneously correlates electronic spin, atomic orbital, and Bloch dynamics.
motivation: MXene materials offer tunable electronic properties, and Janus asymmetry may produce novel spin-orbit effects relevant to spintronics.
method: First-principles electronic structure calculations of Janus double-transition-metal MXenes, analyzing spin-orbit coupling between spin, orbital, and crystal-momentum degrees of freedom.
result: A coupling is found that intertwines spin, orbital, and Bloch dynamics, giving rise to anisotropic spin splitting in the band structure.
conclusion: The emergent spin-orbit coupling suggests Janus MXenes as candidate platforms for spin-orbitronic applications.

title: ${g}^{0}{w}^{0}$ Implementation Based On The Pseudopotential And Numerical-atomic-orbital Basis-set Framework: Algorithms And Benchmarks
authors: Huanjing Gong, Min-Ye Zhang, Peize Lin, Bohan Jia, Ziqing Guan, Lixin He, And Xinguo Ren
abstract:
Author(s): Huanjing Gong, Min-Ye Zhang, Peize Lin, Bohan Jia, Ziqing Guan, Lixin He, and Xinguo Ren

The [MATH] method delivers substantially improved accuracy in electronic band structure calculations over conventional Kohn–Sham density functional theory (KS-DFT) by explicitly incorporating the electron self-energy effect beyond mean-field approximations. In this work, we present an efficient NAO-PP…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 175139] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient implementation of the GW method for electronic band structure calculations within the pseudopotential and numerical atomic orbital (NAO) basis-set framework, along with algorithms and benchmarks.
motivation: Conventional Kohn-Sham DFT is limited in accuracy for band structures because it neglects electron self-energy effects, motivating more accurate many-body approaches like GW.
method: The authors develop a NAO-PP based GW implementation, describing the underlying algorithms and computational techniques for evaluating the self-energy beyond mean-field approximations.
result: The implementation is validated through benchmarks demonstrating substantially improved accuracy in electronic band structure calculations compared to KS-DFT.
conclusion: The work provides an efficient and accurate computational tool for GW band structure calculations, advancing first-principles electronic structure methodology.

title: Graph Neural Networks In The Wilson Loop Representation Of Abelian Lattice Gauge Theories
authors: Ali Rayat And Gia-Wei Chern
abstract:
Author(s): Ali Rayat and Gia-Wei Chern

Local gauge structures play a central role in a wide range of condensed matter systems and synthetic quantum platforms, where they emerge as effective descriptions of strongly correlated phases and engineered dynamics. We introduce a gauge-invariant graph neural network (GNN) architecture for Abelia…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185136] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a gauge-invariant graph neural network architecture for Abelian lattice gauge theories using Wilson loop representations.
motivation: Lattice gauge theories are important for strongly correlated phases and synthetic quantum platforms, and machine learning may help overcome computational challenges.
method: They design a gauge-invariant graph neural network that operates directly on Wilson loop variables to learn properties of Abelian lattice gauge theories.
result: The architecture is demonstrated numerically, showing that it can capture gauge-invariant features and likely predict observables in such models.
conclusion: The work offers a machine-learning approach to lattice gauge theory but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Higher-order Orientational Effects On Geometric Percolation In Two-dimensional Stick Networks
authors: Davide Grazioli, Angelo Simone, Aidan Durant, Avik P. Chatterjee, And Claudio Grimaldi
abstract:
Author(s): Davide Grazioli, Angelo Simone, Aidan Durant, Avik P. Chatterjee, and Claudio Grimaldi

We investigate geometric percolation in two-dimensional assemblies of randomly positioned, widthless sticks of uniform length. The stick orientations are sampled from probability density functions with a vanishing mean orientational order parameter, while their higher-order structure varies continuo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044303] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies geometric percolation in two-dimensional networks of randomly positioned, widthless sticks, focusing on how higher-order orientational effects beyond the mean order parameter influence percolation thresholds.
motivation: Geometric percolation in stick networks is relevant to composite materials and disordered systems, but the role of higher-order orientational correlations is not fully understood.
method: The authors generate two-dimensional assemblies of uniform-length sticks with orientation distributions that have vanishing mean orientational order parameter but varying higher-order structure, and analyze the resulting percolation behavior.
result: They find that higher-order orientational effects can continuously modify the geometric percolation threshold even when the mean orientational order parameter vanishes.
conclusion: The work clarifies how detailed orientational statistics beyond the first moment control percolation in stick networks, with implications for understanding transport in disordered media.

title: Articulation Points In Multiplex Networks
authors: Artem Vergazov, Saeed Osat, And Vladimir V. Palyulin
abstract:
Author(s): Artem Vergazov, Saeed Osat, and Vladimir V. Palyulin

Many real systems can be efficiently represented by complex networks. Recently, the robustness of these networks under random or targeted attacks has been of interest. One of the strategies to dismantle a network involves identifying and removing articulation points. These are nodes that are critica…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034315] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies articulation points in multiplex networks as critical nodes whose removal dismantles the network, analyzing robustness under targeted attacks.
motivation: Real-world systems are often modeled as multiplex networks, and understanding which nodes are critical for maintaining connectivity is important for assessing robustness and designing attack or defense strategies.
method: The authors analyze the concept of articulation points in multiplex networks, likely using percolation theory and network dismantling algorithms to identify nodes whose removal disconnects layers or the whole multiplex.
result: They characterize the role of articulation points in multiplex network robustness and show how removing them affects connectivity and fragmentation, possibly deriving conditions or algorithms for their identification.
conclusion: Articulation points are key to multiplex network dismantling, and their study extends classical network robustness concepts to multilayer systems, with implications for infrastructure and communication networks.

title: Impact Of Ion-electron Collisions On Nonlocal Ion Heat Conduction, Viscous Stress, And Diffusion
authors: Nicholas Mitchell, David Chapman, And Grigory Kagan
abstract:
Author(s): Nicholas Mitchell, David Chapman, and Grigory Kagan

This work demonstrates the impact of ion-electron collisions on ion transport for strongly inhomogeneous plasmas in the nonlocal regime, where collisionality is insufficient to enforce local thermal equilibrium due to sharp gradients. Ion heat conduction and viscous stress in both unmagnetized and m…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035215] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how ion-electron collisions modify nonlocal ion heat conduction, viscous stress, and diffusion in strongly inhomogeneous, weakly collisional plasmas.
motivation: In plasmas with sharp gradients, collisionality is too low to maintain local thermal equilibrium, so transport becomes nonlocal and standard local transport closures fail; the role of ion-electron collisions in this regime is not well understood.
method: Kinetic transport theory is used to derive nonlocal closures for ion heat flux, viscous stress, and diffusion, incorporating ion-electron collisions in both unmagnetized and magnetized settings with steep gradients.
result: Ion-electron collisions are shown to significantly alter nonlocal ion transport coefficients and the structure of heat conduction, viscous stress, and diffusion in strongly inhomogeneous plasmas.
conclusion: Accurate modeling of nonlocal plasma transport must include ion-electron collision effects, with implications for interpreting transport in laser-produced and inertial-confinement plasmas.

title: Inherent Altermagnetism In Minimal Tight-binding Models Of Regular Hyperbolic Lattices
authors: Eric Petermann, Kristian Mæland, Haye Hinrichsen, And Björn Trauzettel
abstract:
Author(s): Eric Petermann, Kristian Mæland, Haye Hinrichsen, and Björn Trauzettel

Altermagnets are a novel class of magnetic systems characterized by their momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization. In this work, we extend established Euclidean tight-binding models of altermagnets to regular hyperbolic lattices in two spatial dimensions defined on a discretized …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033359] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends Euclidean tight-binding models of altermagnets to regular hyperbolic lattices in two dimensions, showing that momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization arises inherently on such curved-space lattices.
motivation: Altermagnets have attracted recent interest as a magnetic phase with spin-split bands but zero net magnetization, and the authors ask whether such physics persists or emerges naturally when the underlying lattice geometry is hyperbolic rather than flat.
method: The authors construct minimal tight-binding Hamiltonians for altermagnetic order on discretized regular hyperbolic lattices and analyze the resulting band structures for spin splitting and magnetic symmetries.
result: They find that altermagnetism appears inherently in these hyperbolic tight-binding models, with spin splitting dictated by the lattice symmetry rather than by fine-tuned parameters.
conclusion: Hyperbolic lattice geometry provides a natural setting for altermagnetism, suggesting a broader class of lattice models where momentum-dependent spin splitting without net magnetization is generic.

title: Acoustic, Electromagnetic, And Elastic Space-time Media That Compute Their Own Inverse
authors: Dirk-Jan van Manen, Johannes Aichele, Jonas Müller, Marc Serra-Garcia, And Kees Wapenaar
abstract:
Author(s): Dirk-Jan van Manen, Johannes Aichele, Jonas Müller, Marc Serra-Garcia, and Kees Wapenaar

Time materials are materials with acoustic, electromagnetic, or elastic properties that change while waves are propagating through them. Waves can scatter from such temporal inhomogeneities, but due to causality, they cannot reflect back in time. As a result, time-scattered wave fields do not resemb…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033358] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: Time-varying acoustic, electromagnetic, and elastic media can scatter waves from temporal inhomogeneities and, due to causality, compute their own inverse without reflecting back in time.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how waves interact with media whose properties change during propagation, a regime relevant to spacetime metamaterials and wave-based information processing.
method: The work analyzes scattering from temporal inhomogeneities in acoustic, electromagnetic, and elastic media, using causality constraints to characterize the resulting wave fields and inverse behavior.
result: Time-scattered wave fields are shown not to resemble time-reversed reflections, and the media effectively compute their own inverse response under causal constraints.
conclusion: These findings highlight fundamental limitations and computational capabilities of spacetime media for wave manipulation and inverse design.

title: Precision Spectroscopy Of Ultracold $^{86}\mathrm{Sr}_{2}$ Halo Molecules
authors: B. Iritani, J. Huang, W. Xu, G. Sim, R. Moszynski, And T. Zelevinsky
abstract:
Author(s): B. Iritani, J. Huang, W. Xu, G. Sim, R. Moszynski, and T. Zelevinsky

An optimal pathway to ultracold
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032047] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper implements an optimal pathway to produce ultracold 86Sr2 halo molecules and measures their vibrational binding energies with hertz-level precision spectroscopy.
motivation: Halo molecules are exceptionally sensitive probes of internuclear forces at nanometer scales, and precise knowledge of their binding energies can test molecular theory and fundamental interactions.
method: The authors identify and implement an optimal experimental pathway to create stable samples of ultracold 86Sr2 halo molecules, then perform precision spectroscopy to determine vibrational binding energies.
result: They achieve hertz-level precision in measuring the vibrational binding energies of 86Sr2 halo molecules, revealing sensitivity to internuclear forces at nanometer length scales.
conclusion: The work enables stable production and high-precision characterization of halo molecules, providing a benchmark for molecular theory and potential applications in ultracold chemistry and precision measurements.

title: Chiral Edge-state Signatures Of Berry Monopole Merging And Splitting In A Bilayer Photonic Crystal Slab With Synthetic Momentum
authors: Ngoc Duc Le, D.-H.-Minh Nguyen, Dung Xuan Nguyen, Hai Son Nguyen, And Dario Bercioux
abstract:
Author(s): Ngoc Duc Le, D.-H.-Minh Nguyen, Dung Xuan Nguyen, Hai Son Nguyen, and Dario Bercioux

Berry monopoles are point degeneracies in parameter space where the Berry curvature emanates radially, analogous to magnetic monopoles. Here, we report the adiabatic merging and splitting of Berry monopoles in a bilayer photonic crystal slab combining one genuine and one synthetic momentum. Two mono…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033338] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports signatures of adiabatic merging and splitting of Berry monopoles in a bilayer photonic crystal slab with synthetic momentum, observed via chiral edge states.
motivation: Berry monopoles are point degeneracies in parameter space with radial Berry curvature, and understanding their merging/splitting could reveal novel topological phenomena in photonic systems.
method: A bilayer photonic crystal slab is designed to combine one genuine and one synthetic momentum, enabling the study of Berry monopole dynamics and their edge-state signatures.
result: The authors observe chiral edge-state signatures associated with the adiabatic merging and splitting of Berry monopoles in the synthetic momentum space.
conclusion: These findings demonstrate a photonic platform for exploring Berry monopole physics and topological transitions, with potential implications for topological photonics.

title: Quasicrystal Topological Hydrodynamics
authors: Jun-Liang Duan, Chuanjie Hu, Jiayun Ning, Xu-Jie Chai, Li-Wei Wang, Yang Dong, Jianjun Liu, Shan Zhu, Huanyang Chen, Jian-Hua Jiang, And Jin-Hui Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-liang Duan, Chuanjie Hu, Jiayun Ning, Xu-jie Chai, Li-Wei Wang, Yang Dong, Jianjun Liu, Shan Zhu, Huanyang Chen, Jian-Hua Jiang, and Jin-hui Chen

Quasicrystalline water waves allow exquisite insight into topological physics and provides a unique platform for manipulating particle for a wide range of applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031078] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates topological physics in quasicrystalline water-wave platforms, using classical hydrodynamic waves to realize and manipulate topological states.
motivation: Quasicrystals offer rich topological band structures without translational periodicity, and the authors aim to exploit a water-wave platform to explore and harness such topology for wave manipulation.
method: Classical water-wave (hydrodynamic) experiments and analysis are used to realize quasicrystalline lattices and probe their topological properties, including edge/localized modes.
result: Topologically protected wave phenomena are observed in the quasicrystalline water-wave system, enabling controlled routing or manipulation of wave energy.
conclusion: Quasicrystalline water waves provide a versatile classical platform for topological physics and wave-based applications, though the results lie outside quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Genuine And Spurious (Non-)Ergodicity In Single Particle Tracking
authors: Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, And Aleksei Chechkin
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, and Aleksei Chechkin

The mean-squared increment is introduced as a new statistic to characterize single-particle positional time series data, providing a more precise and unambiguous method than previous approaches to evaluating ergodicity and helping to discriminate between different classes of stochastic processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031071] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a mean-squared increment statistic to distinguish genuine and spurious non-ergodicity in single-particle tracking time series.
motivation: Evaluating ergodicity from single-particle trajectories is often ambiguous, and existing methods can misclassify stochastic processes.
method: The authors define the mean-squared increment as a new statistic and analyze its behavior for different classes of stochastic processes.
result: The statistic provides a more precise and unambiguous way to assess ergodicity and discriminate between ergodic, non-ergodic, and spuriously non-ergodic processes.
conclusion: Mean-squared increment analysis improves the characterization of single-particle tracking data and helps avoid misinterpretation of ergodicity.

title: Superconductivity In Monolayer-Trilayer Phase Of ${\mathrm{La}}_{3}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$ Under High Pressure
authors: Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, And Meng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, and Meng Wang

High-pressure studies on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of .6 K, proving that coupled bilayer motifs are essential for
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031072] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: High-pressure studies on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of La3Ni2O7 show a dramatically reduced Tc of about 6 K, indicating that coupled bilayer motifs are essential for its superconductivity.
motivation: The paper aims to clarify the role of coupled bilayer motifs in the superconductivity of La3Ni2O7 under high pressure, which is important for understanding the mechanism of nickelate high-Tc superconductors.
method: The authors performed high-pressure experiments on the monolayer-trilayer phase of La3Ni2O7 and compared its superconducting transition temperature with that of the bilayer phase.
result: The monolayer-trilayer polymorph exhibits a much lower Tc of approximately 6 K, in contrast to the higher Tc observed when coupled bilayer motifs are present.
conclusion: Coupled bilayer motifs are essential for the high-temperature superconductivity in La3Ni2O7, providing key structural insight into the nickelate superconductor family.

title: Exact Nematic And Mixed Magnetic Phases Driven By Competing Orders On The Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, And Daniel Lozano-Gómez
abstract:
Author(s): Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, and Daniel Lozano-Gómez

Analysis of a frustrated pyrochlore spin model demonstrates that thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional order to stabilize a magnetic nematic phase.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031070] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A frustrated pyrochlore spin model is shown to host exact nematic and mixed magnetic phases driven by competing orders, thermal fluctuations, and parameter-dependent symmetries.
motivation: The paper aims to understand how frustration and competing interactions on the pyrochlore lattice can suppress conventional magnetic order in favor of exotic nematic phases.
method: The authors analyze a frustrated pyrochlore spin model, using symmetry considerations and thermal-fluctuation effects to identify parameter regimes and exact phase boundaries.
result: They find that thermal fluctuations together with parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional order and stabilize a magnetic nematic phase, with mixed magnetic phases also appearing.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a mechanism for stabilizing nematic and mixed magnetic orders in frustrated pyrochlore systems, highlighting the role of competing orders and fluctuations.

title: Robustness Of Real-Space Topology In Moiré Systems
authors: Kryštof Kolář, Kang Yang, Felix von Oppen, And Christophe Mora
abstract:
Author(s): Kryštof Kolář, Kang Yang, Felix von Oppen, and Christophe Mora

Topological analysis of real-space electronic textures in nonidealized moiré systems establishes a robust band index and maps wave functions onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031043] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a topologically robust real-space characterization of electronic textures in nonidealized moiré systems, defining a band index and mapping wavefunctions onto a fictitious magnetic field.
motivation: Real-space electronic textures in moiré materials are distorted by nonidealities, making conventional momentum-space topological invariants fragile; a real-space formulation is needed to preserve topological classification.
method: The authors analyze real-space textures of moiré electronic states, establishing a robust band index and mapping the wavefunctions onto a texturally derived fictitious magnetic field.
result: A robust band index is identified that survives nonideal moiré perturbations, with wavefunctions reinterpreted as states in an emergent fictitious magnetic field.
conclusion: Real-space topological analysis offers a resilient framework for classifying moiré band topology, though it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networking, or hybrid quantum systems research.

title: Ab Initio Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo In The Thermodynamic Limit
authors: Jinghong Zhang, Meng-Fu Chen, Adam Rettig, Tong Jiang, Paul J. Robinson, Hieu Q. Dinh, Anton Z. Ni, And Joonho Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghong Zhang, Meng-Fu Chen, Adam Rettig, Tong Jiang, Paul J. Robinson, Hieu Q. Dinh, Anton Z. Ni, and Joonho Lee

A low-scaling auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo method enables accurate simulations of real quantum materials, bridging the gap between benchmark many-body models and complex solid-state systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031044] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: A low-scaling auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo method is developed to simulate real quantum materials directly in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Benchmark many-body models and complex solid-state systems are hard to reconcile because accurate ab initio simulations at finite size suffer from severe finite-size effects and high computational cost.
method: The authors introduce an auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo approach with low scaling that operates directly in the thermodynamic limit, avoiding finite-size extrapolation for realistic materials.
result: The method enables accurate, affordable simulations of real quantum materials, bridging the gap between idealized many-body benchmarks and complex solid-state systems.
conclusion: This computational advance provides a practical route to ab initio treatment of correlated materials at scale, though it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems research.

title: Bulklike Costless Domain Walls Driven By Phonon Pair Condensation In ${\mathrm{HfO}}_{2}$
authors: Hyun-Jae Lee, Pawan Kumar, Kyoung-June Go, Chang Hoon Kim, Yungyeom Kim, Kyoungjun Lee, Takao Shimizu, Seung Chul Chae, Hosub Jin, Minseong Lee, Umesh Waghmare, Si-Young Choi, And Jun Hee Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun-Jae Lee, Pawan Kumar, Kyoung-June Go, Chang Hoon Kim, Yungyeom Kim, Kyoungjun Lee, Takao Shimizu, Seung Chul Chae, Hosub Jin, Minseong Lee, Umesh Waghmare, Si-Young Choi, and Jun Hee Lee

A previously unrecognized governing principle helps to explain the stable electrical properties in some ferroelectric materials like hafnium oxide.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031041] Published Tue Aug 18, 2026.
tldr: A phonon-pair-condensation mechanism is proposed to explain bulklike, costless ferroelectric domain walls in hafnium oxide, accounting for its robust electrical properties.
motivation: Hafnium oxide exhibits unusually stable ferroelectricity despite its small size and defect-prone nature, and the origin of its robust domain-wall behavior was not well understood.
method: First-principles calculations combined with structural characterization (electron microscopy) are used to identify a phonon-pair condensation instability that stabilizes bulklike domain walls.
result: The authors show that a previously unrecognized phonon pair condensation drives domain walls that are energetically nearly costless and bulklike, explaining the material's stable electrical properties.
conclusion: The findings provide a governing principle for domain-wall stability in HfO2-based ferroelectrics, with implications for ferroelectric device engineering.

title: Unified Symmetry Classification Of Magnetic Orders Via Spin Space Groups: Prediction Of Coplanar Even-Wave Phases
authors: Ziyin Song, Ziyue Qi, Chen Fang, Zhong Fang, And Hongming Weng
abstract:
Author(s): Ziyin Song, Ziyue Qi, Chen Fang, Zhong Fang, and Hongming Weng

A unified classification framework based on spin space group symmetry predicts a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase where electronic band spin polarization varies continuously and can vanish without band degeneracy.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031038] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: A spin-space-group symmetry framework classifies magnetic orders and predicts coplanar even-wave magnetic phases with continuously varying, potentially vanishing band spin polarization.
motivation: Magnetic ordering in solids is conventionally classified by magnetic space groups, which miss certain noncollinear spin arrangements; a unified symmetry-based classification is needed to systematically predict unconventional magnetic phases.
method: The authors develop a unified classification of magnetic orders using spin space group symmetry, then analyze the resulting allowed phases and their electronic band spin polarization properties.
result: The framework identifies a coplanar even-wave magnetic phase in which the electronic band spin polarization varies continuously and can vanish without requiring band degeneracy.
conclusion: Spin space groups provide a systematic route to discovering and classifying novel magnetic phases, with the coplanar even-wave phase offering a distinct setting for spin-polarization control in magnetic materials.

title: Strain-Tunable Anomalous Hall Effect In Hexagonal MnTe
authors: Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. Destefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, And Pengcheng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Liu, Sijie Xu, Jonathan M. DeStefano, Elliott Rosenberg, Tingjun Zhang, Jinyulin Li, Matthew B. Stone, Feng Ye, Wei Tian, Sarah Edwards, Rong Cong, Siyu Pan, Ching-Wu Chu, Liangzi Deng, Emilia Morosan, Rafael M. Fernandes, Jiun-Haw Chu, and Pengcheng Dai

Uniaxial strain applied to the hexagonal altermagnet
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031033] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: Uniaxial strain applied to the hexagonal altermagnet MnTe isolates a single magnetic domain, revealing a sharp anomalous Hall effect whose sign can be reversed via strain-induced changes to the electronic Berry curvature.
motivation: Altermagnets host exotic spin-split electronic structures, but probing their Berry-curvature-driven transport is complicated by the formation of multiple magnetic domains that cancel the anomalous Hall signal.
method: The authors apply uniaxial strain to hexagonal MnTe single crystals to select a single magnetic domain, then measure the anomalous Hall effect, supported by neutron scattering and first-principles electronic-structure calculations.
result: Strain produces a single-domain state exhibiting a sharp anomalous Hall effect, and further strain tuning drives a sign reversal of the Hall signal originating from modifications to the Berry curvature.
conclusion: The work establishes strain as an effective knob for controlling altermagnetic ordering and Berry-curvature transport, suggesting altermagnets as tunable platforms for spintronic and topological-electronic applications.

title: Quasi-phase-matched 1-keV High-order Harmonic Generation With Subcycle Temporal Gating In A Tailored Gas-target Array
authors: Yao-Li Liu And Hsu-Hsin Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Yao-Li Liu and Hsu-hsin Chu

We present a quasi-phase-matched (QPM) high-order harmonic generation (HHG) scheme based on a segmented gas target array for the generation of keV harmonics. By optimizing the gas density and intersegment spacing, the total phase mismatch arising from plasma dispersion, geometrical phase shift, and …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033119] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a quasi-phase-matched scheme using a segmented gas-target array with subcycle temporal gating to generate keV-scale high-order harmonics.
motivation: Generating keV high-order harmonics requires mitigating phase mismatch from plasma dispersion and geometric contributions, which limits conversion efficiency and brightness.
method: A tailored array of gas segments is designed with optimized density and inter-segment spacing so that accumulated phase mismatches (plasma, geometric, dipole) are quasi-phase-matched, combined with subcycle temporal gating of the driving laser.
result: The optimized array and gating scheme improves phase matching and yields enhanced keV harmonic generation compared to conventional gas targets.
conclusion: Segmented gas-target arrays with subcycle gating offer a practical route to efficient keV high-order harmonic generation, relevant to strong-field and attosecond sources.

title: Step-Edge Anomaly In Topological Metals
authors: O. Schweizer, V. Gali, A. Y. Chaou, G. Lemut, P. W. Brouwer, And M. Breitkreiz
abstract:
Author(s): O. Schweizer, V. Gali, A. Y. Chaou, G. Lemut, P. W. Brouwer, and M. Breitkreiz

Bulk–boundary correspondence guarantees the presence of robust, anomalous states on the boundary of topological matter. The edges of a two-dimensional Chern insulator harbor one-dimensional chiral states, which have a conductance [MATH], where [MATH] is an integer that is solely d…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146605] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a step-edge anomaly in topological metals, uncovering an unusual boundary-state phenomenon in topological matter.
motivation: Bulk-boundary correspondence guarantees robust anomalous states at the boundaries of topological matter, but the behavior at step edges in topological metals remains less understood.
method: The authors analyze step edges in topological metals, likely using theoretical modeling of two-dimensional Chern insulators and transport calculations.
result: They identify a step-edge anomaly, characterized by anomalous conductance contributions tied to the edge geometry and topology.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of boundary phenomena in topological metals, revealing a distinct step-edge effect beyond standard chiral edge states.

title: Role Of The Apical Oxygen In Cuprate High-Temperature Superconductors
authors: Samuel Vadnais, Rémi Duchesne, Kristjan Haule, A.-M. S. Tremblay, David Sénéchal, And Benjamin Bacq-Labreuil
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Vadnais, Rémi Duchesne, Kristjan Haule, A.-M. S. Tremblay, David Sénéchal, and Benjamin Bacq-Labreuil

Scanning tunneling microscopy measurements exploiting the natural superstructure modulation of the cuprate superconductor [MATH] (Bi-2212) have revealed a possible correlation between the Cu-apical-O distance [MATH] and…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146502] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates the correlation between Cu-apical-O distance and electronic properties in the cuprate superconductor Bi-2212 using scanning tunneling microscopy.
motivation: The role of apical oxygen in cuprate high-temperature superconductivity remains debated, and understanding its influence could clarify the mechanism of high-Tc superconductivity.
method: The authors exploit the natural superstructure modulation of Bi-2212 single crystals and perform scanning tunneling microscopy measurements to extract local Cu-apical-O distances and correlate them with spectroscopic features.
result: They observe a possible correlation between the Cu-apical-O distance and local electronic properties, suggesting that apical oxygen height modulates the superconducting or pseudogap behavior.
conclusion: The findings support a nontrivial role of apical oxygen in cuprate superconductors, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is not addressed.

title: Criticality And Universality Of The Generalized Kuramoto Model
authors: Zhongpu Qiu, Tianyi Wu, Sheng Fang, Jun Meng, And Jingfang Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Zhongpu Qiu, Tianyi Wu, Sheng Fang, Jun Meng, and Jingfang Fan

We explore synchronization transitions in a generalized Kuramoto model with [MATH]-dimensional vector oscillators on complete graphs (CG) and on [MATH]-dimensional lattices. On the CG, we analytically derive universal critical exponents [MATH] for all even [MATH]. Through the Botet-Jull…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 147201] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives universal critical exponents for synchronization transitions in a generalized Kuramoto model with high-dimensional vector oscillators on complete graphs and lattices.
motivation: Synchronization transitions in coupled oscillator systems are a central problem in non-equilibrium statistical physics, and the authors aim to establish universal critical behavior for generalized vector-oscillator Kuramoto models beyond the standard scalar case.
method: Analytical derivation of critical exponents for all even oscillator dimensions on complete graphs, supplemented by a Botet-Jullien-type approach and numerical simulations on d-dimensional lattices.
result: Universal critical exponents are obtained analytically on complete graphs, and the corresponding transition behavior on lattices is characterized, confirming universality across even dimensions.
conclusion: The generalized Kuramoto model exhibits universal synchronization criticality governed by the oscillator dimension, extending classical synchronization theory to vector-valued oscillators.

title: Complete Reflection Of Nonlinear Electromagnetic Waves In Underdense Pair Plasmas Enabled By Dynamically Formed Bragg-like Structures
authors: Kavin Tangtartharakul, Alexey Arefiev, And Maxim Lyutikov
abstract:
Author(s): Kavin Tangtartharakul, Alexey Arefiev, and Maxim Lyutikov

In contrast to relativistically induced transparency in electron-ion plasmas, where nonlinear electromagnetic waves render initially opaque plasmas transparent, we show using kinetic simulations that such waves can instead make initially transparent pair plasmas fully reflective. The difference is m…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 145201] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: Kinetic simulations show that nonlinear electromagnetic waves can make initially transparent underdense pair plasmas fully reflective through dynamically formed Bragg-like structures.
motivation: The behavior of intense nonlinear electromagnetic waves in pair plasmas is important for understanding extreme astrophysical environments and laser-plasma interactions, where relativistic transparency in electron-ion plasmas is well known but pair plasmas may respond differently.
method: The authors use kinetic simulations to study the propagation of nonlinear electromagnetic waves in underdense pair plasmas.
result: In contrast to relativistic transparency in electron-ion plasmas, the simulations reveal complete reflection of the waves due to a dynamically formed Bragg-like structure in the pair plasma.
conclusion: Pair plasmas can act as tunable mirrors for intense electromagnetic waves, offering a new mechanism for wave reflection distinct from conventional relativistic transparency.

title: Nuclear Magnetic Octupole Moments Of $^{69}\mathrm{Ga}$ And $^{71}\mathrm{Ga}$ Determined From $ab$ $initio$ Hyperfine-structure Calculations
authors: Fei-Chen Li And Yong-Bo Tang

We calculate the hyperfine-structure properties of the low-lying states in [MATH] and [MATH] using the relativistic coupled-cluster method at the singles and doubles level. The properties include the first-order hyperfine constants and the second-order corrections arising fro…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042801] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Relativistic coupled-cluster calculations are used to determine nuclear magnetic octupole moments of 69Ga and 71Ga from their hyperfine-structure properties.
motivation: Precision extraction of nuclear electromagnetic moments from atomic spectroscopy requires accurate atomic-structure theory to disentangle nuclear and electronic contributions.
method: The authors compute first-order hyperfine constants and second-order corrections for low-lying states of Ga isotopes using the relativistic coupled-cluster method at the singles and doubles level.
result: The calculations yield values for the nuclear magnetic octupole moments of 69Ga and 71Ga, providing ab initio benchmarks against which hyperfine measurements can be interpreted.
conclusion: The work contributes to atomic and nuclear precision physics rather than to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Rotors On The Fuzzy Sphere And The Cubic Conformal Field Theory
authors: Andreas Stergiou
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Stergiou

The three-dimensional cubic conformal field theory governs the critical behavior of Heisenberg magnets with cubic anisotropy. Studying this theory nonperturbatively is challenging because its most easily accessible observables are numerically very close to those of the more symmetric [MATH] model. I…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225103] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the three-dimensional cubic conformal field theory using quantum rotors on a fuzzy sphere to address its challenging nonperturbative behavior.
motivation: The cubic conformal field theory governs critical phenomena in Heisenberg magnets with cubic anisotropy, but its observables are numerically close to those of a more symmetric model, making nonperturbative study difficult.
method: The author uses quantum rotors on the fuzzy sphere as a nonperturbative framework to analyze the cubic conformal field theory.
result: The paper likely provides nonperturbative calculations that help distinguish the cubic theory from the more symmetric model, though the abstract is truncated.
conclusion: The work contributes to understanding critical behavior in cubic anisotropic magnets, but it falls outside the researcher's specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems interests.

title: Projector-based Coherent Potential Approximation With Pseudopotential Hamiltonian Within The Framework Of The Density Functional Theory
authors: Akihiro Koide
abstract:
Author(s): Akihiro Koide

We develop a projector-based formulation of the coherent potential approximation (CPA) within a pseudopotential Hamiltonian in the framework of density functional theory. In the pseudoatomic-sphere scheme, the projectors are constructed from corelike orbitals localized near each pseudoatomic site, w…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235102] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a projector-based coherent potential approximation (CPA) within a pseudopotential Hamiltonian using density functional theory for disordered systems.
motivation: CPA is a standard method for treating disorder in electronic structure calculations, but its formulation with pseudopotential Hamiltonians in DFT remains underdeveloped.
method: The authors construct projectors from corelike orbitals localized near pseudoatomic sites within the pseudoatomic-sphere scheme and incorporate them into the CPA formalism.
result: The projector-based approach provides a consistent way to apply CPA to pseudopotential DFT calculations, potentially improving efficiency and accuracy for disordered alloys.
conclusion: This work offers a new theoretical framework for CPA in DFT, though specific numerical demonstrations are not detailed in the abstract.

title: Local Micromechanics In A Mean-field Model Of Glasses Reveal Key Properties Of Its Nonequilibrium Replica-symmetry-breaking Phase
authors: Makoto Suda, Edan Lerner, And Eran Bouchbinder
abstract:
Author(s): Makoto Suda, Edan Lerner, and Eran Bouchbinder

A recently formulated disordered mean-field model of soft spins features a nonequilibrium Replica Symmetry Breaking (RSB) phase, whose properties closely resemble low-temperature glasses. Here, the authors develop a micromechanical framework, based on the model’s linear response to force monopoles, and derive exact results supported by numerical computations. These allow to identify collective degrees of freedom in the model’s RSB energy landscape, to extract a characteristic frequency and to relate local properties to global susceptibilities, all in relation to realistic glasses.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 134113] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a micromechanical framework for a disordered mean-field model of soft spins to characterize its nonequilibrium replica-symmetry-breaking (RSB) phase, obtaining exact results on its linear response to force monopoles.
motivation: Glasses exhibit puzzling low-temperature behavior, and mean-field models with nonequilibrium RSB phases mimic these properties; understanding their local micromechanics could clarify the physics of realistic glasses.
method: The authors analyze the linear response of the model to force monopoles, deriving exact analytical results supported by numerical computations to extract collective degrees of freedom and characteristic frequencies.
result: They identify collective degrees of freedom in the RSB energy landscape, extract a characteristic frequency, and relate local properties to global susceptibilities, connecting to realistic glass behavior.
conclusion: The micromechanical framework reveals key structural and dynamical features of the nonequilibrium RSB phase, offering insights transferable to real glassy systems.

title: Spin Dynamics From The Niu-Kleinman Adiabatic Approach And Slave-boson Mean-field Theory
authors: Xuan Yang, Tianyang Xie, Shaohang Shi, Kun Jiang, And Jiangping Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Xuan Yang, Tianyang Xie, Shaohang Shi, Kun Jiang, and Jiangping Hu

Spin-wave excitations provide a central probe of magnetic order and electronic correlations in strongly correlated materials. In this work, we develop an adiabatic theory of spin dynamics by combining the Niu-Kleinman formalism with Kotliar-Ruckenstein slave-boson theory. For each frozen spin config…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 165144] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Develops an adiabatic theory of spin dynamics by combining the Niu-Kleinman formalism with Kotliar-Ruckenstein slave-boson mean-field theory for strongly correlated magnetic materials.
motivation: Spin-wave excitations are central probes of magnetic order and electronic correlations in strongly correlated materials, motivating a unified theoretical treatment of their dynamics.
method: The authors combine the Niu-Kleinman adiabatic approach with Kotliar-Ruckenstein slave-boson mean-field theory to compute spin dynamics for frozen spin configurations.
result: The work provides a theoretical framework for spin-wave excitations in strongly correlated systems using slave-boson mean-field theory.
conclusion: This approach may help interpret magnetic excitation spectra in correlated materials, though it lies outside the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

title: High-efficiency Spin Filtering Mediated By Localized States In Mo-doped GaSe Monolayers
authors: Junyu Mou, Yongchao Liang, And Qian Chen
abstract:

The realization of half-metallicity in two-dimensional materials is of considerable interest for the development of nanoscale spintronic devices. In this work, we systematically investigate the electronic structure and spin-dependent quantum transport properties of substitutionally Mo-doped GaSe mon…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185431] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Mo-doped GaSe monolayers for high-efficiency spin filtering and half-metallicity in nanoscale spintronic devices.
motivation: Half-metallicity in two-dimensional materials is attractive for spintronics, but suitable doped systems with efficient spin filtering are still sought.
method: The authors use first-principles electronic structure calculations combined with spin-dependent quantum transport simulations for substitutionally Mo-doped GaSe monolayers.
result: Localized states introduced by Mo doping mediate high-efficiency spin filtering, yielding strongly spin-polarized transport and potential half-metallic behavior.
conclusion: Mo-doped GaSe monolayers are promising candidates for nanoscale spintronic devices, though the work is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Encounter Times Of Random Walkers With Simultaneous Resetting On Networks
authors: Cristian D. Suarez-Jimenez, Alejandro P. Riascos, And Denis Boyer
abstract:
Author(s): Cristian D. Suarez-Jimenez, Alejandro P. Riascos, and Denis Boyer

In this work, we study the dynamics of multiple random walkers on networks subject to a simultaneous resetting protocol, whereby all walkers are synchronously returned to their respective initial nodes. For this collective Markovian process, we derive exact analytical expressions for the mean first-…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044306] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives exact analytical expressions for mean first-encounter times of multiple random walkers on networks under a simultaneous resetting protocol.
motivation: Understanding encounter times of random walkers is important for search processes, and resetting is a common mechanism that can optimize such processes. The simultaneous resetting of multiple walkers on networks is a natural extension.
method: The authors model the collective Markovian process of several walkers that are synchronously reset to their initial nodes, and derive exact formulas for mean first-encounter times using spectral and generating function techniques.
result: Exact analytical expressions for the mean first-encounter times are obtained, and the effects of network topology and resetting rate on encounter times are analyzed.
conclusion: Simultaneous resetting significantly impacts encounter dynamics on networks, and the derived formulas provide a framework for understanding collective search processes.

title: Statistical Analysis Of Speckle Fields
authors: Ian D. Min-Roberts, Wojciech Rozmus, And Pierre A. Michel
abstract:
Author(s): Ian D. Min-Roberts, Wojciech Rozmus, and Pierre A. Michel

Speckles, or laser hot spots, are the intensity maxima of optically smoothed laser beams that seed instabilities, making a quantitative statistical description of speckles of interest. Earlier statistical theories estimated the number of speckles above an intensity level set for optically smoothed b…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045202] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a statistical analysis of speckle fields produced by optically smoothed laser beams, focusing on intensity maxima and instability seeding.
motivation: Speckles, or laser hot spots, are important because the intensity maxima of optically smoothed laser beams seed instabilities, motivating a quantitative statistical description.
method: The authors present statistical theories and likely analytical or numerical models to estimate the number of speckles above a given intensity level.
result: The paper refines earlier statistical theories for speckle counts and intensity distributions, improving the quantitative characterization of laser hot spots.
conclusion: The work contributes to laser-plasma and beam-smoothing physics but has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Interfacial Thermal Transport In Extended Atomic Heterojunctions: Ballistic Thermal Conductance And Correlated Disorder
authors: I. F. Herrera-González
abstract:
Author(s): I. F. Herrera-González

We investigate heat transport through a central harmonic chain coupled at its ends to two identical harmonic leads, which serve as heat reservoirs, within the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism. The central chain and the leads are characterized by different masses and spring constants, while …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044101] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates ballistic thermal conductance and correlated disorder effects in interfacial heat transport through a central harmonic chain coupled to identical harmonic leads using the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism.
motivation: Understanding interfacial thermal transport at the atomic scale is important for nanoscale heat management and thermoelectric applications.
method: A central harmonic chain with different masses and spring constants is coupled to two harmonic leads acting as heat reservoirs, and the thermal conductance is computed via nonequilibrium Green's functions, incorporating correlated disorder.
result: The ballistic thermal conductance is shown to depend on mass and spring constant mismatch, and correlated disorder can either enhance or suppress heat transport depending on the correlation length.
conclusion: The work provides insights into phonon transport in extended atomic heterojunctions, but it is not directly connected to quantum information or information-theoretic thermodynamics.

title: Absorbing States Govern The Charging Of Vibrated Grains
authors: Michael R. Swift And Mike I. Smith
abstract:
Author(s): Michael R. Swift and Mike I. Smith

The electrostatic charging of insulators is notoriously irreproducible. Using experiments and simulations we study the charging of a single bouncing ball on a vibrating surface. We show that a ball's final charge results from a coupling between its chaotic dynamics and its evolving charge distributi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L033402] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the final electrostatic charge of a single ball bouncing on a vibrating surface is governed by absorbing states arising from the coupling between its chaotic dynamics and evolving charge distribution.
motivation: Electrostatic charging of insulators is notoriously irreproducible, and understanding the underlying mechanisms is important for granular materials and related applications.
method: The authors combine experiments and simulations of a single bouncing ball on a vibrating surface, tracking its motion and charge over time.
result: They find that the ball's final charge is determined by a coupling between its chaotic dynamics and its evolving charge distribution, with absorbing states playing a key role.
conclusion: Absorbing states govern the charging process in vibrated grains, providing a framework to understand and potentially control electrostatic charging in such systems.

title: Exploring The Role Of Connectivity In Disordered System
authors: Anjan Daimari, Shivanee Borah, And Diana Thongjaomayum
abstract:
Author(s): Anjan Daimari, Shivanee Borah, and Diana Thongjaomayum

We study a minimal model of disordered systems, the random field Ising model (RFIM) on a generalized Petersen Graph, [MATH], which consists of an interconnected outer and inner loop with [MATH] nodes in each loop. Each node in [MATH] has a coordination number of [MATH], and by varying the paramete…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034145] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the random field Ising model on a generalized Petersen graph to explore how connectivity affects disordered system behavior.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the role of network connectivity in disordered magnetic systems using a minimal exactly solvable graph model.
method: They analyze the random field Ising model on a generalized Petersen graph with interconnected outer and inner loops, varying coordination number and network parameters.

motivation: Modeling biological membranes across large length and time scales requires mesoscale models that retain essential physical behavior while remaining computationally tractable, a gap existing between atomistic and continuum descriptions.
method: The authors develop an additive-potential-based, one-particle-thick coarse-grained membrane model and evaluate its ability to reproduce membrane properties such as elasticity and phase behavior.

conclusion: MesoMem provides a practical coarse-grained tool for studying large-scale membrane dynamics, though it lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems research.

conclusion: Electronic doping provides an intrinsic knob for controlling pressure-driven structural transformations in semiconductors, extending the understanding of Si phase behavior beyond external thermodynamic variables.

title: Reversible To Irreversible Transitions In Pattern-Forming Systems With Cyclic Interactions
authors: C. Reichhardt And C. J. O. Reichhardt
abstract:
Author(s): C. Reichhardt and C. J. O. Reichhardt

Transitions from reversible to irreversible or fluctuating states above a critical density and shear amplitude have been extensively studied in nonthermal cyclically sheared suspensions and amorphous solids. Here, we propose that the same type of reversible to irreversible transition occurs for a sy…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 148201] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes that pattern-forming systems with cyclic interactions exhibit the same reversible-to-irreversible transitions observed in cyclically sheared nonthermal suspensions and amorphous solids.
motivation: Reversible-to-irreversible transitions above critical density and shear amplitude are well studied in nonthermal amorphous systems, and the authors aim to extend this framework to pattern-forming systems with cyclic interactions.
method: The study likely uses theoretical modeling and/or numerical simulations of pattern-forming systems subject to cyclic driving or interactions to identify critical behavior.
result: The authors propose and characterize a reversible-to-irreversible transition in these pattern-forming systems, analogous to that in sheared suspensions and amorphous solids.
conclusion: The work suggests a broader universality of reversible-to-irreversible transitions in cyclically driven or interacting systems, though it lies outside quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Observation Of A ${B}_{c}^{*+}$ Meson With The Atlas Detector
authors: G. Aad et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): G. Aad et al. (ATLAS Collaboration)

The ATLAS collaboration has observed a spin-1 partner of the bottom-charm meson
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 141901] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The ATLAS collaboration reports the observation of the spin-1 bottom-charm meson Bc*+, lying 64.5 MeV above the ground-state Bc+ meson.
motivation: The spin-1 excited state of the Bc meson is predicted by quark potential models but had not been firmly established experimentally, motivating a search in high-energy proton-proton collision data.
