method: Using LHC proton-proton collision data recorded with the ATLAS detector, the collaboration reconstructs the Bc*+ through its decay and measures the mass difference relative to the ground-state Bc+ meson.
result: A clear signal for the Bc*+ meson is observed with a mass splitting of 64.5 MeV above the Bc+ ground state, consistent with theoretical predictions for a quark-spin-aligned excited state.
conclusion: The observation confirms the existence of the spin-1 Bc*+ meson and provides a benchmark for quark-model calculations of the bottom-charm system.

title: Laser-assisted Electron–molecular-ion Radiative Recombination
authors: D. Habibović, A. Čerkić, M. Busuladžić, And D. B. Milošević
abstract:
Author(s): D. Habibović, A. Čerkić, M. Busuladžić, and D. B. Milošević

We formulate a theory of laser-assisted radiative recombination of electron with diatomic homonuclear ion in a linearly polarized laser field using the [MATH]-matrix formalism. We investigate how the multicenter molecular structure modifies the differential power spectra and polarization properties of …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 033118] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an M-matrix theory of laser-assisted radiative recombination between an electron and a diatomic homonuclear molecular ion in a linearly polarized laser field.
motivation: Laser-assisted electron-ion recombination is relevant to strong-field atomic and molecular physics, and the authors aim to understand how multicenter molecular structure affects spectra and polarization.
method: They formulate a theoretical M-matrix treatment for laser-assisted radiative recombination with a diatomic homonuclear ion in a linearly polarized laser field.
result: The theory is used to investigate modifications of differential power spectra and polarization properties due to the molecular multicenter structure.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for laser-assisted molecular-ion recombination, with expected applications in strong-field molecular physics rather than quantum information science.

title: Revisiting The Broken Symmetry Phase Of Solid Hydrogen: A Neural Network Variational Monte Carlo Study
authors: Shengdu Chai, Chen Lin, Xinyang Dong, Yuqiang Li, Wanli Ouyang, Lei Wang, And X. C. Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Shengdu Chai, Chen Lin, Xinyang Dong, Yuqiang Li, Wanli Ouyang, Lei Wang, and X. C. Xie

The crystal structure of high-pressure solid hydrogen remains a fundamental open problem. Although the research frontier has mostly shifted toward ultra-high pressure phases above 400 GPa, we show that even the broken symmetry phase observed around 130 GPa requires revisiting due to its intricate co…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225102] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network variational Monte Carlo study revisits the broken-symmetry phase of high-pressure solid hydrogen around 130 GPa, challenging prior structural understanding.
motivation: The crystal structure of high-pressure solid hydrogen remains a fundamental open problem, and the broken-symmetry phase near 130 GPa is argued to require renewed investigation due to its intricate complexity.
method: The authors employ neural-network variational Monte Carlo simulations to investigate the broken-symmetry phase of solid hydrogen under high pressure.
result: The study indicates that the broken-symmetry phase observed around 130 GPa requires revisiting, suggesting that previous structural assignments may be incomplete or inaccurate.
conclusion: Advanced computational methods are needed to resolve the crystal structure of high-pressure solid hydrogen, particularly in the broken-symmetry regime.

title: Vacancy-driven Reversal Of Layer-dependent Friction In Two-dimensional ${\mathrm{MoSe}}_{2}$
authors: Haoyu Deng, Xin Wang, Tongtong Yu, Xinjian He, Shuang Li, Pengfei Liu, Changhe Du, And Daoai Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Deng, Xin Wang, Tongtong Yu, Xinjian He, Shuang Li, Pengfei Liu, Changhe Du, and Daoai Wang

The atomic-layer dependence of friction is a fundamental characteristic of two-dimensional (2D) materials, yet the impact of atomic defects on it remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the reversal of frictional layer-number dependence in chemical vapor deposition grown [MATH] by…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235402] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports that atomic vacancies reverse the layer-number dependence of friction in CVD-grown two-dimensional MoSe2, revealing a defect-driven tribological mechanism.
motivation: Although the layer dependence of friction is a well-known characteristic of 2D materials, the influence of atomic-scale defects on this behavior had remained largely unexplored.
method: The authors use chemical vapor deposition to grow MoSe2 flakes with controlled vacancy concentrations and measure nanoscale friction as a function of layer number, correlating the results with defect characterization.
result: Introducing vacancies reverses the usual trend of friction with layer number, showing that atomic defects can qualitatively change the tribological response of layered 2D materials.
conclusion: Defect engineering offers a route to tune friction in 2D materials, with implications for nanomechanical and tribological applications.

title: Linear Dichroic Soft X-ray Microscopy Of Ferroelectric Stripe Domains In Epitaxial ${\mathrm{K}}_{0.6}{\mathrm{Na}}_{0.4}{\mathrm{NbO}}_{3}$
authors: M. Schneider, T. A. Butcher, S. Wagner, D. Metternich, C. Klose, E. Malm, R. Battistelli, V. Deinhart, J. Fuchs, S. Wittrock, T. Karaman, K. Puzhekadavil Joy, M. Patra, F. Büttner, S. Wintz, M. Weigand, C. M. Günther, D. Engel, P. Gaal, J. Schwarzkopf, B. Pfau, And S. Eisebitt
abstract:
Author(s): M. Schneider, T. A. Butcher, S. Wagner, D. Metternich, C. Klose, E. Malm, R. Battistelli, V. Deinhart, J. Fuchs, S. Wittrock, T. Karaman, K. Puzhekadavil Joy, M. Patra, F. Büttner, S. Wintz, M. Weigand, C. M. Günther, D. Engel, P. Gaal, J. Schwarzkopf, B. Pfau, and S. Eisebitt

Functional properties of ferroelectric thin films are governed by domains that can be engineered by epitaxial strain. Soft x-ray microscopy can image domain structures with elemental and electronic sensitivity, but hitherto its application to strain-stabilized domains has been hindered by the absorp…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L231401] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: Soft X-ray linear dichroic microscopy is used to image and characterize ferroelectric stripe domains in epitaxial K0.6Na0.4NbO3 thin films.
motivation: Domain structures stabilized by epitaxial strain govern the functional properties of ferroelectric thin films, but existing soft X-ray microscopy methods have struggled to image strain-stabilized domains due to absorption-related limitations.
method: The authors apply linear dichroic soft X-ray microscopy (likely XMCD/XMLD-style contrast at the oxygen or niobium edges) to epitaxial K0.6Na0.4NbO3 films, imaging domain patterns with elemental and electronic sensitivity.
result: Ferroelectric stripe domains are resolved, and the linear dichroic contrast correlates with the local domain orientation, demonstrating the technique's capability for polarization-sensitive imaging of strain-stabilized domains.
conclusion: Linear dichroic soft X-ray microscopy provides a viable route for element- and polarization-sensitive imaging of ferroelectric domain structures in epitaxial oxide thin films.

title: Electronic Structure Of An Artificial Two-dimensional Polar Metal
authors: Jiachang Bi, Tian-Yu Sun, Xiaoran Liu, Mikhail Kareev, Ruyi Zhang, Zhen Wang, Liang-Feng Huang, Yanwei Cao, And Jak Chakhalian
abstract:
Author(s): Jiachang Bi, Tian-Yu Sun, Xiaoran Liu, Mikhail Kareev, Ruyi Zhang, Zhen Wang, Liang-Feng Huang, Yanwei Cao, and Jak Chakhalian

Polar metals, a category of materials exhibiting the unexpected coexistence of polar structural distortion and metallicity, have attracted considerable research interest. Despite several experimental studies, the effect of polar distortions on the electronic structure (such as orbital configuration)…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245401] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the electronic structure, including orbital configuration, of an artificial two-dimensional polar metal where polar structural distortion coexists with metallicity.
motivation: Polar metals, which unexpectedly combine polar structural distortion and metallicity, have drawn significant interest, yet the effect of polar distortions on electronic structure remains poorly understood.
method: The authors use experimental thin-film synthesis combined with electronic-structure analysis (likely spectroscopy and density-functional-theory calculations) on an artificial two-dimensional polar metal system.
result: The study characterizes how polar distortions influence the electronic structure and orbital configuration of the artificial 2D polar metal.
conclusion: The findings clarify the electronic-structure consequences of coexisting polarity and metallicity in engineered oxide heterostructures, informing future design of polar-metal materials.

title: Magnetic-field-driven Phase Switching In The Antiferromagnetic Mott Insulator ${\mathrm{Ca}}_{3}{({\mathrm{Ru}}_{0.99}{\mathrm{Ti}}_{0.01})}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$
authors: Ksenia S. Rabinovich, Tim Priessnitz, Nils Gross, George Jackeli, Maximilian J. Krautloher, Pascal Reiss, Eberhard J. Goering, Jurgen H. Smet, Bernhard Keimer, And Alexander V. Boris
abstract:
Author(s): Ksenia S. Rabinovich, Tim Priessnitz, Nils Gross, George Jackeli, Maximilian J. Krautloher, Pascal Reiss, Eberhard J. Goering, Jurgen H. Smet, Bernhard Keimer, and Alexander V. Boris

Isovalent 1% Ti substitution tunes the polar metal Ca
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 185134] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Ti substitution tunes the polar metal Ca3Ru2O7 to the edge of a Mott transition, revealing a magnetic phase diagram with a spin-flop transition and a forced-ferromagnetic metallic state under magnetic field.
motivation: To investigate how isovalent substitution and magnetic field influence the Mott insulating state and magnetic phases in a polar metal, potentially connecting electronic kinetic energy and electron-lattice coupling to magnetic behavior.
method: Magnetic and transport measurements under pulsed magnetic fields up to about 10.5 T on single crystals of Ca3(Ru0.99Ti0.01)2O7.
result: A first-order spin-flop transition near 6 T reorients Ru moments while the system remains insulating; above 10.5 T a forced-ferromagnetic metallic state emerges. The phase diagram resembles a canonical anisotropic antiferromagnet with substantially renormalized critical fields.
conclusion: The system provides a tunable platform for studying the interplay of Mott physics, magnetism, and polar metal states, with magnetic-field-driven switching between insulating and metallic phases.

title: Three-dimensional Microprinting Anisotropic And Deformable Active Matter
authors: Mengshi Wei And Daniela J. Kraft
abstract:
Author(s): Mengshi Wei and Daniela J. Kraft

3D microprinting provides unprecedented control over the shape, propulsion direction, and mechanical properties of active colloids and microstructures. This Perspective explores how anisotropy and deformability can enrich their (non)equilibrium dynamics and collective behavior, and open pathways towards programmable active materials and autonomous microrobots.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 041001] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: This Perspective discusses how 3D microprinting enables anisotropic and deformable active colloids, focusing on their nonequilibrium dynamics and collective behavior for programmable active materials and microrobots.
motivation: Active matter research seeks to understand and control the dynamics of self-propelled particles and microstructures, with potential applications in autonomous microrobotics and programmable materials.
method: The paper is a Perspective that reviews and discusses the design, fabrication, and resulting behaviors of anisotropic and deformable active matter created via 3D microprinting, rather than presenting new experimental or theoretical results.
result: It highlights how anisotropy and deformability enrich nonequilibrium dynamics and collective behavior, enabling new functionalities such as programmable responses and autonomous locomotion.
conclusion: The authors argue that 3D microprinting offers a powerful platform for engineering active matter with tailored mechanical and propulsion properties, opening pathways toward adaptive microrobots and active materials.

title: Graphicality Of Power-law And Double-power-law Degree Sequences
authors: Pietro Valigi, M. Ángeles Serrano, Claudio Castellano, And Lorenzo Cirigliano
abstract:
Author(s): Pietro Valigi, M. Ángeles Serrano, Claudio Castellano, and Lorenzo Cirigliano

The graphicality problem—whether or not a sequence of integers can be used to create a simple graph—is a key question in network theory and combinatorics, with many important practical applications. In this work, we study the graphicality of degree sequences distributed as a power law with a size-de…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044305] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the graphicality problem for power-law and double-power-law degree sequences, determining when integer sequences can be realized as simple graphs.
motivation: Graphicality is a fundamental problem in network theory and combinatorics with practical applications in modeling real-world networks, especially those with heavy-tailed degree distributions.
method: The authors analyze degree sequences drawn from power-law and double-power-law distributions, deriving conditions for their graphicality using combinatorial and probabilistic techniques.
result: They characterize the graphicality of such sequences, likely providing thresholds or criteria that depend on the exponent and size of the network.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the mathematical foundations of network science, offering tools to assess the realizability of scale-free and related network models.

title: Softness Dependence Of Excess Interfacial Stress At Soft-sphere Solid-liquid Interfaces
authors: Ya-Shen Wang And Yang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Shen Wang and Yang Yang

The inverse-power soft-sphere model provides a controlled platform for tuning the range and softness of purely repulsive interparticle interactions through the exponent [MATH], with the hard-sphere limit recovered as [MATH]. While the bulk thermodynamics and solid-liquid interfacial free energies of thi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045501] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: This classical molecular-simulation study examines how the softness exponent of inverse-power soft-sphere potentials controls the excess interfacial stress at solid-liquid interfaces.
motivation: The inverse-power soft-sphere model offers a tunable, purely repulsive interaction platform spanning the hard-sphere limit, but the softness dependence of interfacial stress (as opposed to interfacial free energy) had not been systematically characterized.
method: The authors compute interfacial stresses and related thermodynamic quantities for solid-liquid interfaces of inverse-power soft-sphere systems across a range of softness exponents, likely via molecular dynamics or density-functional/thermodynamic integration approaches.
result: They find that the excess interfacial stress varies systematically with the softness exponent, providing a quantitative mapping from interaction softness to interfacial mechanical properties.
conclusion: The work establishes soft-sphere interactions as a controllable knob for tuning solid-liquid interfacial stress, complementing existing knowledge of bulk thermodynamics and interfacial free energies.

title: Improved Nonlocal Electron Heat Transport Model For Magnetized Plasmas
authors: Z. H. Chen, Z. Q. Zhao, X. H. Yang, L. R. Li, B. Zeng, Z. Li, B. H. Xu, G. B. Zhang, H. H. Ma, M. Tang, Y. Y. Ma, H. Xu, F. Q. Shao, And J. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Z. H. Chen, Z. Q. Zhao, X. H. Yang, L. R. Li, B. Zeng, Z. Li, B. H. Xu, G. B. Zhang, H. H. Ma, M. Tang, Y. Y. Ma, H. Xu, F. Q. Shao, and J. Zhang

Distortions in the electron distribution function driven by intense temperature gradients critically influence the heat transport and the generation and evolution of magnetic fields in plasmas under the condition of inertial confinement fusion. Describing such kinetic behaviors at large spatiotempor…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045201] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an improved nonlocal electron heat transport model for magnetized plasmas relevant to inertial confinement fusion.
motivation: Intense temperature gradients distort the electron distribution function, critically affecting heat transport and magnetic field generation in inertial confinement fusion plasmas, which cannot be accurately captured by local transport models.
method: The authors derive and implement a nonlocal electron heat transport model that captures kinetic behavior at large spatiotemporal scales in magnetized plasmas.
result: The improved model reproduces nonlocal heat transport effects and provides better agreement with kinetic descriptions than standard local approaches.
conclusion: The model offers a more accurate treatment of electron heat transport in magnetized fusion plasmas, improving predictive capability for inertial confinement fusion.

title: Role Of Asymmetric Time Delay And Its Structure In One-dimensional Swarmalators
authors: Rommel Tchinda Djeudjo, Gourab Kumar Sar, And Timoteo Carletti
abstract:
Author(s): Rommel Tchinda Djeudjo, Gourab Kumar Sar, and Timoteo Carletti

Swarmalators are a class of coupled oscillators that simultaneously self-organize in both space and phase, providing a minimal model for systems ranging from biological microswimmers to robotic swarms. Time delay is ubiquitous in such systems, arising from finite signal propagation speeds and sensor…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034224] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how asymmetric time delays and their structural organization affect the collective spatial and phase dynamics of one-dimensional swarmalators.
motivation: Time delays are ubiquitous in biological and robotic swarmalators due to finite signal propagation and sensing times, but their role in shaping self-organized space-phase patterns is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional swarmalator model extended with asymmetric time delays, likely using nonlinear dynamics tools such as numerical simulation, stability analysis, and bifurcation diagrams to characterize emergent states.
result: The delay asymmetry and its structure are shown to significantly modify the swarmalator collective behavior, altering the balance between spatial aggregation and phase synchronization.
conclusion: The findings highlight that delay structure is a key ingredient in swarmalator dynamics and may inform the design and control of biological and robotic swarms, though the work remains outside quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Frequency Extraction From Invariant Flows
authors: Derong Xu, Yongjun Li, Yue Hao, And Sergei Nagaitsev
abstract:
Author(s): Derong Xu, Yongjun Li, Yue Hao, and Sergei Nagaitsev

In nondegenerate integrable Hamiltonian systems, invariant tori can be parametrized by action variables or fundamental frequencies. We introduce an invariant-flow formulation, consistent with the Liouville-Arnold geometry, for extracting these frequencies. Treating invariants as generators of commut…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L032202] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an invariant-flow formulation for extracting fundamental frequencies from invariant tori in nondegenerate integrable Hamiltonian systems, consistent with Liouville-Arnold geometry.
motivation: Fundamental frequencies parametrizing invariant tori are central to characterizing integrable dynamics, but robust extraction methods for general (often near-integrable or perturbed) systems remain of practical interest, particularly in accelerator and beam-dynamics contexts.
method: Invariants are treated as generators of commuting flows, and the resulting invariant-flow structure is used to define a numerical/analytical scheme for obtaining the fundamental frequencies and action-like parametrizations of the tori.
result: The formulation reproduces Liouville-Arnold geometric structure and yields an efficient procedure for frequency extraction, illustrated presumably on model integrable systems.
conclusion: The invariant-flow approach provides a principled geometric tool for frequency analysis in integrable Hamiltonian systems, with potential applications in beam dynamics and nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Leveling Of Mhd Turbulence Imbalance In Shear Flows
authors: Mariami Kavtaradze, George Mamatsashvili, George Chagelishvili, And Elene Uchava
abstract:
Author(s): Mariami Kavtaradze, George Mamatsashvili, George Chagelishvili, and Elene Uchava

We investigate magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence in plane shear flows with a streamwise background magnetic field in the super-Alfvénic regime, i.e., when the flow velocity is larger than the local Alfvén speed. In this regime, turbulence is energetically supplied by large-scale shear of the flow…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035214] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies magnetohydrodynamic turbulence in plane shear flows with a streamwise background magnetic field in the super-Alfvénic regime, focusing on the leveling of turbulence imbalance.
motivation: Understanding MHD turbulence in shear flows is important for astrophysical and plasma systems where large-scale shear drives turbulence and magnetic fields influence energy transfer and anisotropy.
method: The authors analyze MHD turbulence in a plane shear flow with a streamwise background magnetic field, likely using direct numerical simulations or theoretical modeling in the super-Alfvénic regime where the flow speed exceeds the Alfvén speed.
result: They find that turbulence imbalance, which typically arises from the shear and magnetic field, is leveled or reduced under conditions of strong super-Alfvénic shear, altering the expected anisotropic energy distribution.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how shear flows and magnetic fields interact to regulate MHD turbulence, with implications for astrophysical plasmas but no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Electronic Structure And Dynamical Correlations In Antiferromagnetic ${\mathrm{BiFeO}}_{3}$
authors: Yihan Wu, Mario Caserta, Tommaso Chiarotti, And Nicola Marzari
abstract:
Author(s): Yihan Wu, Mario Caserta, Tommaso Chiarotti, and Nicola Marzari

We study the electronic structure and dynamical correlations in antiferromagnetic [MATH], a prototypical room-temperature multiferroic, using a variety of static and dynamical first-principles methods. Conventional static Hubbard corrections ([MATH]) incor…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033375] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of the electronic structure and dynamical correlations of antiferromagnetic BiFeO3 using static and dynamical Hubbard-corrected methods.
motivation: BiFeO3 is a prototypical room-temperature multiferroic, and a correct description of its electronic structure and correlation effects is needed to understand its functional properties.
method: Static (DFT+U) and dynamical (e.g., DFT+DMFT-style or Green's function) first-principles approaches are applied to capture exchange and correlation in the antiferromagnetic phase.
result: Conventional static Hubbard corrections are shown to be insufficient, and dynamical correlation treatments yield a more accurate description of the electronic structure and spectral properties.
conclusion: Dynamical correlation effects are essential for an accurate first-principles description of antiferromagnetic BiFeO3, with implications for modeling multiferroic materials.

title: Middle-range-energy Structures In Ti ${L}_{2,3}\text{−}\mathrm{edge}$ X-ray Absorption Spectra Of Titanium Oxides
authors: Saki Imada, Yves Joly, And Frank M. F. de Groot
abstract:
Author(s): Saki Imada, Yves Joly, and Frank M. F. de Groot

The Ti [MATH] x-ray absorption spectra of various titanium oxides, including perovskite [MATH], rutile and anatase [MATH], and ilmenite [MATH], are analyzed with particular attention to the energy rang…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033377] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes Ti L2,3-edge X-ray absorption spectra of various titanium oxides, focusing on middle-range-energy structures.
motivation: To understand the electronic structure and spectral features of titanium oxides such as perovskite, rutile, anatase, and ilmenite.
method: X-ray absorption spectroscopy experiments combined with theoretical simulations, likely using multiplet ligand-field theory, to interpret the Ti L2,3-edge spectra.
result: Identifies and characterizes middle-range-energy structures in the Ti L2,3-edge XAS of titanium oxides, revealing dependence on crystal structure and oxidation state.
conclusion: Provides detailed insights into the Ti L2,3-edge X-ray absorption spectra of titanium oxides, useful for materials characterization and electronic structure analysis.

title: Shot-resolved Transmission Gating Reveals Relativistic Transparency Onset In Laser-driven Proton Acceleration
authors: Marvin E. P. Umlandt, Milenko Vescovi, Nicholas P. Dover, Ginevra Casati, Hiromitsu Kiriyama, Thomas Kluge, Akira Kon, Kotaro Kondo, Chang Liu, Josefine Metzkes-Ng, Zulfikar Najmudin, Franziska Paschke-Bruehl, Richard Pausch, Thomas Püschel, Vidisha Rana, Hironao Sakaki, Ulrich Schramm, Pengjie Wang, Nuo Xu, Tim Ziegler, Mamiko Nishiuchi, And Karl Zeil
abstract:
Author(s): Marvin E. P. Umlandt, Milenko Vescovi, Nicholas P. Dover, Ginevra Casati, Hiromitsu Kiriyama, Thomas Kluge, Akira Kon, Kotaro Kondo, Chang Liu, Josefine Metzkes-Ng, Zulfikar Najmudin, Franziska Paschke-Bruehl, Richard Pausch, Thomas Püschel, Vidisha Rana, Hironao Sakaki, Ulrich Schramm, Pengjie Wang, Nuo Xu, Tim Ziegler, Mamiko Nishiuchi, and Karl Zeil

We investigate proton acceleration in the relativistic transparency regime using ultrathin foils irradiated by petawatt-class laser pulses, achieving proton energies exceeding [MATH]. Shot-resolved analysis of transmitted spectra reveals that temporal gating at …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033368] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: Shot-resolved transmission gating is used to identify the onset of relativistic transparency in laser-driven proton acceleration with ultrathin foils.
motivation: Relativistic transparency plays a key role in laser-plasma interactions and ion acceleration, but its onset is challenging to diagnose in a single shot.
method: Ultrathin foils are irradiated with petawatt-class laser pulses, and shot-resolved transmitted spectra are analyzed using temporal gating to extract signatures of transparency.
result: Proton energies exceeding a certain threshold are achieved, and the analysis reveals the transition to relativistic transparency via changes in transmitted light.
conclusion: The technique provides a shot-resolved diagnostic for the transparency onset, which can help optimize laser-driven proton acceleration.

title: First-principles-based Description Of ${\mathrm{VO}}_{2}$ Using $\mathrm{DFT}+\mathrm{DMFT}$ With Bond-centered Orbitals
authors: Peter Mlkvik, Nicola A. Spaldin, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Mlkvik, Nicola A. Spaldin, and Claude Ederer

We present a combined density-functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) study of the full structural phase space of rutile-based vanadium dioxide [MATH], including also the less studied M2 and T phases, using an unconventional bond-centered orbital basis. The use of…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033342] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: A DFT+DMFT study of the full structural phase space of rutile-based vanadium dioxide using an unconventional bond-centered orbital basis.
motivation: VO2 exhibits a rich phase diagram with metal-insulator transitions that remain challenging to describe from first principles, motivating a more accurate and physically transparent computational framework.
method: The authors combine density-functional theory with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT) in a bond-centered orbital basis to study rutile, M2, and T phases of VO2.
result: The bond-centered orbital approach captures the structural and electronic properties across the phase space, including the less-studied M2 and T phases.
conclusion: Bond-centered orbitals offer a viable first-principles route for describing strongly correlated vanadium dioxide phases within DFT+DMFT.

title: Enduring Mechanical Memory From The Constitutive Response Of Elastically Recoverable Nanostructured Materials
authors: Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, And Ramathasan Thevamaran
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, and Ramathasan Thevamaran

Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams exhibit return point memory, opening new opportunities for mechanical computing applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031073] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams exhibit return point memory, enabling mechanical computing applications.
motivation: To explore mechanical memory and computing using elastically recoverable nanostructured materials.
method: Experimental characterization of the constitutive response of vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams, focusing on return point memory.
result: The carbon nanotube foams demonstrate return point memory and elastic recoverability, allowing reversible mechanical states.
conclusion: These findings open new opportunities for mechanical computing based on nanostructured materials.

title: Unraveling Non-polymorphic Phase Evolution In Mg-Ag-Sb For Designing Thermally Recoverable Thermoelectrics
authors: Shizhen Zhi, Xiaojing Ma, Shanghao Chen, Tianyu Zhang, Yao Xu, Jiang Chen, Sheng Ye, Chenhao Lin, Linmao Wen, Jinxuan Cheng, Rongpei Shi, Xingjun Liu, Feng Cao, Lijun Zhang, Yuhao Fu, Qian Zhang, And Jun Mao
abstract:
Author(s): Shizhen Zhi, Xiaojing Ma, Shanghao Chen, Tianyu Zhang, Yao Xu, Jiang Chen, Sheng Ye, Chenhao Lin, Linmao Wen, Jinxuan Cheng, Rongpei Shi, Xingjun Liu, Feng Cao, Lijun Zhang, Yuhao Fu, Qian Zhang, and Jun Mao

Thermal degradation in MgAgSb thermoelectric material can be reversed with low-temperature annealing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031035] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates non-polymorphic phase evolution in MgAgSb thermoelectric materials to enable thermally recoverable thermoelectric performance via low-temperature annealing.
motivation: Thermal degradation limits the long-term usability of MgAgSb thermoelectric materials, and understanding the phase evolution responsible for degradation could allow performance to be restored rather than permanently lost.
method: The authors combine structural and microstructural characterization with phase-evolution analysis to identify the non-polymorphic phase transitions occurring in MgAgSb during thermal cycling, and test whether low-temperature annealing reverses degradation.
result: Thermal degradation in MgAgSb is shown to be reversible through low-temperature annealing, enabled by the identified non-polymorphic phase evolution pathway.
conclusion: Understanding and controlling phase evolution in MgAgSb provides a route to thermally recoverable thermoelectrics, improving material durability for energy-harvesting applications.

title: Evolution Of Polycrystallinity In Homogeneously Nucleated Colloidal Crystals
authors: Merin Jose, Nicholas H. P. Orr, Taiki Yanagishima, And Roel P. A. Dullens
abstract:
Author(s): Merin Jose, Nicholas H. P. Orr, Taiki Yanagishima, and Roel P. A. Dullens

Direct observations of the birth and growth of polycrystalline colloidal crystals clarify the role of grain formation, a key aspect in understanding and tuning the properties of polycrystalline materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031036] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: Direct imaging of homogeneously nucleated colloidal crystals reveals how polycrystallinity emerges through grain formation and growth.
motivation: Understanding grain formation in polycrystalline materials is key to tuning their properties, but direct observations of the birth and growth of grains are rare.
method: The authors use colloidal crystals as a model system and perform direct real-space observations of homogeneous nucleation and subsequent polycrystalline evolution.
result: They clarify the role of grain formation and growth, providing a microscopic picture of how polycrystallinity develops in a nucleating colloidal assembly.
conclusion: The findings offer insights into tuning polycrystalline materials by controlling nucleation and grain evolution in colloidal model systems.

title: Origins And Predictability Of The Hydrostatic Limit Of Molecular Liquids
authors: Cecilia M. S. Alvares, Cameron J. G. Wilson, Nicholas P. Funnell, Mark S. Senn, And Gabriele C. Sosso
abstract:
Author(s): Cecilia M. S. Alvares, Cameron J. G. Wilson, Nicholas P. Funnell, Mark S. Senn, and Gabriele C. Sosso

Loss of hydrostaticity limits high-pressure experiments, as pressure transmitting media solidify under compression. Here, we report a strong and positive correlation between the increase of molar density with pressure ([MATH]) and the hydrostatic limit (HL) associated with the vitrification of isotherm…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035433] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper correlates the pressure-dependent increase in molar density of molecular liquids with their hydrostatic limit, which is set by vitrification under high pressure.
motivation: Loss of hydrostaticity limits the fidelity of high-pressure experiments because pressure-transmitting media solidify under compression, so predicting the hydrostatic limit is practically important.
method: The authors use molecular dynamics simulations combined with high-pressure experiments to track molar density changes and vitrification behavior across isothermal compression of molecular liquids.
result: A strong positive correlation is found between the rate of molar density increase with pressure and the hydrostatic limit associated with vitrification.
conclusion: The observed correlation offers a route to predict the hydrostatic limit of molecular liquids from density–pressure behaviour, aiding the design of high-pressure experiments.

title: Structural Crossovers Of Quasi-one-dimensional Patchy Hard Superellipses
authors: Sakineh Mizani, Martin Oettel, Péter Gurin, And Szabolcs Varga
abstract:
Author(s): Sakineh Mizani, Martin Oettel, Péter Gurin, and Szabolcs Varga

We study a quasi-one-dimensional associating fluid composed of hard superellipses carrying two patches interacting through a directional Kern-Frenkel potential. Using the transfer operator method, we show that the selective patch-patch association promotes horizontal alignment and chain formation at…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035431] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a quasi-one-dimensional fluid of hard superellipses with two patches using transfer operator methods, revealing structural crossovers and chain formation driven by directional patch-patch interactions.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how anisotropic shape and selective patchy interactions control self-assembly and ordering in quasi-one-dimensional associating fluids.
method: They model hard superellipses with two patches interacting via a Kern-Frenkel potential and apply the transfer operator method to compute structural and thermodynamic properties.
result: Selective patch-patch association promotes horizontal alignment and chain formation, leading to structural crossovers as density or interaction strength varies.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the phase behavior and assembly of patchy anisotropic particles in confined quasi-one-dimensional systems, relevant to soft matter and statistical mechanics.

title: Global Warming Drives Connectivity Loss Among Climate Tipping Elements
authors: Tomas Scagliarini, Lorenzo Gamba, Antonello Provenzale, Timothy M. Lenton, And Manlio de Domenico
abstract:
Author(s): Tomas Scagliarini, Lorenzo Gamba, Antonello Provenzale, Timothy M. Lenton, and Manlio De Domenico

This article is part of a Physical Review Collection on the
tldr: The paper uses complex-network analysis to show that global warming weakens the connectivity among Earth-system climate tipping elements.
motivation: Climate tipping elements can undergo abrupt, irreversible transitions, and understanding how they interact and coevolve as the climate warms is crucial for anticipating cascading regime shifts.
method: The authors model tipping elements as nodes in a network and quantify changes in their connectivity as a function of projected global warming, analyzing the coevolution of these interacting subsystems.
result: Increasing global warming is found to drive a systematic loss of connectivity among the tipping elements, indicating a reorganization of the Earth-system interaction network.
conclusion: Warming-induced connectivity loss could alter the collective dynamics and cascade risks of climate tipping elements, with implications for planetary-scale stability.

title: Loop Expansion In Polymer Field Theory: Application To Phase Separation
authors: Kiyoharu Kawana And Kyosuke Adachi
abstract:
Author(s): Kiyoharu Kawana and Kyosuke Adachi

Liquid-liquid phase separation underlies phenomena ranging from protein condensate formation to the phase coexistence of synthetic polymers. Although the random phase approximation (RPA) is widely used to predict such phase behavior, its quantitative accuracy for binodals of polymer solutions, parti…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033343] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper applies a loop expansion in polymer field theory to improve predictions of liquid-liquid phase separation beyond the random phase approximation.
motivation: The random phase approximation (RPA) is widely used to predict phase behavior of polymer solutions but has limited quantitative accuracy for binodals.
method: The authors develop a systematic loop expansion in polymer field theory and apply it to calculate phase separation properties.
result: The loop expansion yields corrections to RPA predictions, potentially improving the accuracy of binodals and phase coexistence for polymer systems.
conclusion: This work provides a field-theoretic framework for more accurate description of liquid-liquid phase separation in polymer solutions.

title: Real-Space Visualization Of The Intrinsic Aging In $n$-type ${\mathrm{Mg}}_{3}(\mathrm{Sb},\mathrm{Bi}{)}_{2}$ Thermoelectrics
authors: Yuxiang Gong, Nuo Qu, Sumayya, Yu-Ke Zhu, Jianbo Zhu, Tinglu Song, Qianru Lin, Lankun Wang, Ran Xin, Fengkai Guo, Wei Cai, Yuan Yu, Jiehe Sui, And Zihang Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxiang Gong, Nuo Qu, Sumayya, Yu-Ke Zhu, Jianbo Zhu, Tinglu Song, Qianru Lin, Lankun Wang, Ran Xin, Fengkai Guo, Wei Cai, Yuan Yu, Jiehe Sui, and Zihang Liu

Spontaneous degradation of an Mg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031049] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: Real-space imaging reveals that intrinsic defect relaxation, rather than external stimuli, drives the spontaneous long-timescale degradation of n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 thermoelectric materials.
motivation: n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 is a leading thermoelectric material, but its spontaneous aging degrades performance and the microscopic origin of this degradation is unclear.
method: The authors use real-space visualization techniques (microscopy/spectroscopy) to track defect evolution in the material over long timescales without external driving.
result: Intrinsic defect relaxations are shown to govern the long-timescale property evolution, demonstrating that spontaneous degradation originates internally rather than from external stimuli.
conclusion: Understanding intrinsic aging mechanisms is essential for stabilizing n-type Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 thermoelectrics and improving their long-term device reliability.

title: Deformation And Organization Of Droplet-Encapsulated Soft Beads
authors: Shunsuke Saita, Finn Bastian Molzahn, Clara Delahousse, Julien Husson, And Charles N. Baroud
abstract:
Author(s): Shunsuke Saita, Finn Bastian Molzahn, Clara Delahousse, Julien Husson, and Charles N. Baroud

Many biological, culinary, and engineering processes lead to the coencapsulation of several soft particles within a liquid interface. In these situations the particles are bound together by the capillary forces that deform them and influence their biological or rheological properties. Here, we intro…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 148203] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how soft beads coencapsulated within a droplet deform and organize under capillary forces, affecting their biological or rheological properties.
motivation: Many biological, culinary, and engineering processes involve coencapsulation of soft particles at liquid interfaces, but the interplay between capillary deformation and particle organization is not well understood.
method: The authors introduce an experimental system of droplet-encapsulated soft beads and analyze their deformation and collective organization driven by capillary interactions.
result: The study characterizes how capillary forces bind and deform the soft particles, leading to distinct organizational patterns that depend on interfacial and elastic properties.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into soft matter physics and rheology of encapsulated particle systems, but have no direct relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Observation Of $\mathrm{ϒ}(1\mathrm{S})+Z$ Associated Production And Measurement Of The Effective Double-Parton Scattering Cross Section In Proton-Proton Collisions At $\sqrt{s}=13\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{TeV}$
authors: A. Hayrapetyan et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. Hayrapetyan et al. (CMS Collaboration)

The observation of the associated production of an [MATH] meson with a [MATH] boson and a measurement of the ratio of its fiducial cross section to the fiducial cross section of the [MATH] boson are presented. Both the [MATH] meson and the [MATH] boson are identified via…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 141902] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The CMS Collaboration reports the first observation of associated production of a Upsilon(1S) meson with a Z boson in proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV and measures the effective double-parton scattering cross section.
motivation: Associated production of quarkonium and electroweak bosons provides a probe of double-parton scattering and quantum chromodynamics, but had not been observed for Upsilon(1S)+Z.
method: The analysis uses proton-proton collision data at sqrt(s)=13 TeV collected by the CMS detector, identifying Upsilon(1S) via its dimuon decay and Z boson via its dilepton decay, and extracting the fiducial cross section ratio.
result: The Upsilon(1S)+Z production is observed with a significance exceeding 5 standard deviations, and the ratio of its fiducial cross section to the Z boson fiducial cross section is measured, yielding an effective double-parton scattering cross section consistent with expectations.
conclusion: This measurement establishes Upsilon(1S)+Z associated production as a new channel for studying double-parton scattering and provides constraints on effective cross sections in high-energy proton-proton collisions.

title: Real-Space Hybrid Topological Singularities In Structured Elastic Waves
authors: Tong Fu, Pengfei Zhao, Liyou Luo, Zhiling Zhou, Dong Liu, Wanyue Xiao, Jensen Li, And Shubo Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Tong Fu, Pengfei Zhao, Liyou Luo, Zhiling Zhou, Dong Liu, Wanyue Xiao, Jensen Li, and Shubo Wang

Real-space singularities govern a broad spectrum of wave phenomena, yet they remain largely unexplored in elastic wave systems. Here, we report hybrid topological singularities that emerge on the surfaces of finite-sized solids due to the full vectorial character of elastic waves. These textures fus…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 146604] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports hybrid topological singularities appearing on the surfaces of finite-sized elastic solids, arising from the full vectorial nature of elastic waves.
motivation: Real-space singularities govern many wave phenomena but have remained largely unexplored in elastic wave systems, motivating their study in vectorial elastic media.
method: The authors analyze the vectorial polarization textures of structured elastic (phononic) waves in finite-sized solids to identify and classify hybrid topological singularities on their surfaces.
result: Hybrid topological singularities are shown to emerge on solid surfaces due to the vectorial character of elastic waves, fusing multiple singularity types into new textures.
conclusion: The findings extend topological singularity physics into elastic wave systems, suggesting new routes for controlling elastic/acoustic wave behavior via surface topology.

title: Effect Of Composition And Pressure On Diamond Formation Timescales From Hydrocarbon Demixing At Icy Planetary Interior Conditions
authors: Mungo Frost et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Mungo Frost et al.

Under extreme conditions hydrocarbons are known to demix, forming diamond and a hydrogen-rich phase. Here, the authors probe the timescale of this process as a function of pressure and composition. Various hydrocarbon samples were compressed to between 20 and 80 GPa in diamond anvil cells prior to serial x-ray free electron laser heating and time-resolved diffraction. They find that carbon-rich precursors form diamond in 10s of microseconds over the whole pressure range, while hydrogen rich ones take longer. [Image credit: Greg Stewart/SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204101] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper measures how fast diamond forms from demixing hydrocarbons under extreme pressure and temperature conditions relevant to icy planetary interiors.
motivation: Hydrocarbon demixing into diamond and hydrogen-rich phases is thought to occur inside icy planets, but the kinetics and composition/pressure dependence of this process were poorly constrained.
method: Various hydrocarbon samples were compressed to 20–80 GPa in diamond anvil cells and heated with serial x-ray free electron laser pulses, with diamond formation tracked via time-resolved x-ray diffraction.
result: Carbon-rich precursors converted to diamond within tens of microseconds across the entire pressure range, whereas hydrogen-rich precursors required substantially longer timescales.
conclusion: Diamond formation kinetics in icy planetary interiors depend strongly on hydrocarbon composition and pressure, informing models of planetary interior evolution.

title: Emergence Of Cooperation In Nonlinear Higher-order Public Goods Games
authors: Jaume Llabrés, Onkar Sadekar, Federico Malizia, And Federico Battiston
abstract:
Author(s): Jaume Llabrés, Onkar Sadekar, Federico Malizia, and Federico Battiston

Evolutionary game theory has provided substantial contributions to explain the emergence of cooperation under unfavorable conditions in ecology, economics, and the social sciences. Recently, inspired by newly available empirical evidence on group interactions, higher-order networks have emerged as a…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034316] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how cooperation emerges in nonlinear public goods games played on higher-order networks, where group interactions beyond pairwise links shape evolutionary outcomes.
motivation: Empirical evidence shows many social and ecological interactions occur in groups rather than pairwise, motivating models that go beyond dyadic networks to explain sustained cooperation under unfavorable conditions.
method: The authors formulate evolutionary dynamics of nonlinear public goods games on higher-order (hypergraph/simplicial) structures, analyzing how group size, nonlinear payoff functions, and higher-order connectivity affect the evolution of cooperation.
result: Cooperation can be promoted or suppressed depending on the nonlinearity of the public goods payoff and the structure of higher-order group interactions, revealing distinct dynamical regimes absent in pairwise network models.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions qualitatively reshape the emergence of cooperation, underscoring the need for group-level network descriptions in evolutionary game theory.

title: Polarized Neutrons For The Study Of Individual And Collective Fast Dynamics In Proteins
authors: Agathe Nidriche, Jacques Ollivier, J. Ross Stewart, And Judith Peters
abstract:
Author(s): Agathe Nidriche, Jacques Ollivier, J. Ross Stewart, and Judith Peters

Neutron scattering is a powerful technique to investigate atomic structures and molecular dynamics of proteins at the nanoscale. When it comes to dynamics, incoherent and coherent scattering respectively provide information on the single and collective dynamics of nuclei. In proteins, hydrogen has t…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034413] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: A neutron scattering study exploiting polarized neutrons to separate incoherent (single-particle) and coherent (collective) fast dynamics of hydrogen-bearing nuclei in proteins.
motivation: Protein function depends on nanoscale molecular motions, and distinguishing individual from collective dynamics requires scattering techniques that can isolate coherent and incoherent contributions.
method: Polarized neutron scattering (with spin-analysis to separate coherent/incoherent channels) combined with quasielastic/spectroscopic measurements on protein samples to probe picosecond-timescale hydrogen dynamics.
result: The measurements resolve and characterize single-particle versus collective fast dynamical modes in proteins, demonstrating the utility of polarized neutrons for deconvolving the two scattering contributions.
conclusion: Polarized neutron scattering provides a viable route to separately access individual and collective protein dynamics, informing biophysical models of protein function.

title: Active Transport As A Mechanism Of Microphase Selection In Biomolecular Condensates
authors: Le Qiao, Peter Gispert, Lukas S. Stelzl, And Friederike Schmid
abstract:
Author(s): Le Qiao, Peter Gispert, Lukas S. Stelzl, and Friederike Schmid

The size and organization of biomolecular condensates formed by liquid-liquid phase separation are set by multiple cellular mechanisms that are not yet fully understood. Here, we identify a transport-driven mechanism: Stochastic binding of phase-separating proteins to cytoskeletal motor proteins, fo…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033345] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that stochastic binding of phase-separating proteins to cytoskeletal motor proteins creates an active transport mechanism that selects the size and microphase organization of biomolecular condensates.
motivation: The size and internal organization of biomolecular condensates formed by liquid-liquid phase separation are governed by cellular mechanisms that remain poorly understood, motivating a search for physical mechanisms that set condensate microphase selection.
method: The authors model stochastic binding of phase-separating proteins to cytoskeletal motor proteins, driving active transport within and around condensates, likely via theory and simulation of the resulting non-equilibrium phase behavior.
result: Active transport arising from motor-protein binding is identified as a mechanism that selects specific condensate microphases and controls their size.
conclusion: Transport-driven non-equilibrium effects provide a generic route to microphase selection in biomolecular condensates, complementing passive thermodynamic descriptions of phase separation.

title: Reversibility, Chaos, And Attractors In Periodically Sheared Elastic Filaments
authors: Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia Du Roure, Anke Lindner, And David Saintillan
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia du Roure, Anke Lindner, and David Saintillan

Combining experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations, a previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible filaments under periodic shear is unveiled.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031067] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Experiments and simulations on actin filaments under periodic shear reveal a transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible filaments.
motivation: Understanding how semiflexible filaments behave under periodic driving is important for nonequilibrium soft-matter and biological physics, but the reversibility-to-chaos transition in single filaments was previously unexplored.
method: Combined experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations of semiflexible filaments subjected to periodic shear flow.
result: A previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaotic dynamics is observed in single semiflexible filaments.
conclusion: Periodic shear can drive semiflexible filaments into chaotic dynamics, revealing new nonequilibrium behavior in driven elastic filaments.

title: Erratum: Temperature Dependence Of $ρ$- And ${a}_{1}$-Meson Masses And Mixing Of Vector And Axial-Vector Correlators [Phys. Rev. Lett. 88, 042002 (2002)]
authors: Michael Urban, Michael Buballa, And Jochen Wambach
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Urban, Michael Buballa, and Jochen Wambach
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 149901] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the authors' 2002 Physical Review Letters paper on the temperature dependence of rho- and a1-meson masses and mixing between vector and axial-vector correlators.
motivation: The original work addressed how hadronic spectral properties change in a hot medium, a topic in finite-temperature QCD and nuclear physics.
method: As an erratum, it provides corrections to the published article rather than introducing a new theoretical or experimental method.
result: The erratum lists specific corrections to the original results on temperature-dependent meson masses and correlator mixing.
conclusion: The correction ensures the accuracy of the original findings but does not advance quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Neutron Drip Line In Calcium Isotopes From A Chiral Interaction
authors: B. S. Hu, A. Ekström, C. Forssén, G. Hagen, W. G. Jiang, T. Miyagi, And T. Papenbrock
abstract:
Author(s): B. S. Hu, A. Ekström, C. Forssén, G. Hagen, W. G. Jiang, T. Miyagi, and T. Papenbrock

Interactions derived from effective field theories of quantum chromodynamics have thus far failed to bind calcium nuclei beyond neutron number [MATH], while nuclear density functionals typically place the neutron drip line near [MATH], at [MATH]. We present the chiral interaction ${\math…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 142502] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes the neutron drip line of calcium isotopes using a new chiral interaction derived from effective field theory.
motivation: Effective field theory interactions from QCD have previously failed to bind calcium nuclei beyond a certain neutron number, while density functional theory places the drip line differently; resolving this discrepancy is important for nuclear structure.
method: The authors employ a chiral interaction from effective field theory and perform ab initio many-body calculations for calcium isotopes to determine the neutron drip line.
result: The chiral interaction binds calcium isotopes beyond the previously inaccessible neutron number and predicts a drip line that may align with density functional expectations.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that chiral interactions can successfully describe neutron-rich calcium isotopes and provides a benchmark for nuclear theory.

title: Solubility Enhanced Surfactant-Induced Flow In Air-Liquid-Air Sheets
authors: Jun Eshima, Tristan Aurégan, Emmanuel Villermaux, Howard A. Stone, And Luc Deike
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Eshima, Tristan Aurégan, Emmanuel Villermaux, Howard A. Stone, and Luc Deike

Liquid interfaces appear throughout nature and engineering and are typically contaminated by surface active agents (surfactants), which are characterized by a wide range of solubility. We demonstrate that solubility enhances by an order of magnitude surfactant-induced flow in air-liquid-air films, i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 144001] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how surfactant solubility enhances surfactant-induced flows in air-liquid-air films.
motivation: Surfactants are ubiquitous at liquid interfaces, but the influence of their solubility on interfacial flows in thin air-liquid-air sheets is not fully understood.
method: The authors experimentally and theoretically analyze flow in air-liquid-air films with surfactants of varying solubility, characterizing the induced Marangoni flows.
result: Solubility enhances surfactant-induced flow by an order of magnitude in these films, and the paper explains the mechanism underlying this enhancement.
conclusion: Surfactant solubility is a key parameter controlling interfacial flow in air-liquid-air sheets, with implications for natural and engineering systems involving contaminated interfaces.

title: Observation Of Nuclear Suppression In Coherent $\mathrm{ϒ}(1\mathrm{S})$ Photoproduction Off Heavy Nuclei At The Lhc
authors: A. Belyaev et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. Belyaev et al. (CMS Collaboration)

The first measurement of coherent [MATH] meson photoproduction off heavy nuclei is performed using ultraperipheral lead-lead collisions collected by the CMS experiment at a nucleon-nucleon center-of-mass energy of 5.02 TeV. The nuclear gluonic structure is probed at a nucleon mome…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 142301] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The CMS collaboration reports the first measurement of coherent Upsilon(1S) photoproduction off heavy nuclei in ultraperipheral PbPb collisions, observing nuclear suppression.
motivation: To probe nuclear gluonic structure and test gluon shadowing/saturation effects at small nucleon momentum fractions.
method: Ultraperipheral lead-lead collisions at 5.02 TeV were analyzed for coherent Upsilon(1S) photoproduction, and the measured cross section was compared to theoretical predictions.
result: A significant nuclear suppression of coherent Upsilon(1S) photoproduction is observed relative to expectations from unscaled proton-proton data.
conclusion: The measurement provides new constraints on nuclear gluon distributions and supports the presence of gluon shadowing or saturation in heavy nuclei.

title: Susceptible-infectious-susceptible Epidemics On Temporal Contact Graphs With Clique Structure
authors: Robin Persoons And Piet van Mieghem
abstract:
Author(s): Robin Persoons and Piet Van Mieghem

We consider temporal networks that are a union of disjoint cliques at all times [MATH]. We call temporal networks that consist of disjoint cliques temporal clique graphs. We extend the exact solution of mean-field SIS epidemics with self-infections on the complete graph, derived by Prasse et al. [
tldr: The paper extends the exact mean-field solution of SIS epidemics with self-infections from complete graphs to temporal networks composed of disjoint cliques.
motivation: Temporal networks with clique structure arise in many contact processes, but exact epidemic solutions for such networks are lacking beyond the complete-graph case.
method: The authors analytically solve a mean-field SIS model on temporal clique graphs, generalizing the Prasse et al. exact solution for complete graphs with self-infections.
result: An exact solution for the SIS epidemic dynamics on temporal clique graphs is derived, characterizing the prevalence in terms of network and infection parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for understanding epidemic spreading on temporal networks with clique organization, though it lies outside quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Instability Of Solutions In A Mass-conserving Reaction Diffusion System
authors: R. Marangell, J. J. Wylie, And B. H. Bradshaw-Hajek
abstract:
Author(s): R. Marangell, J. J. Wylie, and B. H. Bradshaw-Hajek

We study the spectral stability of traveling and stationary front and pulse solutions in a class of degenerate reaction diffusion systems. We characterize the essential spectrum of the linearized operator in full generality and identify conditions under which it lies entirely in the left half plane.…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034225] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spectral stability of traveling and stationary front and pulse solutions in a mass-conserving degenerate reaction-diffusion system.
motivation: Reaction-diffusion systems with mass conservation and degeneracy arise in various physical and biological contexts, but their stability properties are not fully understood.
method: The authors linearize the system around traveling and stationary solutions and characterize the essential spectrum of the linearized operator in full generality.
result: They identify conditions under which the essential spectrum lies entirely in the left half-plane, yielding stability criteria for the solutions.
conclusion: The work provides a general spectral stability framework for degenerate mass-conserving reaction-diffusion systems, with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Avalanche Assemblies In Arbitrary Connection Topologies
authors: Maik Schünemann, Marc Kesseböhmer, And Udo Ernst
abstract:
Author(s): Maik Schünemann, Marc Kesseböhmer, and Udo Ernst

Complex systems are commonly modeled as networks of units that integrate external input and emit brief pulses of activity upon reaching a threshold. Such pulse-coupled interactions can give rise to cascades of activity propagating through the network in the form of avalanches. While the statistics o…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034414] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies avalanche dynamics in networks of pulse-coupled units with arbitrary connection topologies, analyzing cascade statistics.
motivation: Complex systems often exhibit cascading activity, and understanding how connection topology shapes avalanche statistics is important for network dynamics.
method: The authors model networks of threshold units that emit pulses and analytically or numerically investigate avalanche propagation under arbitrary connection topologies.
result: They characterize how avalanche statistics depend on the underlying network topology, extending prior results beyond specific connectivity structures.
conclusion: The findings provide a general framework for avalanche assemblies in diverse network architectures, relevant to complex systems and neuroscience.

title: Time-nonlocal Internal-variable Lb-pf Model For Continuous Nucleation During Dendritic Solidification
authors: Borui Zhao And Dongke Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Borui Zhao and Dongke Sun

Continuous nucleation in nonequilibrium solidification is often treated as an instantaneous response controlled by the current undercooling. In welding, casting, and layer-wise metal additive manufacturing, however, liquid regions can undergo nonmonotonic thermal histories and reach similar undercoo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 035310] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a time-nonlocal internal-variable Lb-pf model for continuous nucleation during dendritic solidification, capturing nonmonotonic thermal histories in metal additive manufacturing.
motivation: Continuous nucleation in nonequilibrium solidification is typically modeled as instantaneous, which fails for processes like welding and additive manufacturing where liquid regions experience nonmonotonic thermal histories.
method: A time-nonlocal internal-variable phase-field (Lb-pf) model is developed to incorporate memory effects in nucleation, likely using a history-dependent nucleation rate.
result: The model reproduces nucleation behavior under nonmonotonic undercooling and may better predict grain structures in solidification processes.
conclusion: Time-nonlocal effects are important for accurately modeling continuous nucleation in complex thermal histories relevant to metal additive manufacturing.

title: Self-propulsion In The One-dimensional Swarmalator Model
authors: Kevin P. O'keeffe
abstract:
Author(s): Kevin P. O'Keeffe

We study the one-dimensional swarmalator model with self-propulsion [MATH], where [MATH] is the body orientation. The static states of the ordinary model unfold into traveling, breathing, split-wave, and chaotic states, two of which admit analytic reductions: A traveling two-cluster …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034223] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a one-dimensional swarmalator model with self-propulsion, showing that static states transition into traveling, breathing, split-wave, and chaotic states.
motivation: The swarmalator model combines spatial swarming with oscillator synchronization, and adding self-propulsion may reveal new dynamical phases relevant to active matter.
method: The authors analyze the one-dimensional swarmalator model with self-propulsion through numerical simulations and analytic reductions for traveling two-cluster states.
result: They identify traveling, breathing, split-wave, and chaotic states, with two states admitting analytic reduction, and characterize the transitions from static states.
conclusion: Self-propulsion enriches the swarmalator model with novel nonequilibrium phases, though the work remains within classical active matter and nonlinear dynamics.

title: Growth Bistability In Small Bacterial Populations Exposed To Antibiotics
authors: B. Ledoux And D. Lacoste
abstract:
Author(s): B. Ledoux and D. Lacoste

With the development of microfluidics, it has now become possible to assess the susceptibility of bacteria to antibiotics at the single-cell level instead of relying on population measurements. Such studies are particularly relevant when the growth of a bacterial population in the presence of antibi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034411] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates growth bistability in small bacterial populations exposed to antibiotics using microfluidics and single-cell measurements.
motivation: Single-cell antibiotic susceptibility studies can reveal population heterogeneity that bulk measurements miss, which is important for understanding bacterial growth under antibiotic stress.
method: The authors use microfluidics to assess bacterial growth at the single-cell level and likely develop or analyze a model of growth bistability in small populations.
result: The study characterizes conditions under which small bacterial populations exhibit bistable growth in response to antibiotics.
conclusion: Growth bistability may have implications for antibiotic tolerance and the interpretation of single-cell susceptibility assays.

title: Curvature In Infectious Disease Network: A Metric For Vaccination And Control
authors: Sara Najem
abstract:
Author(s): Sara Najem

We investigate the geometric structure of evolving infectious-disease networks using a notion of node curvature, which is based on the heat-kernel expansion that naturally extends to edges. Applying this measure to networks reconstructed from infection counts whose degree and strength distributions …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 034312] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a node-curvature metric based on heat-kernel expansion to characterize the geometry of evolving infectious-disease contact networks and guide vaccination and control strategies.
motivation: Understanding the geometric structure of epidemic networks could reveal structural vulnerabilities and improve targeted vaccination or intervention strategies beyond traditional degree- and strength-based measures.
method: The authors define node curvature via the heat-kernel expansion extended to edges and apply it to networks reconstructed from infection count data with varying degree and strength distributions.
result: The curvature measure distinguishes network structures and identifies nodes whose removal or vaccination would most disrupt epidemic spread, correlating with control efficacy.
conclusion: Curvature provides a useful geometric diagnostic for epidemic networks, offering a quantitative basis for prioritizing vaccination and control interventions.

title: Endocytosis Shapes Extracellular Chemical Gradients In Autonomous Cell-cell Attraction
authors: Jeremy Barrios, Andrew Goetz, Susan E. Leggett, And Purushottam D. Dixit
abstract:
Author(s): Jeremy Barrios, Andrew Goetz, Susan E. Leggett, and Purushottam D. Dixit

Receptor-mediated ligand endocytosis underlies essential homeostatic functions and in signaling contexts it is often regarded as a mechanism for signal attenuation. Here, we show that ligand removal can paradoxically enhance directional information in autonomous cell-cell attraction. Many cell syste…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033374] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: Ligand endocytosis can enhance directional information in autonomous cell-cell attraction by reshaping extracellular chemical gradients.
motivation: Receptor-mediated endocytosis is often viewed as a signal attenuation mechanism, but its effect on directional information in cell-cell communication is unclear.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and analysis of extracellular chemical gradients to study how ligand removal by endocytosis affects cell-cell attraction.
result: They find that endocytosis can paradoxically increase directional information and improve autonomous cell-cell attraction.
conclusion: Ligand endocytosis may play a constructive role in cell signaling by shaping gradients to enhance directional sensing during cell-cell attraction.

title: Identification Of Distortions To The Ni Atomic Potential At 100 GPa With Temperature Measurements
authors: D. A. Chin, G. Hess, E. A. Smith, M. E. Signor, D. T. Bishel, G. Bunker, S. Boccato, R. Torchio, S. Bonev, Y. Ping, H. Sio, S. Anzellini, T. Irifune, N. Abdolrahim, P. M. Nilson, J. R. Rygg, And G. W. Collins
abstract:
Author(s): D. A. Chin, G. Hess, E. A. Smith, M. E. Signor, D. T. Bishel, G. Bunker, S. Boccato, R. Torchio, S. Bonev, Y. Ping, H. Sio, S. Anzellini, T. Irifune, N. Abdolrahim, P. M. Nilson, J. R. Rygg, and G. W. Collins

Characterizing the temperature of materials in high-energy-density (HED) experiments is a major gap in the benchmarking of HED matter, such as matter in the deep interiors of planets and low-mass stars. Extended x-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy is one of the few techniques capabl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033372] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: Temperature measurements using EXAFS spectroscopy identify distortions in the nickel atomic potential at 100 GPa, relevant to high-energy-density matter.
motivation: Characterizing temperature in high-energy-density experiments is crucial for benchmarking matter in planetary interiors and low-mass stars.
method: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy is used to measure temperature and extract details of the Ni atomic potential under extreme pressure.
result: The measurements reveal distortions to the Ni atomic potential at 100 GPa that affect temperature determination in warm dense nickel.
conclusion: These findings improve models of high-energy-density matter and provide constraints for planetary interior simulations.

title: High-dimensional Inverse Design Of Inertial Fusion Implosions Via Differentiable Simulation
authors: A. J. Crilly, P. Travis, J. P. Brodrick, J. B. Coughlin, And A. S. Joglekar
abstract:
Author(s): A. J. Crilly, P. Travis, J. P. Brodrick, J. B. Coughlin, and A. S. Joglekar

Inertial confinement fusion implosion design requires simultaneous optimization of strongly coupled target and driver parameters across high-dimensional design spaces. Existing automated design approaches typically rely on nondifferentiable radiation-hydrodynamics codes treated as black boxes, makin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033353] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a differentiable simulation framework for high-dimensional inverse design of inertial confinement fusion implosions.
motivation: Inertial confinement fusion implosion design requires optimizing many coupled target and driver parameters, but existing automated approaches treat nondifferentiable radiation-hydrodynamics codes as black boxes.
method: The authors develop differentiable radiation-hydrodynamics simulations and use gradient-based optimization to perform high-dimensional inverse design of ICF implosions.
result: The approach enables efficient optimization across high-dimensional design spaces, potentially yielding improved ICF implosion designs compared to black-box methods.
conclusion: Differentiable simulation offers a promising route for automated, high-dimensional inverse design in inertial confinement fusion and other complex physical systems.

title: Broadband Hard X-ray Attosecond Pulses From Extremely Chirped Electron Beams
authors: River R. Robles, Veronica Guo, David Cesar, Paris Franz, Aliaksei Halavanau, Alberto Lutman, Takahiro Sato, Sanghoon Song, Nicholas Sudar, Yanwen Sun, Zhen Zhang, Diling Zhu, And Agostino Marinelli
abstract:
Author(s): River R. Robles, Veronica Guo, David Cesar, Paris Franz, Aliaksei Halavanau, Alberto Lutman, Takahiro Sato, Sanghoon Song, Nicholas Sudar, Yanwen Sun, Zhen Zhang, Diling Zhu, and Agostino Marinelli

Attosecond pulses from free-electron lasers have opened the doors to atomic site-specific studies of bound electronic dynamics on their natural, subfemtosecond timescales. Key to their success has been electron beam shaping techniques enabling the generation of subfemtosecond current spikes with pea…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033350] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates broadband hard X-ray attosecond pulse generation from free-electron lasers using extremely chirped electron beams.
motivation: Attosecond X-ray pulses enable atomic site-specific studies of bound electronic dynamics on natural subfemtosecond timescales, but generating them with broad bandwidth remains challenging.
method: The authors employ electron beam shaping techniques to produce subfemtosecond current spikes with high peak current and controlled chirp in a free-electron laser.
result: They achieve broadband hard X-ray attosecond pulses suitable for probing ultrafast electronic dynamics.
conclusion: The work advances X-ray free-electron laser capabilities for attosecond science, but it is outside the quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems directions.

title: Fast Solidification Of A Gravity-Stretched Liquid Jet
authors: JS. Smink, CW. Visser, And H. Lhuissier
abstract:
Author(s): JS. Smink, CW. Visser, and H. Lhuissier

A new technique for generating solid fibers from a liquid jet is easier to model—and thus easier to control—than past methods.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 144004] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: A new technique produces solid fibers from a gravity-stretched liquid jet in a way that is simpler to model and control than previous methods.
motivation: Generating solid fibers from liquid jets is industrially useful, but existing methods are hard to model and therefore hard to control precisely.
method: The authors study a gravity-stretched liquid jet undergoing fast solidification, characterizing the jet dynamics and solidification front to derive a tractable model.
result: The proposed approach yields fibers whose formation is easier to model and control than in past fiber-drawing techniques (Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 144004).
conclusion: The work provides a better-understood route to solid fiber production, with potential for improved process control in fiber manufacturing.

title: Emergence Of Purely Elastoplastic Turbulence In Shear Flows
authors: Muhammad Abdullah, Shravan Pradeep, Doug J. Jerolmack, Becca Thomases, And Paulo E. Arratia
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Abdullah, Shravan Pradeep, Doug J. Jerolmack, Becca Thomases, and Paulo E. Arratia

Yield-stress fluids only flow above a critical stress. Here, we observe the emergence of a distinct, elasticity-driven flow state in a yield-stress fluid in the absence of inertia. Numerical simulations show that this elastoplastic turbulent state is characterized by non-Gaussian bimodal velocity di…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 144002] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the emergence of a purely elastoplastic turbulence state in yield-stress fluids under shear, driven by elasticity rather than inertia.
motivation: Yield-stress fluids only flow above a critical stress, and their behavior in the absence of inertia is not well understood, motivating a search for new flow states in this regime.
method: The authors combine experiments on a yield-stress fluid with numerical simulations to characterize a novel elasticity-driven flow state in the inertialess limit.
result: They identify an elastoplastic turbulent state marked by non-Gaussian bimodal velocity distributions, distinct from conventional inertial turbulence.
conclusion: The findings establish a new class of purely elastoplastic turbulence driven by elasticity, expanding the taxonomy of turbulent flow regimes.

title: Visualization Of The Chromatin Structure In Intact Nuclei Of Cancer Cells Using Small-angle X-ray Scattering
authors: E. G. Iashina, S. V. Grigoriev, E. Y. Varfolomeeva, R. A. Pantina, N. D. Fedorova, R. A. Kovalev, A. A. Piryazev, And D. A. Ivanov
abstract:
Author(s): E. G. Iashina, S. V. Grigoriev, E. Y. Varfolomeeva, R. A. Pantina, N. D. Fedorova, R. A. Kovalev, A. A. Piryazev, and D. A. Ivanov

Cancer cells show global changes in chromatin structure that lead to stable alterations in gene expression and potentially other nuclear functions. Small-angle neutron and x-ray scattering (SAXS) is one of the most informative and direct ways to study the chromatin structural organization on nanosca…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044402] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: Small-angle X-ray scattering is used to characterize the nanoscale chromatin structure in intact nuclei of cancer cells.
motivation: Cancer cells exhibit global changes in chromatin organization that alter gene expression and nuclear function, motivating a direct structural probe of chromatin at the nanoscale.
method: Small-angle neutron and X-ray scattering (SAXS/SANS) measurements are performed on intact nuclei of cancer cells and interpreted with structural models of chromatin organization.
result: The scattering data reveal characteristic features of chromatin packing in intact nuclei, allowing quantitative visualization of chromatin structural organization.
conclusion: SAXS provides a direct and informative route to probing chromatin architecture in cancer cells, offering structural insight relevant to cancer biology.

title: Production And Decay Dynamics Of The Charmed Baryon ${\mathrm{Λ}}_{c}^{+}$ In ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Annihilations Near Threshold
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)
