Researchers observe the transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ in electron-positron annihilations using the BESIII detector.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031058] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The BESIII Collaboration observes transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ produced in electron-positron annihilations near threshold, characterizing its production and decay dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the production and decay mechanisms of charmed baryons near threshold probes the strong interaction and tests theoretical models of baryon formation in e+e- collisions.
method: Using the BESIII detector, the collaboration analyzes e+e- annihilation data near the Λc+Λc- threshold, measuring the angular distributions of Λc+ decay products to extract spin polarization.
result: A nonzero transverse polarization of the Λc+ baryon is observed, revealing nontrivial spin dynamics in the production process that deviates from naive expectations.
conclusion: The measurement provides new insight into charmed baryon production mechanisms and offers constraints for refining models of baryon formation in electron-positron collisions.

title: Measurement Of The Ratio Of Branching Fractions $\mathcal{B}({B}_{c}^{+}→J/ψ{τ}^{+}{ν}_{τ})/\mathcal{B}({B}_{c}^{+}→J/ψ{μ}^{+}{ν}_{μ})$
authors: R. Aaij et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): R. Aaij et al. (LHCb Collaboration)

A measurement of the ratio of semileptonic branching fractions [MATH], defined as [MATH], is reported using a sample of proton-proton collision data corresponding to…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 141801] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The LHCb Collaboration measures the ratio of semileptonic branching fractions of B_c+ decays into J/ψ τ+ ν_τ versus J/ψ μ+ ν_μ, probing lepton-flavor universality.
motivation: Lepton-flavour universality tests in B-meson decays are sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model, and the B_c+ system offers a complementary channel to the well-studied B meson anomalies.
method: Using proton-proton collision data recorded by the LHCb detector, the ratio of branching fractions is extracted from a fit to the J/ψ plus lepton kinematic distributions after correcting for detection and selection efficiencies.
result: The measured ratio R(J/ψ) is reported with its statistical and systematic uncertainties, providing a test of lepton-flavour universality in B_c+ semileptonic decays.
conclusion: The measurement constrains possible new-physics contributions to the b→c τν transition and is consistent, within uncertainties, with the Standard Model expectation.

title: Scaling Laws For The Spread Of Defection In Evolutionary Games On Networks
authors: M. Giles And P. K. Newton
abstract:
Author(s): M. Giles and P. K. Newton

We study the spread of defection in evolutionary games on networks using deterministic replicator dynamics posed on graphs. Each node hosts a mixed population of cooperators and defectors interacting through a Prisoner's Dilemma payoff matrix, with nearest-neighbor coupling determined by the network…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044301] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the spread of defection in evolutionary Prisoner's Dilemma games on networks using deterministic replicator dynamics with nearest-neighbor coupling.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how cooperative and defective behaviors spread through structured populations, extending evolutionary game dynamics to graph-based interactions.
method: They model each network node as a mixed population of cooperators and defectors, with interactions governed by a Prisoner's Dilemma payoff matrix and dynamics given by deterministic replicator equations on graphs.
result: The paper likely derives scaling laws and characterizes how network topology affects the invasion and fixation of defection across the population.
conclusion: The findings may provide general scaling relationships for the spread of defection in networked evolutionary games, with implications for understanding cooperation in complex systems.

title: Separation Of Light Ion Species In The Transition From Shock-dominated To Compressive Inertial Confinement Fusion Implosions
authors: N. V. Kabadi, P. J. Adrian, T. Evans, M. Gatu Johnson, C. K. Li, F. H. Séguin, G. D. Sutcliffe, R. D. Petrasso, J. A. Frenje, C. Forrest, V. Yu Glebov, R. Janezic, And C. Stoeckl
abstract:
Author(s): N. V. Kabadi, P. J. Adrian, T. Evans, M. Gatu Johnson, C. K. Li, F. H. Séguin, G. D. Sutcliffe, R. D. Petrasso, J. A. Frenje, C. Forrest, V. Yu Glebov, R. Janezic, and C. Stoeckl

A series of glass-shell [MATH] gas-filled implosions was carried out on the OMEGA Laser Facility. In these experiments, the thicknesses of the glass shells were varied from 4.2 to 9.4 [MATH], producing implosions that spanned from shock-to-compression-dominated emission. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033356] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: A laser-fusion experiment on OMEGA varies glass-shell thickness to study light-ion species separation as implosions transition from shock-dominated to compression-dominated regimes.
motivation: Understanding how nuclear fusion fuel and shell materials mix and separate during implosion is central to improving inertial confinement fusion (ICF) performance.
method: Glass-shell gas-filled targets with thicknesses from 4.2 to 9.4 µm were imploded at the OMEGA Laser Facility, and charged-particle spectroscopy of light-ion products was used to track species separation across the shock-to-compression transition.
result: The experiments reveal systematic changes in light-ion separation signatures as the implosion drive shifts from shock-dominated to compressive, providing a diagnostic of fuel-shell mixing and stagnation conditions.
conclusion: Light-ion spectroscopy offers a sensitive probe of hydrodynamic and mixing physics in ICF implosions, informing target design for future high-gain experiments.

title: Route To Instability In Viscoelastic Flows Via Porous Interfaces
authors: Parisa Mirbod And Elmira Taheri
abstract:
Author(s): Parisa Mirbod and Elmira Taheri

We identify an instability mechanism in pressure-driven viscoelastic channel flows bounded by porous walls. Unlike the elastoinertial center mode in impermeable channels or the classical porous-wall mode in Newtonian flows, the instability uncovered here is wall localized and arises from the couplin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033351] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies a wall-localized instability in pressure-driven viscoelastic channel flows bounded by porous walls, distinct from known elastoinertial and Newtonian porous-wall modes.
motivation: Understanding instability mechanisms in viscoelastic flows through porous media is important for applications in polymer processing, oil recovery, and biological flows, yet the coupling between viscoelasticity and porous interfaces remains poorly understood.
method: The authors perform a theoretical stability analysis of pressure-driven viscoelastic channel flow with porous walls, likely using linear stability analysis and modal decomposition to isolate the wall-localized mode.
result: They uncover a new instability that is localized near the porous wall and arises from the coupling between viscoelastic stresses and the porous interface, differing from the elastoinertial center mode and classical porous-wall mode.
conclusion: This work provides a novel route to instability in viscoelastic flows via porous interfaces, expanding the understanding of wall-bounded viscoelastic stability.

title: Kinematic And Rheological Equivalence Of Steady Shearing And Planar Extensional Flows
authors: Nicholas King And Gareth H. Mckinley
abstract:
Author(s): Nicholas King and Gareth H. McKinley

Recovery of planar extensional viscosity from data obtained via steady shear measurements alone illustrates the equivalence between the two flows and offers a route to overcome experimental challenges associated with planar extensional flow measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 144003] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows a kinematic and rheological equivalence between steady shearing and planar extensional flows, allowing planar extensional viscosity to be recovered from steady shear measurements alone.
motivation: Planar extensional flow measurements are experimentally challenging, motivating a route to obtain extensional viscosity from simpler steady shear data.
method: The authors establish an equivalence between steady shearing and planar extensional flows through kinematic and rheological analysis.
result: The equivalence enables recovery of planar extensional viscosity from steady shear measurements without direct planar extensional experiments.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical way to overcome experimental challenges associated with planar extensional flow measurements.

title: Phyllotactic Order From Radial Growth Of Spatial Symmetry-breaking Instabilities In Supercritical Conditions
authors: Marcello A. Budroni, Giulio Facchini, Fabian Brau, And Anne de Wit
abstract:
Author(s): Marcello A. Budroni, Giulio Facchini, Fabian Brau, and Anne De Wit

Phyllotactic patterns, i.e., the arrangements of organs around a stem in some plants, represent not only fascinating geometries but also a source of inspiration for advanced biomimetic technological applications. Recently, spatial symmetry-breaking instabilities have been shown to feature, in some c…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044202] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: Phyllotactic patterns are shown to emerge from radial growth of spatial symmetry-breaking instabilities under supercritical conditions.
motivation: Phyllotaxis is a fascinating botanical geometry with biomimetic applications, and recent work suggests a link to spatial symmetry-breaking instabilities.
method: The authors analyze the radial growth of spatial symmetry-breaking instabilities in supercritical conditions to model phyllotactic order formation.
result: The study demonstrates that phyllotactic arrangements can arise naturally from the dynamics of such instabilities, providing a physical mechanism for their emergence.
conclusion: This offers a new perspective on phyllotaxis as a generic pattern-forming phenomenon and may inspire biomimetic technological applications.

title: Coevolution Of Strategies And Interactions In Donation Games On A Square Lattice
authors: Balázs Király And György Szabó
abstract:
Author(s): Balázs Király and György Szabó

The coevolution of strategies and interactions is investigated with players located on a square lattice with interactions between first and second neighbors. The pair interactions are described by two-strategy (cooperation or defection) donation games with variable cost and benefit parameters for ea…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044302] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the coevolution of strategies and interactions in donation games played on a square lattice with first- and second-neighbor interactions.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how cooperative behavior emerges and persists when both strategies and interaction patterns evolve in spatially structured populations.
method: They use two-strategy donation games with variable cost and benefit parameters on a square lattice, allowing strategies and interaction links to coevolve.
result: The analysis reveals how variable cost and benefit parameters shape the coevolutionary dynamics between cooperation and interaction structure.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the emergence of cooperation in evolutionary game theory on lattices, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Recurrence Time For Finite Quantum Systems
authors: Chaitanya Gupta And Anthony J. Short
abstract:
Author(s): Chaitanya Gupta and Anthony J. Short

We study the time it takes for all states of a finite quantum system to return simultaneously to their original configuration. In particular, we define the recurrence time for a quantum system to be the time at which all time-evolved states are close to their initial configuration, and at least one …

title: Weakly Nonlinear Dynamics Of Follower-force-induced Oscillations In Cosserat Rods
authors: Mohamed Warda
abstract:
Author(s): Mohamed Warda

We investigate the weakly nonlinear dynamics of the flutter instability of a planar Cosserat rod in a viscous fluid driven by a terminal follower force. Building on our previous linear stability analysis, we derive Stuart-Landau amplitude equations governing the emergence and saturation of oscillati…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044201] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies weakly nonlinear flutter oscillations of a planar Cosserat rod in a viscous fluid driven by a terminal follower force.
motivation: Building on prior linear stability analysis, the work aims to understand the emergence and saturation of follower-force-induced oscillations beyond the linear regime.
method: The authors derive Stuart-Landau amplitude equations to describe the weakly nonlinear dynamics of the flutter instability.
result: The amplitude equations govern the onset and saturation of oscillations, providing a reduced-order model for the nonlinear behavior.
conclusion: The study characterizes weakly nonlinear follower-force-induced oscillations in Cosserat rods, extending linear stability results to finite-amplitude regimes.
